entries.summary: Desktop owns global `system | light | dark` mode and remembered Floe light/dark presets. One validated snapshot drives Welcome, Env App, native chrome and generated documents. New/reset selections use Porcelain Light/Dark; valid choices survive upgrades. User changes paint pending feedback before asynchronous persistence, retain acknowledged state on failure and permit retry without losing mounted content, drafts or focus.

entries.title: Desktop runtime bridge
entries.description: Canonical navigation and security boundary for Desktop-integrated Runtime access and direct lifecycle.
entries.summary: Desktop opens independently runnable Runtime through machine-readable startup, scoped transport and session contracts. Its process-local coordinator owns direct Local, WSL, SSH and container lifecycle. Gateway/Provider remain access routes. Runtime service, health, process and session observations cannot become competing owners; plugins use their released brokers rather than Desktop control credentials.

entries.title: Desktop Environment library
entries.description: Browse one Runtime card through its original Runtime, Cloud and Gateway access tabs.
entries.summary: Welcome projects one Environment library from authoritative snapshot owners. Exactly linked Runtime/Cloud entries share a card; paired Gateways add access tabs rather than duplicate cards. Independent Runtime, URL and Cloud owners retain their cards. Grouping never merges registrations, grants permission, substitutes failed transports or changes operation ownership. Unlinking restores independent cards; Cloud failures retain known environments with stale-result context.

entries.title: Desktop interaction continuity
entries.description: Preserve open Welcome sessions through background observations and isolate authority and completion boundaries.
entries.summary: Desktop Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher and Runtime own business facts and execution progress. Background observations must preserve an open dialog or popup, its draft, selection, step, details, focus, native text selection and scroll. Only explicit opening, closing, switching, handoff or the current operation's completion changes visibility. Invalid authority preserves the visible session and input, blocks stale submission and offers verification or an accessible exit. Closing progress does not cancel its task.

entries.title: Environment card presentation
entries.description: Preserve compact Env card tabs, facts, action footers, focus and geometry across snapshots.
entries.summary: Environment cards preserve geometry across perspectives, snapshots, narrow layouts and long translations. Each perspective selects an explicit route without granting authority or falling back. Snapshots retain nodes, selection and focus; owner removal invalidates submission but retains open sessions.

entries.title: Desktop Welcome navigation
entries.description: Switch Welcome pages immediately, retain page state, and present explicitly selected Environment Center tabs.
entries.summary: Welcome owns immediate local page selection. Flower/Environments navigation never waits for Launcher IPC, snapshots or Runtime preparation; visited pages retain state. Runtime readiness still gates Flower requests without blocking return navigation. Explicit Environment Center tab changes may animate destination cards, while refresh and retained-page return preserve stable headers and never replay entrance motion.

entries.title: Desktop Environment connections
entries.description: Explain each Environment connection and apply one address namespace policy to Welcome and settings.
entries.summary: Welcome and settings share a pure connection model derived from host access, placement, Runtime public addresses and health. Presentation never selects transport. Addresses retain their host/container namespace; missing or failed observations remain unconfirmed rather than proving process exit. Private bridge credentials never become browser, clipboard or QR targets. Explicit Stop clears addresses even when a prior window remains open.

entries.title: Desktop runtime readiness
entries.description: Direct Runtime health, access readiness, and Open recovery boundaries.
entries.summary: Desktop admits a managed Environment only after its exact direct target reports compatible Runtime service and Local UI readiness. Gateway/Provider/URL access readiness is separate. Missing, stopped, outdated or damaged Runtime selects direct Start, Update or reinstall recovery. Startup status gaps remain bounded waits. Retained diagnoses preserve presentation only; current Presence and command-time validation own authority.

entries.title: Runtime platform facts and icons
entries.description: Identify the actual Runtime OS from trusted observations and display local platform marks without changing card continuity.
entries.summary: Runtime owns OS/distribution facts; Desktop consumes recognized trusted observations and displays bundled original-color marks with localized names. Last-known facts survive disconnect, failed probes and restart until replaced online. Unknown platforms show a device mark without blocking supported Runtime. Display retains card geometry, selection and focus; client/provider identity never substitutes for Runtime OS.

entries.title: Desktop transport recovery
entries.description: Bridge registry, recovery snapshots, generation fencing, and session disposal.
entries.summary: Each Desktop placement bridge owns one HTTP/2 session, an immutable-generation recovery snapshot, and one exact registry identity. Recovery replaces the stdio exec and HTTP/2 session once through that owner, validates process and Runtime identity, rejects stale callbacks, and disposes transport and model resources through one terminal settlement path. Health observers and individual streams cannot independently recreate the bridge lifecycle.

entries.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
entries.description: Direct SSH and SSH-container Runtime lifecycle execution owned by Desktop.
entries.summary: Desktop manages SSH-host and SSH-container Runtime only through the saved connection and placement. One process-local lifecycle coordinator, Launcher Operation, transport lease and temporary helper serve Start, Stop, Restart, Update, Refresh, Open recovery and Reinstall. Gateway/Provider credentials never substitute for SSH authority. The target stores no Desktop lifecycle lock or supervisor state.

entries.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
entries.description: Windows-only WSL 2 discovery, registration, Linux Runtime lifecycle, private Bridge, and packaging boundaries.
entries.summary: Windows 11 x64 runs Electron only: no native Local, Windows or local-container Runtime. Register initialized Linux x64 WSL2 distributions independently; manage only exact distribution/user Runtime. Windows owns WSL installation/lifecycle/removal. Missing/WSL1/uninitialized distributions, commands, damaged packages or lost Bridge fail visibly with explicit recovery.

entries.title: Desktop session and model source
entries.description: Session routing, Desktop model catalog, Flower attach, and lifecycle invalidation.
entries.summary: Desktop publishes each Environment session's explicit target route and identity. Accepted Runtime Stop, Restart and Update invalidate attached sessions. One model-source process handle per session starts without delaying Env App; that process owns reconnects while provider credentials remain local. Persisted Flower history stays readable when the live model source is unavailable.

entries.title: Desktop Environment registration ownership
entries.description: Single registration owners, versioned connection records, serialized persistence, and generation-safe removal.
entries.summary: Each Environment action names one registration owner: `local_environment` for built-in Local, `runtime_target` for WSL/SSH/containers, `saved_environment` for URLs, or the Gateway-held member identity. Linked cards never choose storage or mutation behavior. Desktop serializes changes against current preferences, immediately publishes committed snapshots and fences late probes/Open tasks so removed registrations cannot reappear.

entries.title: Desktop environment settings
entries.description: Open one target-bound settings session, preserve independent drafts, and save through the registered owner.
entries.summary: One settings window/session per Environment opens without waiting for access reads. Registration controls sections; explicit Environment IDs resolve registered management authority for every operation. Runtime owns access config. Failure preserves drafts/diagnosis; stale responses cannot alter newer opens. Cloud/URL/Gateway cannot read or save Local access settings.

entries.title: Desktop environment settings presentation
entries.description: Apply one theme-aware visual hierarchy, fixed window geometry and responsive controls across settings tasks.
entries.summary: Desktop composes published Floe Dialog, Tabs, controls and presence into one Environment settings surface. Theme tokens own material and contrast; product CSS owns grouping and geometry. Every page preserves readable labels, reachable actions and a fixed viewport. Loading, failure and disclosures retain the draft owner. [Settings sessions](desktop-environment-settings.md) own authority, persistence and recovery; styling adds no operation state.

entries.title: Desktop SSH environment settings
entries.description: Edit SSH registrations in a compact modal with explicit saving, visible custom configuration, and direct dismissal.
entries.summary:
SSH creation and editing share one form and the existing registration save API.
Common fields remain visible ahead of advanced settings; custom configuration
stays discoverable in a summary. Failed saves preserve input. Connection and
secret authority remain with [Environment registrations](desktop-environment-registrations.md).
The window, tab, draft lifetime and asynchronous recovery contract belongs to
[Environment settings](desktop-environment-settings.md).

entries.title: Desktop runtime process lifecycle
entries.description: One Desktop-owned direct Runtime lifecycle for Local, WSL, SSH, and container targets.
entries.summary: Desktop owns managed Runtime lifecycle through one process-local `RuntimeLifecycleCoordinator`. Local, WSL, SSH and container Start, Stop, Restart, Update, Refresh, Open recovery and Reinstall use the saved direct channel. The first accepted operation owns its target until terminal; conflicts return that identity without preemption or queuing. Gateway and Provider provide access only. Old process, database or renderer state cannot create another lifecycle owner or fallback.

entries.title: Desktop managed Environment reinstall
entries.description: Runtime-only direct-channel reinstall with minimal Desktop recovery journal.
entries.summary: Wipe reinstall is Desktop's recovery for a broken managed Runtime. After exact-target/root confirmation, Desktop verifies a Runtime package, attempts process stop, isolates/replaces the root, starts and verifies Runtime, then cleans old data. Old health, databases, journals or unknown process state cannot block the direct filesystem attempt. Preserve-data reinstall instead replaces managed files and rolls back when verification fails.

entries.title: Desktop application updates
entries.description: Signed macOS and Linux application updates with an explicitly unsupported internal Windows channel.
entries.summary: One Desktop update coordinator serves Welcome, menus, command palette, settings, status and compatibility recovery. Packaged macOS uses signed architecture-specific Sparkle appcasts; Linux uses matching DEB/RPM metadata through `electron-updater`. Development, unsupported and misplaced macOS builds fail closed with manual recovery. Internal Windows NSIS builds expose no production feed and report updates unsupported.

entries.title: Gateway Cloud access
entries.description: Separate restricted network routes from independent Runtime Cloud authorization and recovery.
entries.summary: Gateway Cloud v3 manages a Gateway machine and its local directory. RCPP v5 independently enrolls and recovers a Runtime over either direct HTTPS or the selected Gateway proxy. Gateway local v6 owns membership, invitations and restricted egress. Cloud owns environment identity, Namespace ownership and approval. Runtime owns one Cloud association, one selected route and one Flowersec connection controller.

entries.title: Gateway client access
entries.description: Derive management from verified host access and enroll URL clients without administrator grants.
entries.summary: Gateway exposes two fixed paths: verified host administration and environment-only URL access. Clients cannot choose roles or persist management authority. Runtime lifecycle and application authentication remain independent; Cloud operations still require Cloud authorization.

entries.title: Gateway service
entries.description: Manage Runtime-initiated membership without acquiring Runtime lifecycle authority.
entries.summary: redeven-gateway owns durable membership, one-time invitations, client grants, policy and restricted forwarding. Runtime verifies address/code, previews signed enrollment then explicitly joins. Gateway never scans/dials Runtime addresses or manages Runtime lifecycle. LAN needs no Cloud; Gateway loss affects its paths, not independent management authority.

entries.title: Gateway network settings
entries.description: Configure share endpoints, next-start listener bindings and request Host restrictions without changing member authority.
entries.summary: Gateway independently owns admin-confirmed share endpoints, listeners and optional Host restrictions, saved atomically by verified host admin. Listener edits require explicit restart; live sockets persist. Empty restrictions allow hostnames without weakening TLS/invitation/member/Desktop authorization. Invalid input or failed writes preserve saved/live state.

entries.title: Gateway Desktop interactions
entries.description: Gateway enrollment, connection ownership and consent.
entries.summary: Desktop enrolls managed Local, SSH, WSL and container targets. Runtime management, invitation verification and local consent are separate authority checks. Members appear only after joining; no Runtime URL form exists. Observations preserve steps and drafts; confirmed faults require explicit recovery.

entries.title: Gateway access sessions
entries.description: Open member applications over outbound Flowersec connections with isolated end-to-end TLS.
entries.summary: Desktop opens a joined Runtime over its existing outbound Flowersec connection to Gateway. Gateway forwards bytes to the Runtime's fixed application entry; it has no Runtime URL to dial. TLS terminates in Desktop and Runtime. Password, MFA, Host/Origin checks and application authorization remain Runtime-owned. Access artifacts limit initial redemption; no Gateway timer shortens established business sessions.

entries.title: Gateway deployment qualification
entries.description: Qualify outbound membership, isolated TLS applications and Cloud access under real network restrictions.
entries.summary: Qualification must prove Runtime-to-Gateway connection direction and real application behavior. Unit tests alone do not establish Electron certificate handling, browser MFA, MySQL migration or an isolated network path. Record each command's actual result; source changes or installer builds are not proof that an application flow passed. These affected-feature checks are separate from release packaging and the aggregate push gate.

entries.title: CodeSpace system-browser access
entries.description: Open a CodeSpace in an ordinary system browser through the selected Desktop environment route without exposing private bridge credentials.
entries.summary: Desktop resolves a trusted resource ID through the environment transport and opens an isolated short-lived loopback entry. Browser exchanges it for resource-bound HTTP/WS sessions; private bridge tokens never enter it. Runtime owns permissions, AccessGate and editor generation. Environment closure ends routes; failed open leaves no new authorized listener.

entries.title: Native Desktop CodeSpace access
entries.description: Bind a Desktop editor origin to one authorized CodeSpace through the current environment transport.
entries.summary: Desktop owns each CodeSpace window, browser profile, protected loopback listener and selected route. Runtime owns editor generation, permissions and AccessGate. Editors use native HTTP/WebSockets without privileged preload or transport injection. Closing a window, revoking access or stopping an instance ends its connections. Route failure and occupied saved ports fail visibly without transport substitution or request replay.

entries.title: Browser Editor runtime
entries.description: Code App serves Browser Editor codespaces through the local app server and managed code workspace engine APIs.
entries.summary: Browser Editor support is owned by the Code App app server. Codespaces are opened through Local UI `/cs/<id>/` routes or through remote `cs-*` sandbox hosts, while Desktop and Env App can prepare or update managed Browser Editor runtime versions through code workspace engine APIs.

entries.title: Flower MCP runtime
entries.description: Configure external MCP servers and execute their tools through Flower's existing Floret authorization boundary.
entries.summary: Redeven configures MCP and adapts the released official Go SDK, which owns stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions. Floret owns invocation, approval, one-shot effects, history/recovery. Add no second execution queue/lifecycle/retry authority. Unknown call outcomes are terminal and never replayed; invalid persisted config fails without changing bytes.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas
entries.description: Render progressively detailed service topology and exact object context.
entries.summary:
Tessiven presents one progressively detailed canvas for understanding where
business services run. Solid Runtime node cards sit inside tinted dashed visual
groups; external dependencies use a separate card treatment. Default connections
show root-level overview; hover and focus show only the current group or host's
relationships. Wheel zoom and drag pan belong to
the canvas, while object details and the read-only document remain normal selectable
text. Flower is the editing surface; the canvas has no manual content editor.

entries.title: Tessiven relationship summaries
entries.description: Bound group relationship geometry while preserving complete exact relationships and evidence.
entries.summary:
The shared Tessiven presentation projection owns group relationship summaries.
Collapsed groups show at most four call patterns, not every instance call.
Expanded group headers expose one pool-wide overview. Physical node cards keep
exact relationship rows. All original endpoints, relationship IDs and evidence
remain authoritative; summaries never edit documents or manufacture observations.
Full details remain available through search, node filters and bounded pagination.
Missing visible endpoints suppress previews rather than connecting substitute rows.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas navigation and rendering
entries.description: Browse compact service topology with shared layouts and bounded route painting.
entries.summary:
Published Floe owns layout, routing, viewport interaction and route painting.
Tessiven supplies canonical topology projection, localized view controls and
palette. Folding, filtering and navigation never rewrite a saved document.
Canonical relationships remain inspectable while only the current connection
scope is routed and painted. Offscreen geometry cannot expand the SVG layer. Invalid graph data or actual worker failures stay visible;
view changes retain the last valid scene until the next layout is ready.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower replies
entries.description: Read canonical Flower output in a quiet movable canvas window.
entries.summary:
Redeven presents canvas replies in a compact, themed floating reading window.
Flower owns the conversation, actions and live feedback; Floe owns window
geometry, pointer interaction and floating-layer projection. Hiding the window
keeps the composer and conversation alive. Errors, approvals and retry retain
their canonical Flower behavior rather than a canvas-specific recovery path.

entries.title: Runtime settings
entries.description: Navigate and edit runtime configuration through consistent, responsive settings surfaces while preserving API and permission ownership.
entries.summary: Env App owns runtime settings destinations, localized drafts and API adapters; published Floe owns reusable layout/navigation. Narrow layouts remain usable and revisited panels retain draft/scroll. Authenticated APIs own writes; readers cannot edit administrator fields. Failures preserve input, while maintenance uses its existing controller after explicit confirmation.

entries.title: Flower Skills and MCP
entries.description: Manage Flower instructions and external tools from one retained two-tab surface in both product carriers.
entries.summary: Shared Flower owns retained Skills/MCP management; both carriers supply typed authenticated adapters. The rail entry below New chat preserves draft/tab filters, with no duplicate runtime Skills destination. Readers inspect catalogs; administrators mutate configuration. Failures retain input and expose Retry, and every shipped locale supplies explicit copy.

entries.title: UI presentation transactions
entries.description: Heavy selection changes present visual intent first, commit content after paint, and defer layout effects until content presentation.
entries.summary: Heavy navigation acknowledges selection synchronously, commits target visibility after that intent can paint, then performs focus, resize, scroll or measurement after content paint. Published Floe separates visual from committed values; Redeven applies this ordering across Activity, Workbench, terminal, Flower, Files/Git and heavy panels without duplicating business state.

entries.title: Env App floating layer order
entries.description: One product-owned stacking contract orders movable windows, Flower, plugin surfaces, blocking modals, and command UI.
entries.summary: Env App assigns global layers to movable windows, Flower, plugin surfaces, blocking modals and command UI. Interaction reorders only its window band. Published Floe owns visible-viewport constraints and drag geometry; Redeven persists settled geometry and preserves reachable controls, local scrolling and destination interaction.

entries.title: Dialog content placement
entries.description: Keep dialog titles distinct from visible body guidance across Env App, Desktop, drawers, and window-local confirmations.
entries.summary:
Published Floe Webapp owns the shared Dialog structure. Redeven supplies localized
titles, body guidance, and actions. Headers contain identity and controls;
instructions and consequences belong in the body. This applies to ordinary
dialogs, confirmation dialogs, drawers, and window-local confirmations. A missing
or misplaced description is a content integration failure, never a reason to
restore a header subtitle or hide the text.

entries.title: Adaptive desktop layout
entries.description: Preserve desktop workflows in narrow windows while allocating temporary navigation drawers from local space.
entries.summary:
Redeven chooses interaction mode through released Floe layout configuration.
Native Desktop always uses desktop interaction. Browser mobile interaction
requires all three conditions: width below 768 CSS pixels, a coarse primary
pointer, and no primary hover capability. Narrow mouse windows retain Activity
and Workbench. Floe owns media-query observation, local space measurement, and
drawer placement/focus; Redeven owns navigation disclosure and content.
Automatic sidebar placement never changes saved navigation or collapse preferences.

entries.title: Mobile shell navigation
entries.description: Reach shell tools and plugins above persistent mobile navigation without reducing the working area.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns mobile navigation choices; released Floe Shell owns the layout,
visible viewport, presence, and focus boundary. In the browser mobile mode defined
by [adaptive desktop layout](adaptive-desktop-layout.md), the framework toolbar is hidden and its actions remain reachable from a fixed More button.
Navigation panels never cover or disable the bottom bar. Covered page content
stays inert through panel exit, and global confirmations retain full modality.
Closing navigation preserves page content and does not cancel product operations.

entries.title: File preview window actions
entries.description: Read files in Activity and Workbench with one set of product actions in the existing title bar.
entries.summary: Redeven owns file actions/drafts; published Floe supplies titlebar slots and window lifecycle. Desktop Activity and Workbench place compact actions beside the filename before window controls. Actions preserve permissions, text selection, download mapping and discard confirmation. Close fences pending work immediately while retaining visible content through retirement.

entries.title: File preview dismissal
entries.description: Retire a file preview without replacing its document during exit or delaying user actions.
entries.summary:
The file-preview controller owns document state and immediate cancellation;
published Floe owns window and mobile dialog presence. Accepted close must keep
the live document and title unchanged throughout exit, then release all retained
content when the panel unmounts. It must not create a blank iframe, a brighter gray
intermediate surface, extra reads, or an additional close delay. Owner disposal
always releases resources, and stale asynchronous work cannot revive a closed
preview.

entries.title: File preview viewport and rendering
entries.description: Preview fit, renderer ownership, and Markdown reading colors.
entries.summary: Redeven owns preview modes, identity, and renderer lifetimes; published Floe owns sizing, PDF layers, and static PPTX. Documents/images initially fit, including enlargement. Resize updates automatic fit, preserving manual zoom. PDF/PPTX pages have one rendering owner. Stale work cannot replace current content; cancellation is neutral and failures stay local/retryable. HTML uses published isolation; source editing is explicit and incomplete HTML never executes.

entries.title: Static PPTX file preview
entries.description: Read bounded presentations through the released Floe renderer without host tools or document uploads.
entries.summary:
Published Floe owns static PPTX parsing and rendering; Redeven owns the reading
surface and authorized file bytes. Supported presentations open locally with
windowed slides, selectable text, and stable zoom. External resources stay disabled;
obsolete documents cannot replace the active source. Rendering failures expose
local recovery or incomplete-content guidance. Original licenses and corresponding
MPL source remain available with redistribution.

entries.title: HTML file preview
entries.description: Open HTML files as isolated interactive pages while retaining explicit source editing.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns file classification, authorized reads, edit state, and preview
placement. Published Floe owns HTML document construction and isolation policy.
Opening an HTML file displays its page by default; source editing requires an
explicit action and write permission. The document cannot access the trusted
shell or authenticated resources. Oversized, truncated, or unreadable content
never executes and retains the existing localized preview error surface.

entries.title: Git workspace generation and Files decoration
entries.description: Keep Git views and Files decorations revision-consistent through capability gating, generation ownership, and monotonic invalidation.
entries.summary: Each Git projection belongs to one protocol client, repository and revision generation. Changes, Branches and Files have separate owners sharing monotonic invalidation. Files renders immediately and keeps committed decorations while a bounded replacement loads. Stale or invalidated responses cannot restore old state, including after unknown effects.

entries.title: Shared surface material
entries.description: Apply Floe's lightweight material to Redeven controls, product boundaries, and floating surfaces without duplicating decoration or input ownership.
entries.summary:
Published Floe Webapp owns shared material and control motion. Redeven selects
`soft-neumorphic` in Env App and Desktop Welcome, maps product boundaries to the
released surface roles, and keeps business content flat. Native input, local
portals, widget identity, and hot interaction ownership do not change. A visual
conflict is resolved by removing the product override at its source; there is
no copied shadow engine, local dependency overlay, or second theme owner.

entries.title: Product accessibility for AI agents
entries.description: Audit core product semantics while preserving visual presentation and existing input ownership.
entries.summary: Redeven owns names, descriptions, state and relationships while preserving geometry/styles/handlers/focus and hidden/inert exclusion. Published Floe owns reusable controls/focus/layers. Shared gaps require source/behavior evidence and released upstream fixes. Report audit scope accurately; accessibility changes alone certify neither full WCAG nor model performance.

entries.title: Input focus boundaries
entries.description: Identify one stable input boundary and consume the released Floe focus rule across product surfaces.
entries.summary:
Published floe-webapp owns input focus presentation. Redeven supplies product
layout, semantic state, and one declared boundary for custom compound inputs.
Focus changes only the existing border color; geometry and decorative shadows
stay stable. Conflicting host styles fail source or browser checks and must be
removed at their owner. No fallback stylesheet overrides the released contract.

entries.title: Git browser visual states
entries.description: Keep Git selection, repository facts, semantic status, hover, and focus visually independent across themes.
entries.summary: Git file selection and inline diff inspection share a contained surface with independently owned request state. Floe interaction accent marks selection; semantic Git colors mark repository facts. Checked-out and inspected branches remain distinguishable when they coincide. Layout preserves local scrolling, keyboard actions and a current diff across widths and themes.

entries.title: Git diff request lifecycle
entries.description: Preserve diff content across unrelated layout updates while keeping refresh, target changes, and transport recovery authoritative.
entries.summary: One shared Git panel owns preview/full-context reads by target, refresh revision, transport and mode. Stale responses cannot replace current content. Unchanged Workbench placement retains requests, content, expansion and scroll; target changes/refresh invalidate them. Missing transport waits for Shell recovery; empty/errors settle explicitly without automatic retries.

entries.title: Workbench interaction contracts
entries.description: Canonical navigation for Workbench input and surface-lifecycle ownership.
entries.summary: Workbench interaction is governed by explicit ownership contracts rather than widget-specific event heuristics. This overview is the canonical navigation point for input ownership and surface lifecycle. Focused concepts define wheel, pointer, text, terminal, selection, recovery, lazy loading, and shared overlay behavior without mixing those independent responsibilities into one retrieval unit.

entries.title: Workbench composition surfaces and editing
entries.description: Edit notes, text, and optional region names through published Floe surfaces while preserving layout content and materials.
entries.summary: Published Floe owns composition rendering, direct editing, materials and anchored tools; Redeven owns localization, defaults and layout persistence. Native caret, selection and IME remain intact, with optional empty region names. Save/reopen preserves content, color, geometry and material; failed upgrades retain the prior supported layout.

entries.title: Workbench input ownership
entries.description: Wheel, pointer, local-scroll, and text-selection ownership.
entries.summary: Workbench input ownership is declared through explicit marker contracts so canvas zoom, local scrolling, pointer actions, and text selection remain distinguishable. A selected widget boundary does not automatically own wheel input, and local-scroll regions must declare their role rather than relying on incidental DOM structure. These contracts let the canvas remain predictable while nested product surfaces preserve native interaction.

entries.title: Workbench terminal interaction
entries.description: Activity and Workbench consume one actor-owned semantic terminal state through view-local surfaces.
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns PTY, native VT, geometry, controller epoch, semantic history and atomic Presentation. Released terminal-web renders one canvas per view and collects local input. Authority/renderer violations fail closed; auxiliary history or search errors stay local and retryable without disconnecting live output.

entries.title: Terminal fonts across client devices
entries.description: Resolve bundled and locally available terminal fonts without changing another client's shared preferences or terminal grid.
entries.summary: The Env App owns terminal font selection and document-local loading. New preferences use bundled JetBrains Mono at the existing default size of 12; existing font IDs and sizes remain intact. Each client resolves its own available font, while Floeterm owns character cells, cursor positions, and the authoritative session grid. A missing saved font falls back visibly without rewriting that preference. Font loading failure keeps the terminal usable in system monospace and offers an explicit retry.

entries.title: Terminal session groups
entries.description: Persist one environment-wide terminal group catalog while Activity and Workbench render placement-specific trees.
entries.summary: Runtime catalog alone owns group identity/order/revision and each Session assignment. Activity/Workbench share a two-level tree with independent expansion/placement. Default always exists, immutable; every session has one known group_id, and group paths affect new startup only. Stale replies cannot regress; unknown groups refresh without reassignment. Delete closes/hides members first.

entries.title: Official installation progress
entries.description: Observe durable official installation without coupling it to a management page or saved placement.
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns the durable official-install Execution and its progress, idempotency, and recovery. Redeven observes that authority, presents exact market review and permission setup, and retains the operation when management closes. Response loss never creates a second installation. Only current authoritative inventory can expose a launch target; failed setup cannot revive stale permissions or remove saved canvas components.

entries.title: Plugin package review
entries.description: Review official updates and external packages against exact Host-verified source and permission evidence.
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns package inspection, validation, and atomic lifecycle mutation. Redeven presents the exact candidate, source evidence, permissions, and confirmation before submitting through released APIs. Cancellation affects only pre-submit inspection. Unknown mutation outcomes require inventory reconciliation instead of resubmission. Updates retain saved components and use fresh authorized slots after reconciliation; only confirmed uninstall removes their placement.

entries.title: Plugin layout continuity
entries.description: Preserve saved plugin components across runtime lifecycle changes, and open independently in the current display mode.
entries.summary: Redeven persists exact plugin widget/instance/surface identity and geometry; ReDevPlugin owns live authority. Upgrade, disable, permission/reconnect failures retain placement. Only explicit removal or confirmed exact-instance uninstall deletes it. Recovery reconciles unknown outcomes without focusing/rearranging the canvas or silently recreating authority.

entries.title: Workbench surface lifecycle
entries.description: Selection presentation, recovery ownership, lazy widgets, and shared floating surfaces.
entries.summary: Workbench preserves widget identity across selection, activation, loading and recovery. Floe owns generic Dock focus; Redeven adds no visibility store. Selected Terminal local viewports own wheel input without DOM focus; unselected widgets remain Canvas-owned. Shell recovery makes retained content inert above the canvas, with overlays in the shared surface layer.

entries.title: File icon presentation
entries.description: Consume the released Floe file icon catalog consistently across Files, Git, Flower, and Ask Flower.
entries.summary:
Published Floe Webapp owns file recognition rules, SVG artwork, and product
palettes. Redeven supplies filenames, directory and link metadata, and rendered
sizes. JSON, YAML, and TOML remain visually distinct; language, design, office,
and installer formats retain their reviewed identities. Unknown formats use the
upstream generic icon. An icon never grants preview, execution, or extraction
capabilities; those operations retain their existing permission and format checks.

entries.title: Files context menus
entries.description: Keep file operations reachable inside the complete Files workspace across Activity, floating windows, Workbench, and touch layouts.
entries.summary: Published Floe owns file-menu placement, measurement, scrolling, submenu gestures and dismissal. Redeven supplies workspace bounds, actions and localization. Menus remain eight CSS pixels inside Files/surface/visible-viewport intersection; invalid explicit bounds close them. Files never escapes its global layer or duplicates Workbench coordinate conversion.

entries.title: Plugin Center interaction
entries.description: Browse and manage plugins in an Activity page or an input-isolated Workbench bottom drawer with retained navigation and responsive details.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns Plugin Center navigation and presentation; released Floe Webapp owns
Dialog positioning, Portal placement, presence, and modal input. Workbench opens
one retained bottom drawer outside its inert canvas. Activity uses the same
directory in a page. Search, filters, selection, and scroll survive reopening.
Failed actions remain actionable; closing management never cancels an admitted
Host Execution. Released ReDevPlugin remains the authority for lifecycle actions,
permissions, exact inventory identity, and SDK surface lifetime.

entries.title: Plugin surfaces
entries.description: Env App manages official and external plugins through an accessible Launcher, searchable category discovery, exact inventory identities, explicit review, SDK-owned surfaces, Activity windows and pinned pages, and Workbench widgets.
entries.summary: Redeven owns plugin discovery, navigation and placement; released ReDevPlugin owns admission, surface authority, bridge sessions, confirmation and revocation. Activity and Workbench use independent SDK slots. Management preserves search/selection, exposes actionable failures and reconciles unknown outcomes against authoritative state.

entries.title: Flower thread Goals
entries.description: Manage one concise objective and reflect in the same execution context before natural completion.
entries.summary:
Published Floret owns the canonical Goal, model tool, reflection and completion.
Redeven authorizes mutations and presents the typed facts. One current Goal per
thread describes the desired result clearly and concisely without a text-length
recommendation, ceiling or truncation. Goal never depends on Todo. Stop, thread
navigation and recovery remain available; an unresolved request never claims a
successful mutation or completion.

entries.title: Flower command and composer flow
entries.description: Immediate delivery feedback, ordered transport recovery, canonical confirmation, and always-available navigation.
entries.summary: Each input intent has one request ID reused for retries; accepted receipts echo exact request/Thread IDs. New-thread HTTP nests it under create, existing-thread HTTP uses top-level client_request_id with URL-owned ThreadID. The short-lived outbox retains non-secret unconfirmed input/settings; composer, Stop, navigation and interactions remain usable during work.

entries.title: Flower Activity origin page references
entries.description: Freeze only the visible Activity page facts for a new companion conversation.
entries.summary: A new desktop companion captures one removable origin snapshot without reads/editor replacement; existing threads do not. Opening with no selection/New refreshes it, later navigation/editing does not. Submission/retry use exact visible text and existing draft/transport recovery. Terminal context captures current screen like Ask Flower; omit unloaded/unauthorized facts.

entries.title: Flower conversation references
entries.description: Add frozen conversation facts to the current draft and preview or navigate without losing user input.
entries.summary:
The existing composer draft owner stores unadmitted thread references; Floret owns
admitted snapshots. Reference this conversation appends only basic facts to the
current editor, preserves selection and input, and never sends automatically.
Thread identity includes its runtime. Authorized Open selects only after a valid
read. Failed or canceled reads retain the preview and draft; frozen transport
retries retain the original snapshot after source rename or deletion.

entries.title: Flower composer references
entries.description: Show Ask Flower context inside the input and admit exact ordered composer references to Floret.
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorized reference discovery and unadmitted connection-local drafts; Floret owns ordered references after admission. Composer chips show files/directories, frozen conversation references and page context. Stale discovery preserves the editor; captured submission failures retain outbox recovery without overwriting newer edits; labels never supply canonical identity or authorization.

entries.title: Flower input history
entries.description: Recall canonical user text into an empty Flower draft with terminal-style arrow keys while preserving ordinary editor ownership.
entries.summary: Floret/cache supplies canonical user text; published Floe owns transient history navigation and Redeven owns shared drafts/candidates. Unmodified ArrowUp in an exactly empty ordinary editor recalls text for editing, never submits. IME, selection, menus and structured answers retain keys. Scope or external-draft changes stop browsing without discarding text.

entries.title: Absolute filesystem directory selection
entries.description: Select authorized directories through one navigation core in Flower, Spaces, and other filesystem pickers.
entries.summary: Published Floe owns picker navigation, validity and request lifetime; Redeven supplies connection, authoritative path context, localization and form state. Paths are absolute and / means the target filesystem root. Home/Root shortcuts grant no access. Failed navigation preserves intent/form, disables confirmation and offers Retry; execution revalidates current policy.

entries.title: Floating Files window dismissal
entries.description: Close the floating Files window without a blank exit frame while preserving responsive cleanup and reopen behavior.
entries.summary: Files controller owns active request and immediate return focus. Floating host retains title/key/live browser through Floe exit presence, with no extra timer/copied content/second browser. Floe makes exit inert and disposes after motion, including reduced motion. New requests cancel exit through that same lifecycle.

entries.title: Personal directory favorites
entries.description: Persist and share authorized directory shortcuts across Runtime clients without changing navigation or conversation defaults.
entries.summary:
Runtime owns one directory-favorites store. Each authenticated namespace, endpoint
and user has an independent ordered path set and revision. Env App and Desktop
supply this metadata to published Floe controlled pickers and product menus; the
existing filesystem navigator remains the only path validation and selection owner.

entries.title: Flower working directory navigation
entries.description: Select a new Flower draft directory and browse its files from the header, with shared conversation menu navigation.
entries.summary: Flower owns draft/durable-thread directory intent; Env App owns destination navigation. Full-page controls select new draft directories or browse the current directory; the companion omits them. Menus freeze exact thread/directory targets. Activity opens Files/new Terminal; Workbench creates widgets without changing scale or injecting commands into existing shells.

entries.title: Flower mobile navigation
entries.description: Keep conversations, reading, and composition usable within the mobile visible area.
entries.summary: In shared mobile mode, Flower opens its list in a large bottom drawer over retained detail. Floe owns presence/focus/motion and scroll-preserving focus return. Keep draft/selection/DOM and stationary detail/header throughout animation. Covered detail is inert and cannot acknowledge reads until exit. Desktop uses the same adaptive-layout contract.

entries.title: Flower Activity companion
entries.description: Activity presents one Flower surface as a dedicated page or a continuous floating companion without changing canonical ownership.
entries.summary: Env App retains one Flower product tree across its Activity page, desktop companion and available Workbench widget. Published Floe owns the companion shell; Redeven owns placement, focus and read acknowledgement; Floret owns conversation lifecycle. Changing placement or canvas selection never creates another Flower surface or workspace stream.

entries.title: Ask Flower window boundaries
entries.description: Keep contextual Ask Flower controls below host headers without maximizing the launcher.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns the Ask Flower launcher's placement policy in Activity, Workbench,
and Desktop Welcome. Its titlebar and composer remain reachable below the visible
Shell header and native Desktop chrome. The launcher supports dragging and manual
resizing, but neither a maximize button nor titlebar double-click may maximize it.
When available space shrinks, the published Floe geometry constrains the existing
window without replacing the composer or discarding its draft.

entries.title: Flower companion composer and motion
entries.description: Preserve one native editor while placing tools below text and dissolving detail into the compact companion entry.
entries.summary: One native Flower textarea serves collapsed entry and expanded composer, retaining draft, selection, focus and IME. Redeven owns content; published Floe owns shell motion/geometry. Expanded text precedes a bottom toolbar, with controls in More and guidance above. Phase-driven close/reversal never remounts the editor or introduces lifecycle timers.

entries.title: Flower companion presence
entries.description: Project canonical Flower work into the compact companion without displacing drafts, stealing focus, or creating another lifecycle owner.
entries.summary: Collapsed Flower projects canonical summaries and current-run detail through the existing workspace stream. Work, pending decisions and drafts have explicit precedence; historical completion is never new feedback. Presence neither expands Flower nor acknowledges reads. [Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md) owns placement, focus and dismissal.

entries.title: Flower read state
entries.description: Keep unread indicators monotonic and acknowledge only rendered content through silent background recovery.
entries.summary: Redeven owns per-user read confirmation. Unread indicators compare current activity with server confirmation and actual local presentation. Old responses never restore a dot for an already read version; new unseen activity remains unread. Temporary synchronization failures recover silently in the background, without blocking any user operation.

entries.title: Flower incremental live state
entries.description: One workspace facts stream, two bounded reading interests, and one indexed ThreadCache.
entries.summary:
Floret owns canonical history, identity and versions. Redeven authorizes public
projection; one workspace stream delivers it to ThreadCache. Text growth changes
one item at its UTF-8 offset, never copying, scanning or encoding complete history.
Window loss refreshes that reading interest; transport loss uses the existing
connection owner. Both preserve execution, accepted prose and drafts.

entries.title: Flower file edit preparation
entries.description: Show candidate filenames while tool arguments stream without authorizing or executing edits.
entries.summary:
Flower shows candidate filenames while file-editing arguments are being prepared.
The existing Floret argument preview is display-only; actual tool results remain
the authority for completed changes. Progressive names keep long preparations
understandable while one stable activity row continues through approval and
execution.

entries.title: Flower timeline ordering
entries.description: Canonical typed views, separate submission feedback, and stable row identity.
entries.summary: Flower renders the ordered items in Floret's typed current view. Canonical stable IDs plus each item's exact TurnID and RunID determine user, assistant, tool, interaction, queue, and terminal rows. Ordinary captured input appears immediately as a pending user row; only the captured draft is consumed. Queued submissions appear in the queue dock. Canonical request-key confirmation retains the corresponding mounted row without duplicating the transcript; newer drafts remain editable. Summaries never write timeline detail.

entries.title: Flower terminal turn process disclosure
entries.description: Collapse terminal work while preserving valuable output, explicit choices and active reading.
entries.summary: Floret owns turn identity, outcome, timing and explicit final boundaries. Terminal ordinary turns default closed after success, failure, cancellation or interruption; the live-to-terminal transition applies that default once. Pending controls and unresolved effects remain visible. Explicit user choices and active inspection prevent automatic collapse. Dialogue/finals stay visible. Interleaved answered inputs retain visible checkpoints between independently folded sequences.

entries.title: Flower reasoning selection ownership
entries.description: Preserve explicit reasoning choices across cold loads, shared drafts, submission, and restart.
entries.summary: Existing threads display confirmed reasoning settings independently of runtime view versions; new drafts retain only explicit choices. Default is a configuration choice, never On or an inferred effort. Verified capabilities determine controls; unknown controls remain model-controlled. Failed saves preserve confirmed settings and active turns keep immutable execution configuration.

entries.title: Flower personal conversation preferences
entries.description: Remember explicit model, directory, and model-owned reasoning choices without importing thread settings into future defaults.
entries.summary: Explicit model, directory and model-owned reasoning choices are remembered per authenticated namespace, endpoint and user. Loading/switching threads never writes defaults. New roots prefer explicit launch/draft choices, then personal memory, then configuration; existing threads and immutable turns retain confirmed settings.

entries.title: Flower model and navigation presentation
entries.description: Model-source controls, notifications, thread selection, and staged content ownership.
entries.summary: Flower keeps environment and Desktop model sources explicit, preserves thread-owned model and reasoning defaults, and keeps unavailable selections distinct from first-time setup. Thread selection separates immediate visual intent from committed content and rejects stale loads. Transient operation failures use host notifications instead of transcript content, while canonical run and tool failures stay with their owning timeline renderers.

entries.title: Flower setup and settings
entries.description: First-time model setup, actionable starter tasks, and shared provider, permission, and computer settings.
entries.summary: Shared Flower setup/settings serve Desktop and Env App. Empty unconfigured profiles offer explicit setup; configured new conversations offer editable starter drafts without launching turns. A retained modal form preserves saves/errors and makes covered chat inert without acknowledging reads. Existing recovery, model identity and permission owners remain authoritative.

entries.title: Flower provider configuration
entries.description: Configure provider access before choosing models, with stable navigation and explicit authentication states.
entries.summary: Desktop, Flower and Env share one dialog. Hosts own persistence. Choose a brand, connect, then select models. Preserve navigation, focus and recovery actions after connection failures; reject stale responses. Kimi shares one brand while access methods retain separate credentials and models.

entries.title: Flower ChatGPT authentication
entries.description: Select, reauthorize, sign out and remove local ChatGPT accounts with stable interaction and explicit intent.
entries.summary:
The shared [Flower provider dialog](flower-provider-configuration.md) owns account
selection and authentication feedback. Signed-in accounts remain distinct from
previous connections, sign-out preserves a stable compact summary, and explicit
removal forgets only a signed-out local registration. The host retains verified
local admission and persistence ownership.

entries.title: Flower failure recovery
entries.description: One turn-level failure owner and bounded manual recovery without replaying uncertain effects.
entries.summary: Floret owns outcomes, retry checkpoints and automatic historical migrations. Flower keeps accepted content readable with one failure/recovery surface; drafts, queue editing, Stop and navigation remain available. Transport uncertainty never proves success or permits replay. Readiness timeouts offer status refresh; deterministic migration failures remain explicit administrative diagnostics.

entries.title: Flower composer attachments
entries.description: Connection-local attachment staging, long-text conversion, and canonical timeline presentation.
entries.summary: Flower owns connection-local attachment editing; host adapters authenticate staging, Redeven owns staged bytes/unadmitted commands and Floret owns admitted history. Select, paste, drop, retry, remove, preview and attachment-only send share one controller. Text above 50,000 Unicode code points converts only after successful staging, preserving IME and source text on failure.

entries.title: Flower file activity presentation
entries.description: Typed file mutation statistics, diff disclosure, and action ownership.
entries.summary: Canonical typed Floret Activity owns confirmed reads/mutations; output-progress owns provisional argument counts. Rows show user filename and added/deleted totals with matching unified diff. Protocol fields/private paths never become display metadata. Historical targets grant no read authority. Missing typed detail shows purpose/status without inventing a diff.

entries.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
entries.description: Compact tools and bounded thinking without hiding dialogue or taking over active reading.
entries.summary: Desktop/Env App group consecutive tools with adjacent thinking. Active groups open; the first following prose or canonical turn end folds eligible groups, never temporary gaps. Explicit inspection survives. Answered input splits settled work into independently closed groups. This is presentation over published Floret facts, with no canonical summary or migration.

entries.title: Flower activity disclosure interaction
entries.description: Keep native tool activation, disclosure state, viewport following, and floating controls consistent during live updates.
entries.summary:
Shared Flower UI uses canonical Floret facts and one transcript viewport owner.
Live updates cannot move pressed triggers or add hit targets before clicks finish.
Canceled gestures never activate tools; disposal releases transient ownership.
Desktop and Env App share this contract.

entries.title: Flower conversation sidebar
entries.description: Select conversations clearly and reorder endpoint-owned pins without interrupting live interactions.
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share one Flower sidebar with ThreadID-owned rows and endpoint-owned pin order. Selection, running work, unread attention and pending actions remain distinct. Live summaries preserve row/menu/focus identity. Resizing and pin feedback are ephemeral presentation over the canonical ThreadCache.

entries.title: Flower inline media
entries.description: Display assistant media through released Floe previews and authorized Runtime resources.
entries.summary: Assistant images, screenshots, video, audio and self-contained HTML render in shared Flower through released Floe media/HTML isolation. Redeven authorizes resource routing; canonical Floret messages remain the display source. Unavailable, forbidden, oversized or mismatched resources show local retryable errors without interrupting the conversation.

entries.title: Flower explicit long-thread qualification
entries.description: Protect complete conversation rendering and responsive interaction during sustained active-turn growth.
entries.summary:
Long conversations must preserve complete content and responsive interaction while
work continues. This is a required product property, not optional release tuning.
The long-thread suite runs explicitly for acceptance or targeted investigation.
It is not registered in unified commit, integration or CI gates, and is not a
prerequisite for each commit. Keep the independent suite and fixed budgets available
without adding its setup and sustained measurement cost to ordinary development.

entries.title: Flower streaming stability
entries.description: Incremental Markdown and local record updates preserve interactive identity.
entries.summary: Flower renders actor-native changes through the indexed ThreadCache and the published Floe incremental Markdown parser. Ordinary growth changes the affected text/DOM region only. Stable history, code colors, copy controls, focus, selection and disclosure choices remain intact. A semantic change must remain visible; malformed updates recover through the single [live-state boundary](flower-live-timeline.md), never by omitting output or substituting a second lifecycle.

entries.title: Flower live queue CPU qualification
entries.description: Recorded source-volume and bounded reading recovery qualification.
entries.summary:
Ordered queues avoid premature full-history snapshots. Global facts and bounded
root/child reading have separate owners. Local read failure preserves content
without reconnecting or replacing drafts; see the
[live-state contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md).

entries.title: Flower request-history CPU qualification
entries.description: Qualify published execution-owned request facts and stable frontend observers under historical streaming workloads.
entries.summary:
Published Floret v7.79.0 reads canonical request facts once per Engine execution
and advances bounded state only after successful writes. Retry/restart reload
facts; historical render-lineage validation remains intact. Redeven stops sidebar
preview work at the latest useful content and retains unchanged sequence groups,
members and observers during streaming. Three real-Service/Electron samples
reduce median backend CPU 80.3%, combined CPU 53.9% and allocations 87.0%, while
preserving complete output, responsive controls, selection and manual reading.

entries.title: Flower received output progress
entries.description: Request-scoped output estimates, model waiting time, and safe streamed edit statistics.
entries.summary:
Flower shows how long a dispatched model request has waited and how much output
has arrived. Edit rows show line counts while their arguments are generated,
then use the confirmed tool result. Published Floret v7.42.0 owns the generic
in-memory progress and preview lifecycle; Redeven interprets its own tool JSON
and presents the safe observations. No new journal records or schema changes
are required.

entries.title: Flower code highlighting
entries.description: Color stable Markdown code without disturbing streaming, selection, copy or layout.
entries.summary:
Flower owns Markdown parsing and committed segment lifetime. Published Floe
`enhanceCodeBlock` owns visible-code tokenization, scheduling and color application.
Completed language-labelled fences receive syntax colors in both Env App and
Desktop. Original code remains immediately readable and copyable. Highlighting
must not alter text, frame geometry, copy controls, focus or an active selection;
unavailable or excessive highlighting work leaves plain code visible.

entries.title: Flower message appearance
entries.description: Keep assistant reading and sent user messages readable in every shell theme without changing content or interaction.
entries.summary: Shared Flower uses published Floe colors for compact assistant/user reading and contrasting sent-message selection. Theme changes affect paint while preserving DOM, geometry and selection. Queued input stays quieter; forced colors use system roles. Media and resource cards retain canonical identity and never require an empty text bubble.

entries.title: Flower terminal activity presentation
entries.description: Terminal output, truthful result messages, safe input confirmation, and read-only controls.
entries.summary: Flower renders canonical Floret v7 Activity facts. Host-authored labels and descriptions explain the task; every terminal operation has safe expandable details, including writes and empty reads. Disclosure and output scrolling are local presentation state. They never create process lifecycle facts or expose stdin, private working paths, or effect internals. Actionable approval controls belong to the composer.

entries.title: Flower interactions and context state
entries.description: Typed pending interactions, automatic context compression, and unlocked composer behavior.
entries.summary: Approval and waiting-user prompts are projections of Floret typed pending interactions. The bottom action mode is one mutually exclusive surface with fixed priority `input_request` then `approval` then `chat`, while the ordinary thread rail always remains interactive; decision surfaces never make a shared ancestor inert or install a pointer-blocking overlay.

entries.title: Asynchronous layout stability
entries.description: Keep controls and retained content stationary through pending work, feedback, and media decoding.
entries.summary: Floe owns shared geometry; Redeven owns localized feedback. Request/copy/refresh/media completion cannot push adjacent content. Keep compact normal views without empty feedback rows; blocking errors stay visible, retained-content errors use existing-row disclosure. User navigation/disclosure/new records may change layout; async feedback cannot simulate them.

entries.title: Shared interface scale
entries.description: Apply one measured desktop reading and control scale across Flower, Env App, and Desktop without shrinking content viewers or touch targets.
entries.summary: Published Floe owns typography, dimensions, responsive targets and virtual rows; Redeven maps product roles to it. At 16px root/100% zoom, desktop body is 12px/20px, conversation titles 13px/20px, navigation 12px/18px and ordinary rows 28px including spacing. Touch/enlarged text grows naturally. No density setting, root shrink or transform changes scale.

entries.title: Flower approval surface
entries.description: Review bounded approval queues, inspect exact commands, and submit independent or atomic one-time decisions.
entries.summary: Shared Flower renders canonical Floret approvals as a compact keyed list bounded by chat space with reachable header/footer. Runtime owns identity, permission and settlement; UI owns disclosure/submission feedback. Pending unavailable approvals stay visible with disabled decisions and reasons. Failures preserve content and keep Stop/navigation usable.

entries.title: Flower citations
entries.description: Canonical assistant source ownership, safe links, and provider marker presentation.
entries.summary: Floret owns durable assistant sources with end-exclusive Unicode code-point ranges in exact message text. Flower renders provider markers as titled links and strips them on Copy. Only credential-free, whitespace/control-free HTTP(S) URLs are links; marker IDs cannot establish URLs. Missing historical facts remain explicit, while authored bibliographies stay ordinary content.

entries.title: Flower subagent detail window
entries.description: Stable parent-scoped child current views, live replacement, and queued-input controls.
entries.summary: The child detail window reads the complete canonical Floret `ThreadView`. HTTP and live updates share the selected parent-child identity, while Activity and queued-input controls remain attached to the same canonical child. The window preserves navigation and scroll state across updates without creating a second transcript or lifecycle owner.

entries.title: Flower subagent detail presentation
entries.description: Parent header membership, canonical thread routing, and child execution detail and canonical input controls.
entries.summary: Floret parent-scoped ThreadRuntime.List owns membership; complete child ThreadView alone owns details. Open a stable immediate live window without polling/layout-changing sync UI. Routes use thread_id and explicit task_name, never inferred aliases. Malformed identity/contracts or parent-child mismatch fail rather than accepting legacy substitutes.

entries.title: Flower parent event timeline
entries.description: Important child reports and automatic events in the parent conversation with canonical avatars and compact source navigation.
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical child reports/events and admission; UI owns pages/bodies/disclosure only. Reports appear in the selected parent with canonical child avatars, without receipt/admission/preservation notices. Reading wakes neither task. Every full read rechecks recipient authority and canonical fixed-range paging.

entries.title: Tessiven Runtime discovery and operations
entries.description: Discover scoped Runtime paths and delegate explicit connection, business access, and native process operations to their existing owners.
entries.summary: Runtime Tessiven service owns UI/Flower discovery and dispatch over existing registries/catalogs/executors. Discovery neither starts processes nor acquires business sessions. Path refs grant no permission. Lost authority, changed generations/identities or revocation stop dispatch. Lost mutation replies remain uncertain; inspect original operation/current state before deciding, never auto-replay.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower and operations
entries.description: Generate canvas versions and route service actions through their original owners.
entries.summary:
Flower maps authorized code, configuration, and connected Runtime facts into
Tessiven versions through the `redeven-tessiven` system skill. Flower owns canvas
content editing as a core workflow. Resource actions
remain owned by the existing Managed Services and Containers managers. A
transport failure after a mutation is dispatched is terminal with an unknown
outcome, so the user must inspect the original manager before trying again.

entries.title: Authorized platform model gateway
entries.description: Session-scoped platform catalogs, credential boundaries, stable request identity, and background execution.
entries.summary: Redeven AI uses the trusted control channel's platform lease and gateway origin to discover authorized models. The Runtime never receives a platform Provider API key. Floret continues to own thread execution, tools, canonical history, and recovery; the platform Edge owns authorization, binding, reservations, and final accounting.

entries.title: Model directory and selection
entries.description: Runtime metadata and explicit selection.
entries.summary: Runtime owns atomic metadata. Reads/send preflight use shipped/saved snapshots; refresh never blocks configured chat. Background refresh is disclosed, opt-in and excludes OpenRouter. OpenRouter/Ollama discover on addition; manual refresh remains available.

entries.title: Model web search
entries.description: Resolve provider and model search intent once for settings, admission, and provider transport.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns provider and model search preferences. One backend resolver supplies
settings projections and Turn preparation; the final tool surface drives prompts
and wire declarations. Floret v7.40.2 validates hosted events against the actual
frozen provider request. Undeclared hosted execution remains a provider failure
because its remote effects cannot be assumed absent.

entries.title: Local ChatGPT plan authentication
entries.description: Admit official ChatGPT sign-in only through verified local host access and preserve provider history, credentials and billing choice.
entries.summary: OpenAI uses one API-key or ChatGPT-account method; omission keeps API-key behavior. ChatGPT uses public sign-in/Responses contracts, never Codex secrets/private backend. Floret owns engine/history/provider state; Redeven owns verified local admission, protected accounts/config/UI. Billing never silently changes; callers cannot obtain credentials. Canonical lifecycle reports failures.

entries.title: ChatGPT account lifecycle
entries.description: Persist verified local sign-ins, reuse issued registrations and complete renewal, cancellation and logout independently of connection editing.
entries.summary: The protected account store owns verified registrations/sessions; reuse unless explicit new-account/workspace intent. Email is no identity key. OAuth persistence is independent of connection editing; identity-only grants cannot infer. Retry refreshes OAuth inputs; renewal/logout serialize tokens. Cancellation/failed storage block credential use. Durable logout tracks interrupted cleanup; remote revocation remains separate.

entries.title: Provider configuration validation
entries.description: Apply provider-specific optional fields and reject incomplete model configurations before saving.
entries.summary: Redeven owns configuration, credentials and Flower readiness across every settings entrypoint and provider-bundle save. Floret's public runtime contract is unchanged. Invalid saves preserve configuration and credentials; authentication/network failures remain execution errors.

entries.title: Provider API and catalog review
entries.description: Match the shipped model catalog to official APIs, regional endpoints, and released adapter capabilities.
entries.summary: Runtime, Web, Desktop and iOS share one authenticated catalog. Official contracts and pinned models.dev inventory require released adapters and qualified limits, replay, tools, images and reasoning. Refreshes preserve configured model selections and stored conversation identities.

entries.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention
entries.description: Authorized image reads produce immutable native model attachments with canonical retention and preview membership.
entries.summary:
image.read inspects authorized files/snapshots. Redeven owns bytes/authorization;
Floret owns history/membership. File references stay references; results use native
images, not browsers, temporary servers or Base64 result JSON. Original snapshots
remain available after model preparation.

entries.title: AI tool runtime
entries.description: Canonical navigation and ownership boundary for Redeven AI tools and Floret runtime integration.
entries.summary: Redeven exposes typed AI tools through product-owned registration, policy, presentation, and concrete execution adapters while Floret owns admitted conversation, turn, invocation, approval, and projection lifecycle. This overview is the canonical navigation point for the focused tool, terminal, model/context, thread, and subagent contracts. Detailed behavior belongs in those concepts rather than one cross-domain implementation inventory.

entries.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
entries.description: Keep canonical Floret storage opaque and preserve every supported product migration through deterministic imports.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns canonical Agent data and its physical and logical formats; Redeven owns product facts, read state and uploaded resources.
- Outcome: supported existing data upgrades automatically and remains usable for new conversations.
- Invariants: stable database kinds, contiguous transactional migrations, immutable historical decoders, public Floret APIs and one service generation.
- Failure boundary: unknown formats, future versions, drift or failed validation block Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

entries.title: Flower backup and recovery
entries.description: Restore preserved Flower collections without replaying old work or backing up every upgrade.
entries.summary: Readiness drains generations; storage owners snapshot/migrate their data and Floret ends old execution. Recover history/settings/read-state/uploads without stopping other surfaces. Freeze Flower writes during capture/replacement, verify complete collections and retain snapshots. Space, malformed data, migration or interruption blocks Flower while preserving recovery; no effect replay or binary rollback.

entries.title: Flower historical writer acceptance
entries.description: Verify every immutable distributed-writer fixture through actual product upgrade and continuation.
entries.summary:
- Authority: locked Redeven writers with released Floret dependencies produce fixture bytes; current tests only copy them.
- Outcome: supported historical data upgrades, remains inspectable and can continue a new conversation.
- Invariants: immutable originals, exact source/module identities, digest verification, product write paths and complete final-main acceptance.
- Failure boundary: fixture drift or a failed upgrade blocks integration; a successful database open alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Flower attachment resources
entries.description: Owner-scoped uploads, canonical membership, provider reads, quotas, and last-reference cleanup.
entries.summary: Redeven owns bytes/metadata, authenticated owner, quotas and retention; Floret owns turn membership. Upload once, send opaque attachment_id, display attachment://v1 locators and revalidate provider resources. Never expose paths or substitute product claims for canonical membership. Owner/media/quota/membership/metadata/digest/byte failures reject only the affected reference.

entries.title: AI tool permissions and dispatch
entries.description: Tool registration, scheduling, permission, readonly, and target-routing contracts.
entries.summary: Redeven owns product visibility, presentation, current permission policy, prompt, and approval UX; Floret owns invocation and product-neutral tool implementations. Saved thread permission applies at the next authorization boundary within the same task, including queued work, continuation, retry and restart. Each prepared invocation keeps its own snapshot through approval and execution. Missing or invalid authority fails closed. Ordinary calls in one model response enter authorization together and may execute concurrently; dependent work waits for a later response.

entries.title: Computer and browser use runtime
entries.description: Keep target execution, authorization and observation under one Runtime owner while composing semantic actions in bounded scripts.
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns targets, adapter resources, active control and script
processes. Published Floret owns Agent lifecycle, tool effects and canonical
results. Flower prefers authorized commands and integrations for data work,
semantic browser or desktop operations for interaction, and explicit images for
visual decisions. A missing target, permission or capability fails explicitly;
no adapter silently selects another tab, window or device.

entries.title: Computer semantic snapshots
entries.description: Normalize browser, AX and AT-SPI facts into bounded, revision-scoped semantic trees at the Runtime boundary.
entries.summary:
ComputerUseRuntime owns the model-visible semantic schema, version 2. Browser,
macOS AX and Linux AT-SPI collect native facts; Runtime validates and normalizes
one bounded tree. Relationships never point outside that tree. Unsupported
facts stay absent. Invalid protocol, protected fields or inconsistent graphs
produce a closed observation failure, discard content and preserve confirmed
input effects without replay. Existing target authority and privacy scans remain
mandatory; semantic metadata does not grant input or capture permission.

entries.title: Computer script execution and semantic observations
entries.description: Execute bounded JavaScript against one authorized target without exposing host capabilities or replaying partial effects.
entries.summary:
One `computer.exec` is one Floret tool invocation and one effect attempt.
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns its isolated QuickJS process and checks every host
operation. The guest receives only the controlled `ui`, `browser` and `log`
interfaces. Partial progress survives failure; uncertain effects never replay.
Loops, conditions and navigation within the same selected page may compose in one call.
A new target or permission boundary stops the batch with its confirmed prefix.
A permission requirement or private input ends it through Floret's existing
interaction boundary.

entries.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries
entries.description: Distinguish valid empty data, truncation, strict lookup failures and pre-dispatch rejection.
entries.summary:
Browser and native script reads return promised shapes or explicit errors.
Missing observations never become empty data, and invalid input never dispatches.
[Script execution](computer-use-scripts.md) owns the namespace and failure barrier.
Completed input stays recorded even when a later read fails.

entries.title: Optional built-in browser installation
entries.description: Confirm browser acquisition, persist the environment capability switch, and keep setup separate from canonical Flower questions.
