entries.summary: Runtime owns one optional Chromium install. Enabled by default, it downloads only after authenticated user confirmation, never discovery/settings/tools. Disable persists, cancels install, closes managed processes and blocks use/prompts while retaining bytes/site data. Floret owns waiting/continuation. Failed verification publishes no partial package; offer explicit retry/source choice.

entries.title: Built-in browser Linux system preparation
entries.description: Authorize exact versioned AppArmor preparation without weakening the browser sandbox.
entries.summary: Installation manager owns readiness; a short Runtime command performs the approved system transaction. Ubuntu namespace restrictions get explicit preparation, then version reuse. Preserve Chromium sandbox/global AppArmor; admit only catalog bytes at a fixed root-owned path, without API credentials. Dependencies, sandbox and unknown launch failures stay distinct; failed/cancelled publication preserves data.

entries.title: Browser and desktop settings
entries.description: Separate environment capability, Chrome pairing, conversation target selection, and grants in one shared settings surface.
entries.summary: Desktop/Env App share one Browser and desktop dialog. Runtime capability, thread selection/grants and extension consent are separate authorities. Open/refresh/close never selects, grants, runs, installs or launches. Failed reads stay unknown; lost selections remain unavailable until recovery/replacement. Floret alone owns conversation lifecycle.

entries.title: Guided personal browser connection
entries.description: Prepare, install and confirm a same-host browser connection without exposing native-host configuration.
entries.summary:
Desktop and Env App share one personal browser connection guide. ComputerUseRuntime owns
connections; Floret ask_user and Respond remain the conversation owners.
The guide is bounded UI observation, not a second execution lifecycle. Users confirm installation and the first connection in Chrome; that profile then restores the same environment connection after restarts. Routine tasks reuse the verified connection without manually selecting a target.

entries.title: Chrome connection diagnostics and recovery
entries.description: Identify Chrome prerequisites, preserve connection failures, and guide recovery on the actual environment host.
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns readiness/live handshakes; Desktop/Env App share host-specific guidance. Installed Chrome or accepted launch is not control readiness or task continuation. Resource, graphical-session, launch, status and continuation failures have distinct recovery. Only a compatible live profile enters Floret Respond; preserve guidance, never substitute browsers.

entries.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs
entries.description: Bind an explicit profile and tab to the Runtime while preserving login state and unrelated user browsing.
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns browser connections, authorization and target control.
Managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension bindings share the same
restricted page executor. A selected tab never implies authority over sibling
tabs or a different device. Disconnect, revocation, closed tabs and uncertain
effects stop subsequent work without automatically selecting a replacement.

entries.title: Semantic desktop operations and explicit control
entries.description: Use macOS window Accessibility and private Linux AT-SPI before image input while preserving user control.
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns desktop target execution. macOS targets an explicit
application window; Linux owns a private Xvfb and D-Bus session. Semantic actions
use native accessibility first. A foreground operation requires current task
authorization and respects explicit Stop and takeover. Platform permissions do not prove
that every application or action can run unobtrusively in the background.

entries.title: Computer target selection across threads
entries.description: Resolve logical targets without side effects and preserve each authorized thread selection across turns and restart.
entries.summary:
The Computer Use Runtime owns discovery and selection over Redeven product
settings. Users describe work; Flower finds the browser page or application
window. The current selection is a working position, not a requirement to bind
resources in settings. Candidates never grant access. Stale, disconnected or
occupied resources fail explicitly without changing the previous selection.

entries.title: Computer use safety pauses and user control
entries.description: Separate operation facts from independent Agent questions and require fresh observation before further input.
entries.summary:
Floret owns questions, answers, cancellation and continuation. Redeven owns
computer execution, authorization, private input and media. Operations return
facts or errors; Flower decides whether to call `ask_user` separately. A blocked
capture is never a successful screenshot. Answers reach the Agent unchanged and
do not grant permission, clear safety or replay an operation. Fresh safe
observation is required before further actions. No host waiting table, recovery
journal or second conversation lifecycle exists.

entries.title: Private browser observation and input
entries.description: Fence secret-surface observation, private frames, ordered input and recovery checks around a canonical interaction.
entries.summary: Runtime owns observer-bound private input/pixels; Floret owns takeover/continuation. Bind operations to current observer, revision, thread/run/target; never expose secrets or replay uncertain effects. Disconnect revokes input. Canonical answer starts a new Run with fresh observation; private input additionally waits for decoded matching observer/interaction/target pixels.

entries.title: Computer use media and visual requests
entries.description: Resolve authenticated keyframes and bounded live samples into decoded Flower pixels without persisting image bytes in model history.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns authorized screenshots; Floret owns history/preparation. Flower
shows frames inline/in Stage. Durable frames and ephemeral samples have separate
lifetimes; tool success does not prove delivery. Model encodings never replace original assets.

entries.title: Flower computer viewer presentation
entries.description: Present decoded computer frames with shared window geometry, accessible status and explicit recovery.
entries.summary:
Published Floe owns Stage window geometry and launcher interaction; Flower owns
canonical visual status and presentation scope. Users can view decoded pixels,
move or restore the Stage, and retain geometry across visibility changes. Opening
and closing affect viewing only, never target or execution authority. Missing,
interrupted or private frames retain explicit recovery and cannot borrow an
unrelated public image. Media authorization and sampling remain with the
[Computer use media contract](../ai/computer-use-media.md).

entries.title: Computer use product qualification
entries.description: Establish scope-specific evidence for decoded frames, real target input, control handback and isolated cleanup.
entries.summary:
Redeven qualifies Computer use through the actual product renderer, Runtime,
media decoder and target adapter. A passing scenario proves only its declared
target and provider scope. Fixture outcomes, decoded pixels and cleanup are
required evidence; successful HTTP responses or tool metadata alone are
insufficient. Failed input and uncertain effects must never be replayed to
manufacture a passing result.

entries.title: Computer use qualification evidence
entries.description: Read measured browser and desktop outcomes without conflating adapter, model and final integration scopes.
entries.summary:
The production qualification runners establish scope-specific outcomes under
[the acceptance contract](computer-use-qualification.md). The following results
include September and October 2026 runs. A passing worktree run does not replace the exact-main
pre-push gate, certify arbitrary applications, or turn earlier failed runs into
successes. Private text and pixels are excluded from retained diagnostics.

entries.title: Browser and native drag timing qualification
entries.description: Retain browser and macOS timing evidence and separate model deviations from tool contract failures.
entries.summary:
Browser drag timing is measured from actual input events, with all model and
assertion failures retained. [Script contracts](computer-use-scripts.md) define
behavior; [qualification](computer-use-qualification.md) defines the test lane.
Browser measurements certify only the tested browser paths and durations.

entries.title: Media contention and native read qualification
entries.description: Distinguish deterministic contract checks, real DeepSeek task outcomes and evidence-parser defects for media and tree reads.
entries.summary:
The October 28 qualification validates cancellable media-write admission and
native node/subtree completeness. Production uses published Floret v7.88.0;
its existing cancellable inventory and write-gate contract need no upstream
change. Browser, AX and AT-SPI share the same completeness semantics.

entries.title: Computer use paired model measurements
entries.description: Compare visual primitives and semantic scripts through the production Service and report incomplete or failed evidence explicitly.
entries.summary:
Computer use performance is qualified through the production Flower Service,
published Floret, model adapter and managed browser. Paired fixtures measure the
same task with visual primitives and with semantic scripts available. The report
must retain failures and reject missing, duplicate or unmeasured samples.
Headless performance evidence does not establish native desktop or Chrome focus
behavior; those remain separate [acceptance requirements](computer-use-qualification.md).

entries.title: Codex computer and browser use design evidence
entries.description: Separate official guidance and observed packaged behavior from Flower decisions and unresolved platform limits.
entries.summary:
Flower borrows observable design principles, not private implementation code.
Official documentation and read-only inspection of installed app 26.908.40834
and Chrome extension 1.26.901.11451 support command-first routing, persistent
script batches, AX-first interaction, compact observations and independent
visibility/control. They do not establish a universal guarantee that arbitrary
external browser pages can never activate another window. Flower's Runtime
remains the sole execution and authorization owner.

entries.title: AI tool approval and interaction runtime
entries.description: Floret v7 pending interactions, effect authorization, and Flower row-local outcomes.
entries.summary: Floret owns typed approval/input; Redeven authorizes and renders without a second lifecycle. Resolve commits canonical results before view publication. Since v7.26.0, unresolved interaction and active projection publish atomically; waiting clears run_progress, other active summaries retain it. Persistence failure stays unresolved; reject/cancel is row-local, not a global failure.

entries.title: AI terminal tool runtime
entries.description: Redeven PTY resources with Floret v7 canonical effect and Activity ownership.
entries.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. One adapter authorizes execution once and publishes current views. Product SQL stores no parallel terminal lifecycle or effect recovery.

entries.title: Model reasoning capabilities and transport
entries.description: Discover verified reasoning controls, preserve explicit intent, and map thinking output and history to provider protocols.
entries.summary:
Published Floret owns the portable reasoning selection contract, Ollama metadata
parser, and Ollama wire encoding. Redeven maps model metadata, product settings,
and provider requests to that contract. Only verified capabilities create
controls; Default, Off, On, named effort, and token budget retain distinct
meanings. Invalid selections fail before provider dispatch, while unknown
controls retain the model's default behavior. Active Turns keep immutable
settings through continuation and restart.

entries.title: Flower prompt and rule sources
entries.description: Keep shared Flower identity and output guidance separate from runtime facts, capabilities and native engine guidance.
entries.summary:
Flower's host-owned base system prompt contains its English introduction as
Redeven's general assistant, visual output guidance and local file-delivery rules.
Every run profile uses the same base prompt.
Runtime facts, tool definitions and native Floret guidance retain their own owners
and remain available independently of the product identity.

entries.title: AI model and context runtime
entries.description: Model-source ownership, provider mapping, token limits, context usage, and compaction contracts.
entries.summary: Redeven persists product model and reasoning preferences, provider credentials, and model-source selection, while Floret owns provider-visible context and opaque continuation state. Environment and Desktop model sources remain distinct, context and compaction presentation come from typed Floret observations, and input/output token limits preserve their separate meanings. Product configuration updates merge permission and model state without overwriting unrelated settings.

entries.title: Model provider surface and history
entries.description: Keep provider-visible model history, tool surface refresh, and render lineage under Floret ownership.
entries.summary: Floret owns the provider-visible history and render lineage for each Turn. Redeven supplies the current model surface, prompt, permission snapshot, and ephemeral overlays at the declared boundaries. Historical tool facts remain readable without reintroducing removed tools or rewriting canonical history; provider-surface changes create a new compatible lineage and never become a second continuation store.

entries.title: Model request recovery
entries.description: Recover frozen provider requests through one Engine budget and expose sanitized attempt progress without adding a product lifecycle.
entries.summary: Floret owns retry admission, physical-request deadlines and attempt identity. Redeven supplies protocol facts through one adapter and displays the authoritative current view. Frozen input, confirmed tool exchanges and user cancellation retain their existing authority across transport recovery.

entries.title: Model request measurement
entries.description: Map request-bound native measurement evidence while Floret owns compaction pressure and recovery.
entries.summary: Published Floret v7.70.0 owns one pressure calculation: a qualified native prefix plus an estimate of only the remaining frozen input, or the complete estimate when proof does not match. Redeven supplies protocol facts through optional public contracts.

entries.title: Model request reuse
entries.description: Execute Engine-owned prompt-cache and continuation decisions without creating another history or retry owner.
entries.summary: Floret owns effective reuse decisions and canonical state. Redeven executes them through one prepared request and one Responses consumer. In-memory connections can optimize transmission only after the next canonical state and complete input agree. Failures return to normal turn recovery; supplemental context cannot enable reuse.

entries.title: Flower context compaction and Goal continuation
entries.description: Explicit compaction intent, one upstream execution owner, and recoverable interaction.
entries.summary:
Published Floret v7.74.0 owns compaction admission, installation, Goal continuation,
Stop, Retry and restart. Redeven authorizes and transmits the frozen intent and
presents canonical state. Pure compaction ends after installation or noop; Goal
continuation prepares context and continues work through the existing Engine and
current Goal review in the same execution.

entries.title: Model context usage and compaction
entries.description: Canonical compaction evidence, context usage, and timeline presentation.
entries.summary: Published Floret owns context, compaction and usage; Redeven displays typed snapshots. [Compaction lifecycle](flower-context-compaction.md) owns intent through recovery; [qualification](../operations/flower-compaction-qualification.md) covers deterministic, historical-copy and real-provider checks.

entries.title: Flower context compaction qualification
entries.description: Isolated deterministic, historical-copy, and real-provider compaction acceptance.
entries.summary:
Compaction qualification uses isolated state and explicit test lanes. Production
threads are never continued by historical-copy inspection. The [execution contract](../ai/flower-context-compaction.md) owns intent and recovery; [usage presentation](../ai/model-context-usage-and-compaction.md) maps canonical observations.

entries.title: Flower Ollama context qualification
entries.description: Exercise the selected installed model through Flower and compare compaction, native token usage, live observations, and restart recovery.
entries.summary:
The opt-in Ollama qualification uses the production Flower service, its model
gateway, and the published Floret thread runtime. Native provider usage must
agree with canonical Flower context and cumulative totals; compaction must
preserve facts through a real model-generated checkpoint and restart. Tests own
their temporary state and loopback recording proxy. A provider or assertion
failure fails the run; it never substitutes a simulated response or changes the
user's model configuration.

entries.title: Flower context distribution qualification
entries.description: Historical token attribution evidence and current native-token plus visible-character qualification.
entries.summary:
Current presentation uses published Floret v7.60.3: native input tokens and
same-request visible Unicode characters are independent facts. Historical token
comparison and remainder results below are retained as evidence, not current
product behavior or proof of complete OpenAI attribution. The current contract
is [Presentation](../ai/flower-managed-model-context.md#presentation).

entries.title: Flower Ollama task qualification
entries.description: Run real selected-model tasks through production Flower commands and verify effects, interruption, recovery, and subagent handoffs.
entries.summary:
The opt-in task qualification calls the selected installed Ollama model through
the production Flower service and published Floret runtime. The model chooses
real tool calls; assertions inspect actual files, terminal processes, canonical
views, and the workspace stream. A failed scenario remains a failure, with no
simulated replacement or automatic rerun. Tests own isolated state and stop only
their own services and tools. Source configuration and credentials stay unchanged.

entries.title: DeepSeek Responses
entries.description: Flower consumes Floret stateless Responses transport with explicit web tool limits.
entries.summary:
Flower routes the DeepSeek provider to the published Floret v7.66.1 Responses gateway.
Floret owns `/responses` rendering, SSE parsing, reasoning, usage normalization,
function-call validation, and opaque provider history. Redeven only maps its
model DTOs and canonical dotted tool names to provider-safe aliases.

entries.title: Flower canonical thread queries
entries.description: Find readable conversations and browse their canonical content through a minimal tool contract.
entries.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

entries.title: Floret thread runtime integration
entries.description: Typed Floret v7 thread runtime ownership and Redeven product boundaries.
entries.summary: Floret v7 `ThreadService` is the sole owner of active and canonical thread lifecycle. Redeven owns endpoint authorization, attachment resource resolution, provider and tool effects, and browser-safe mapping. Every existing-thread mutation proves that the ThreadID belongs to the authenticated endpoint before entering Floret. Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, and the optional independent CompactContext return the current typed view without waiting for provider continuation. Canonical journal facts prevent duplicate user, assistant, tool, and interaction records; transient drafts and execution tokens remain in memory.

entries.title: Floret Redeven adapter and projection
entries.description: Map authorized Redeven requests and Floret typed views without creating a second thread lifecycle.
entries.summary: Redeven's adapter is a thin typed boundary over published Floret. It authorizes endpoint and thread ownership, resolves resources, sanitizes Activity, maps typed views, native updates and failures, and projects live summaries. Floret remains the only lifecycle, persistence, migration, cancellation, and provider-state owner; Redeven never waits on provider work or mirrors a receipt, authority barrier, transcript, or execution projection.

entries.title: Flower subagent parent events
entries.description: Canonical parent reports, passive lifecycle events, and bounded waiting.
entries.summary: SubAgent reports and lifecycle events remain canonical Floret facts, visible to the direct parent without creating another handoff store. They do not wake idle parents; bounded waiting and explicit reads expose reports when the parent continues. Tool approval and user input remain ordinary child interactions, while questions and blockers can be reported through `report_to_parent` without ending the delegated task.

entries.title: Flower subagent runtime
entries.description: Canonical child threads, direct task instructions, scoped reads, and complete handoffs.
entries.summary: Floret v7 owns each SubAgent as a normal canonical child Thread. Redeven exposes product tools and Flower mappings over the typed `ThreadRuntime` without a second child identity, result store, recovery projection, or child lifecycle table. Parent-scoped summaries are bounded status only; the canonical child current view is the only complete handoff authority.

entries.title: Flower thread fork coordination
entries.description: Redeven authorizes a source thread, selects a full-thread or answer-anchored Floret fork, and adopts settings for the canonical destination.
entries.summary: Floret owns journal/destination identity; Redeven authorizes endpoint/source and adopts destination settings. One stable request optionally titles that returned destination only. No product fork receipt/saga/canonical copy. Invalid request, foreign source, Floret failure or conflicting settings fails explicitly, without a recovery coordinator or compensating canonical deletion.

entries.title: Flower thread deletion coordination
entries.description: Synchronous, idempotent convergence across Floret canonical deletion and Redeven product cleanup.
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical thread deletion and Redeven owns product settings, read state, execution authority, and attachment claims. One authenticated DELETE request performs those two owner operations in that order and returns success only after both complete. The operation is synchronous, idempotent, and retryable; it does not claim cross-database atomicity or persist a second lifecycle receipt.

entries.title: Flower plugin generation
entries.description: Flower-generated plugins are Redeven product orchestration through Floret and released ReDevPlugin lifecycle APIs.
entries.summary:
Flower can help users create plugins, but the generated-plugin flow is not a
second plugin platform. Redeven owns the user intent capture, prompt
orchestration, review UX, approval presentation, and product timeline
projection. ReDevPlugin owns templates, validators, package builders, lifecycle
APIs, runtime contracts, sandbox surfaces, and platform policy. Floret owns the
tool dispatch and approval lifecycle that Flower must use.

entries.title: Flower context action admission
entries.description: Ask Flower context actions become Floret-owned message references and durable model-context snapshots at admission.
entries.summary: Redeven owns selected context before admission; Floret owns admitted messages/references/context. One mapper validates authorization/privacy then emits durable ordered MessageReference and UserInput.Context. No product copy persists afterward. Malformed/unknown/forged or failed projection rejects admission while preserving editable draft/references.

entries.title: Redeven environment operations
entries.description: redeven env and redeven targets exec are the product boundaries for Flower and automation environment lifecycle and target diagnostic requests.
entries.summary: Redeven environment lifecycle requests must go through the Redeven product surface, not through inferred container, SSH, systemd, launchctl, or process-manager commands. Flower learns this boundary through the standard `redeven-environment` system skill, not through a bespoke environment workflow embedded in the global prompt.

entries.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
entries.description: Redeven builds a deterministic embedded OKF bundle from source Markdown concepts.
entries.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

entries.title: OKF tool suite
entries.description: OKF tools expose read-only Redeven repository knowledge through index browsing, short search, and concept opening.
entries.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf.index`, `okf.search`, and `okf.open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

entries.title: Gateway v6 protocol
entries.description: Define signed pairing, member invitations, policy, reverse access and versioned Cloud association.
entries.summary: Gateway serves only redeven-gateway-v6, defined by spec/openapi/gateway-v6.yaml. Signed invitations carry admin-confirmed addresses; authenticated exchange returns the signed descriptor/all endpoints. Gateway owns paired Desktop permissions and Runtime-initiated membership. Mismatch/old config fails unchanged; old URL-profile/HTTP-forward routes are absent. Cloud v3 remains separate.

entries.title: RCPP v5 Cloud API
entries.description: Single Cloud input, authoritative Access Point assignment, native OAuth and access authorization.
entries.summary: RCPP v5 separates Cloud authorization from network route. CloudRuntimeBinding owns environment, Runtime identity, Namespace, user or Namespace principal and generation. One Runtime ConnectionController handles direct and Gateway enrollment, registration, heartbeat, reserve maintenance and recovery. Desktop never creates a second credential recovery owner.

entries.title: Self-contained installer distribution
entries.description: Pin a prebuilt installer, authenticate detached release evidence in process, and activate a complete Runtime suite atomically.
entries.summary:
Release packaging builds `redeven-installer_<os>_<arch>` for macOS and Linux,
AMD64 and ARM64, with CGO disabled. It renders `redeven-install.sh` from the
actual four binary digests and signs both the binaries and entry through
`SHA256SUMS`. No receiving-host Go, Cosign, Python, OpenSSL or package manager
is required. A standard shell, HTTPS downloader and SHA-256 utility remain
bootstrap prerequisites.

entries.title: CI and release gates
entries.description: Redeven binds published dependencies, generated assets, UI behavior, release payloads, tests, and OKF to the exact main tip being pushed.
entries.summary:
Redeven runs focused development checks, a fast staged pre-commit gate and one
bounded integration gate for the exact main tip being pushed. Published
dependencies, generated assets, localization, compatibility and OKF must agree.
[Long-thread correctness and responsiveness](../operations/flower-long-thread-gate.md) run as explicit acceptance, outside unified commit, integration and CI gates. Broad browser, Desktop, Docker and native qualification also run explicitly;
release packaging additionally requires same-commit historical conversation
evidence and authenticated target-specific artifacts. Windows remains an internal
certification target and cannot enter the formal release inventory.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin release artifact gate
entries.description: Verify the released ReDevPlugin publication, native runtime evidence, packaging inventory, and exact collector inputs.
entries.summary: Redeven admits only the coordinated ReDevPlugin release published through its exact manifest, registry readbacks, native runtime evidence, and closed installer inventory. Every artifact is bound to the release tag, source commit, target, digest, signature identity, and package receipt before publication; partial, mutable, Windows, or target-mismatched inputs fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin integration gate
entries.description: Qualify released ReDevPlugin Host, market, runtime, and UI integration on the exact main tip.
entries.summary: The plugin integration gate proves that the released ReDevPlugin Host and market contracts remain aligned with Redeven's authorization, placement, renderer, and Desktop lifecycle adapters. It uses the published package and isolated smoke profiles; copied platform paths, implicit grants, second bridges, and stale lifecycle projections fail closed.

entries.title: OKF release assets
entries.description: Release workflow publishes OKF verification assets alongside CLI and desktop artifacts.
entries.summary:
GitHub releases ship `okf_bundle.manifest.json` and `okf_bundle.sha256` together with CLI tarballs, desktop packages, and signed `SHA256SUMS`.

Release workflow publishes OKF verification assets alongside CLI and desktop artifacts.

The signed aggregate checksum remains the public integrity anchor for these standalone verification files.

entries.title: Automated service-template catalog updates
entries.description: Follow verified upstream catalog tags through isolated source updates and the exact-main integration gate.
entries.summary:
The template repository owns recommendation discovery and immutable catalog releases.
Redeven's daily and manually dispatched watcher owns adoption of the published Go
module into source `main`. A successful update pins verified checksums, regenerates
notices and knowledge artifacts, and passes the normal final integration gate.
Failures preserve the last published main tip; a failed or uncertain push requires
remote-ref inspection before another attempt.

entries.title: Flower managed runtime facts
entries.description: One snapshot collector supplies canonical facts through published Floret admission and request boundaries.
entries.summary:
Flower consumes published Floret v7.47.1. One complete collector supplies four
stable partitions: execution environment, date/timezone, repository rule
sources, and available skills. Floret owns chronological admission,
semantic changes, user-role model-context messages, compaction and recovery.
The product owns collection and authorized presentation only.

concepts.summary: Redeven exposes typed AI tools through product-owned registration, policy, presentation, and concrete execution adapters while Floret owns admitted conversation, turn, invocation, approval, and projection lifecycle. This overview is the canonical navigation point for the focused tool, terminal, model/context, thread, and subagent contracts. Detailed behavior belongs in those concepts rather than one cross-domain implementation inventory.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
This concept is the stable overview for the subject.

Floret renders reference display content and snapshots into canonical model history for execution and compaction, preserving order across follow-ups.

Lease release follows the canonical terminal view, not the HTTP response or Desktop connection lifetime, so an existing session cannot admit hidden work after the final lifecycle snapshot.

sections.body: Redeven must consume published Floret releases and must not persist a second copy of Floret-owned conversation, tool, approval, todo, context, projection, or provider state. Tool and execution provenance must come from explicit contracts and results rather than inference.

concepts.summary: The protected account store owns verified registrations/sessions; reuse unless explicit new-account/workspace intent. Email is no identity key. OAuth persistence is independent of connection editing; identity-only grants cannot infer. Retry refreshes OAuth inputs; renewal/logout serialize tokens. Cancellation/failed storage block credential use. Durable logout tracks interrupted cleanup; remote revocation remains separate.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Sign-in and registration
One `chatgpt.Client` owns bounded, five-minute in-memory attempts.

Interrupted logout is completed at startup; normal maintenance scans never clear a live logout.

## Renewal and credential coordination
[Account maintenance](../../internal/chatgpt/lifecycle.go) starts with the Runtime service, independently of AI readiness, connection bindings and open windows. Runtime shutdown cancels maintenance without signing out and never schedules OS background work.

Account updates use model_directory.changed and merge independently of drafts.

## Logout and connection changes
Sign-out first records intent and stops related tasks through Floret's existing immediate Cancel with descendants. The private Desktop model source observes current account facts once per second and passes confirmed account stop reasons to its owning Runtime; it never owns another task lifecycle.

The Runtime Service protocol, secrets schema, Floret public API and domain migration remain unchanged.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: This concept owns local registration and credential lifecycle. Connection configuration stores only account bindings; it cannot commit or roll back OAuth tokens. Cancellation cleanup may retain a verified signed-out registration, and remote revocation failure never becomes confirmed success.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local host admission
The authenticated Runtime settings response publishes `auth_capabilities` with an `openai_chatgpt` availability, disabled reason and connection binding. Desktop identity, loopback URL text, renderer headers and client declarations cannot establish local access.

That source executes against the local account store; the remote settings page exposes no account login, credential transfer or account email.

## Account lifecycle
The [ChatGPT account lifecycle](chatgpt-account-lifecycle.md) is the canonical owner of registration, verified sign-in persistence, issued-client retry, local saved-account selection, renewal, cancellation cleanup and logout. Connection saves and explicit logout have separate results.

## Model and request contracts
The public account model endpoint's listed models preserve server order and are intersected with reviewed adapter capabilities. ChatGPT connections reject custom endpoints, API credentials and custom model declarations.

No error silently switches authentication or API billing.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Measure drag duration between delivered press and release events. Keep
deterministic adapter assertions separate from real-provider task outcomes,
and retain original failures when correcting test expectations.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Native macOS event construction/delivery was reviewed but not changed or timed
in that browser qualification. The subsequent native qualification below owns
evidence for the separate native repair.


## Native drag contract qualification — 2026-10-28

The Floegence-owned floe-native-apps implementation now schedules native
input against one monotonic origin after acknowledged mouse-down. Redeven uses
that public sequence through its existing authorization, event-receipt and held
input cleanup path. No application-specific detection or recovery was added.

A separate AppKit receiver reproduced the old implementation releasing a 500 ms
drag in about 17 ms. The repaired upstream receiver measured system event spans
of 1.11/2.76/501.79/5001.71 ms for requests of 0/1/500/5000 ms. Cancellation of a
5000 ms drag released after 113.91 ms without reaching the endpoint. The
production Redeven helper passed all five corresponding direct scenarios;
500/5000 ms requests measured 503.42/5005.30 ms. These are local event-delivery
measurements, not a guarantee that every application accepts a business action.

The configured real DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017) provider ran five native scenarios
three times: timed drag, invalid-duration rejection followed by a timed drag,
zero-duration drag, accessibility tree inspection and exact text entry. Eleven
original assertions passed. Three failures expected a browser-only diagnostic
field on a valid native rejection; one log parser stopped at a brace in a text
label before the complete JSON evidence. These are test defects, retained in
separate raw reports. One tree task also contained four model JavaScript field
errors before successful observation and a single confirmed input; those errors
remain model failures, not tool defects. Corrected validation/tree assertions
passed six additional real-model tasks. Intentional invalid durations were
rejected before input in every corresponding task.

Upstream Swift scheduling tests cover boundaries, slow receipts, cancellation,
unknown-effect failure and ordinary input. Downstream native protocol tests
reject fractional, non-finite and out-of-range durations before integer
conversion. The default three-tool surface and system prompt remain unchanged;
native help states the duration range, straight-path meaning and timing limits.


Nine additional real-model browser tasks (three repetitions of timed drag,
invalid-duration rejection and multi-page script batching) passed. An initial
command used an unanchored scenario selector, unintentionally admitted three
native cases without their required opt-in, and failed before those model runs;
its nine browser reports are retained separately. The precisely selected rerun
passed all nine assertions. Some successful tasks still contained model syntax,
argument or non-actionable-target errors before recovery; passing the final
fixture contract does not mean every model call was valid.

The final published v0.25.1 dependency passed all five direct native scenarios
and the affected Go consumers, vet, 38 Swift tests and the normal commit gate.
Its macOS implementation is byte-identical to the earlier qualified candidate.
Five final model tasks passed four assertions: one valid drag was refused with
TAKEOVER_REQUIRED before input. Three validation repeats passed two assertions;
the other receiver recorded an extra intermediate release from an unidentified
source. Neither failure is reclassified as a model mistake or silently passed.
The disposable receiver now records event source PID and marker without filtering
events or weakening assertions. Three subsequent validation tasks all passed,
with one marked source per run and 1002.99–1003.62 ms system-event durations.
That new evidence cannot retrospectively identify the earlier event source;
the original failed reports remain retained. No production takeover rule changed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Media retention](image-read-and-retention.md) keeps the write gate until a
cancelled maintenance scan has settled. A partial inventory cannot authorize
deletion. [Semantic reads](computer-use-semantics.md) disclose omitted children;
read failures cannot become empty leaves. The shared core guide clarifies one
node versus a subtree or loaded collection. The three default tool definitions
and base system prompt are unchanged. No application-specific recovery, automatic
input replay or alternative parameter signatures were added.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Configuration and credential-file hashes remain unchanged. Production source
hashes match between the 36-case run and supplemental run; only the test parser
changes. No real user thread is continued. Reports retain raw failures outside
Git. The configured wire alias is verified, not the remote model weights.
These observations do not establish universal model success or certify arbitrary
applications. Linux uses deterministic native fixtures, not a real-model run.
The user explicitly excludes Redeven push and its push gate; local feature
qualification does not claim remote CI or exact-main push certification.

concepts.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries
concepts.description: Distinguish valid empty data, truncation, strict lookup failures and pre-dispatch rejection.

frontmatter.description: Distinguish valid empty data, truncation, strict lookup failures and pre-dispatch rejection.
frontmatter.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries

concepts.summary:
Browser and native script reads return promised shapes or explicit errors.
Missing observations never become empty data, and invalid input never dispatches.
[Script execution](computer-use-scripts.md) owns the namespace and failure barrier.
Completed input stays recorded even when a later read fails.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Successful reads and argument counts
All guest methods, including image and download-cursor methods, validate explicit
minimum/maximum argument counts before dispatch. Existing type and option
validation remains authoritative; extra arguments return SCRIPT_ARGUMENT_ERROR
with a closed method and documented_arity diagnostic. Valid signatures do not change.

Runtime requires the promised result for semantic observations, node/text/collection/
attribute reads and condition waits. Missing or invalidated reads fail through the
existing observation-error boundary, seal the invocation and retain completed
input without replay. Empty arrays, empty text, zero counts and null attributes
remain valid data. Snapshot projection never fills absent observations with an
empty tree. A confirmed action may invalidate an old observation and still be
followed by an explicit fresh read. A documented wait timeout remains a result;
requireState turns it into CONDITION_TIMEOUT. Takeovers and target changes keep
their existing control boundaries.

The browser controller routes node/text/query/table/attribute/condition reads
through one observation boundary, including direct lower-level read exceptions.
It supplies the required semantic_read failure stage, retains the live source,
and uses the existing bounded read retry only; inputs never enter that retry.
A rejected read cannot become a malformed transport response that disconnects
the target. A later explicitly requested read can recover on the same page.

## Validated inputs and bounded browser reads
The browser adapter validates the complete operation before virtual focus,
scroll preparation or input. Invalid arguments retain a closed diagnostic with
phase, field, expected form and recovery; page errors and supplied secrets are
never copied into it. Keys use characters or documented names with
Alt/Control/Meta/Shift modifiers; physical codes such as Equal are not names.
Primitive computer.wait defaults to zero milliseconds and adds no settling
promise. Legacy waitFor retains its returned state. requireState throws CONDITION_TIMEOUT and seals later host operations, even if guest code catches the error. Earlier completed input remains recorded.
Its closed diagnostic retains method, requested state, timeout_ms and zero-based
operation_index, mirrored in failed_action/failed_operation_index. Matching text
and raw exceptions stay private. completed_actions records completed operations;
a completed wait operation does not imply its requested condition was met.

Browser locators expose query({limit,cursor}) over the authorized loaded AX
scope and an attribute allowlist. Results carry total, truncation, document and
cursor; changed contents invalidate pagination. Only returned page references
enter the bounded reference table. Each page is at most 200 items and 48 KiB of
items. Virtualized, unloaded rows are never counted as visited. href removes
credentials, query and fragment and must not be reconstructed as an action URL.
Browser rows reads a unique table/grid and returns header/data rows and cell roles,
with explicit loaded-tree scope. Pages contain at most 200 rows/48 KiB of item
content; each row is limited to 200 cells/44 KiB, each cell to 2,000 Unicode
characters. cells_truncated/text_truncated mark loss; exact totals cannot be
inferred from incomplete rows. Cursor identity includes full cell contents.
Nested tables are excluded. count reports loaded matches. attribute returns a
scalar safe attribute; linkSummary labels its redacted URL as non-actionable.
Native targets reject these browser reads inside scripts before adapter dispatch.

scroll_progress belongs to the scroll return value. It reports immediate
before/after measurements, with null or unchanged values remaining inconclusive.
Semantic wheel input uses the visible intersection of the target, not clickable-control
enabled state or its offscreen full-box center. Browser-native intersection geometry
owns ancestor clipping and transforms; document targets use their viewport. Existing
hit testing checks target ancestry and embedding-frame overlays before one wheel.
Scroll-into-view preparation remains separately reported when the wheel is rejected;
it can move the viewport. No alternative-point search or automatic input replay is
added. Immediate offsets do not select the next action for the model.

The core help demonstrates awaited node reads and logging the returned scroll
result; node and snapshot objects do not carry scroll measurements.

Repeated identical observations in the same script namespace/document/scope
receive a bounded advisory after two repeats. This never replays input, changes
target, adds a planner, or persists a second lifecycle.

Single-node detail does not enumerate a subtree. child_refs describes only
returned relationships; check children_truncated, use snapshot for a subtree
and browser rows/query/count for loaded collections.

sections.body:
Collection results describe only the authorized loaded tree; they do not certify
unloaded content. Native targets reject browser-only reads before dispatch.
Validation and observation recovery never replay completed input.

concepts.description: Bind an explicit profile and tab to the Runtime while preserving login state and unrelated user browsing.

frontmatter.description: Bind an explicit profile and tab to the Runtime while preserving login state and unrelated user browsing.
frontmatter.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs

concepts.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns browser connections, authorization and target control.
Managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension bindings share the same
restricted page executor. A selected tab never implies authority over sibling
tabs or a different device. Disconnect, revocation, closed tabs and uncertain
effects stop subsequent work without automatically selecting a replacement.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Connecting an explicitly chosen tab or creating a new tab in Browser and desktop also selects that target for the current conversation. Approval Required uses the current target and URL through tool approval; temporary URL authorization never becomes a saved origin grant.

It is not a model tool or a second browser-opening path.

## Managed profiles
Both Flower carriers use the shared browser installation controller at `/_redeven_proxy/api/browser/installation`.

The default profile creates its first page lazily; later loss of a selected page fails explicitly.

Semantic clicks check visible/enabled state, stable bounds and the actual input-session hit target before input, including parent-frame overlays. Preparatory scrolling is not a completed click; a blocked click reports `action_executed:false` and requires fresh observation when preparation changed the viewport. Condition waits inspect rendered state and use bounded sampling for CSS changes. Browser result labels use the current safe observation title when available; they do not treat a discovery label as current account identity.

Screenshot geometry changes within the same document receive up to one second
of read-only settling inside the invocation budget. Each attempt checks geometry
before and after capture; persistent movement returns capture/viewport_unstable
without pixels. Cancellation, document changes and the latched privacy guard
remain authoritative. Input is never repeated to repair an observation.

The existing frame observation inventory owns reference document identity. Child
navigation or removal revokes that frame and its descendants; unchanged parent
refs remain valid. Root replacement, cancellation and handback still invalidate
all refs. Snapshot/image revisions remain page-wide, and ref resolution verifies
the owning document again after its DOM/AX read.

Locator key presses require a focusable DOM element. AX document roots are not elements; use `ui.key('PageDown')` for page-level keys. Document validation and exact confirmed DOM.focus rejections return ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE with focus/not_focusable diagnostics, without dispatching a key or retiring the connection. Generic command failures, lost focus/input acknowledgements and failed key release remain uncertain; no action is replayed. Returned uncertainty retains a safe stage/reason, requests fresh observation, and keeps both the warning and completed-prefix facts in model-visible output.

Download association uses `browser.downloadCursor()` before the triggering input, followed sequentially by `browser.waitForDownload({after:cursor})`; an exact known `id` is also accepted. A cursor is bounded in-memory state owned by the page. Old files never satisfy it and multiple new files fail as ambiguous. No automatic input replay, latest-file inference or durable download ledger exists.

Captured downloads use the published SourceDownload identity as their sole writer;
raw CDP notifications do not create duplicate semantic records. Distinct same-named
exports remain distinct. AMBIGUOUS_DOWNLOAD carries bounded exact candidates.

browser.readDownload(id,{offset,limit}) reads captured bytes by exact source ID,
with bounded base64 output and explicit continuation. Sequential reads reuse one
short-lived source stream; cancellation, idle expiry and disposal retire it.
browser.saveDownload(id) copies up to 256 MiB into the current task scratch area;
the run owns the destination, authorization and partial-file cleanup. Offset, byte
count, identity and available total size are validated on every chunk. The guest
cannot choose a destination or read arbitrary paths. Terminal/file tools process
the returned path and deliver final artifacts to the user destination.

Hit tests translate viewport CSS points into the owning CDP session document
coordinates, including scrolled frames. Cross-process frame input checks every
embedding document for overlays. An unavailable protocol hit test returns
`TARGET_OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE` with `observation_stage:hit_test`, without
claiming the element is covered. Screenshot capture uses the native viewport
including non-overlay scrollbars and derives the immutable image transform from
captured dimensions. Geometry must remain stable before/after capture. Scoped
scroll uses the control center and verifies its hit target before dispatch.

## Chrome extension and explicit CDP
The MV3 extension uses Native Messaging and `chrome.debugger` bound to an exact tab.

Its webNavigation creation events retain bounded, in-memory popup source facts; Chrome tab-group opener metadata is not treated as the source of an action.

A remote Linux task uses its remote managed browser or private desktop; it cannot silently drive local user Chrome.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Internal source cancellation drains the active operation before clearing its
ephemeral cancellation flag. It never sets user_control, changes private mode,
or clears permission/Stop barriers. Drained cancelled reads return observation
failure and permit later authorized same-target reads; uncertain mutations stay
terminal without replay. Routine invalidated screenshots with no bytes or
attachments retain observation_invalidated and needs_observation. Inconsistent
target, safety or frame payloads still fail.

Private control recovery after Runtime restart uses the same initial managed profile preparation as ordinary tools. The private input helper cannot create a second owner of the default profile; passive sampling never launches resources.

See the [Codex design evidence](computer-use-design-evidence.md) for the public and installed-code comparison; no forced reload or CSP rewriting is used.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## User contract
The shared Browser and desktop dialog opens Browser settings for this environment.

Users never choose a file   or follow an archive download link.

No agent installation tool, automatic re-enable, shell fallback or target substitution is introduced.

## Distribution and state
Standard Runtime release suites carry `computer.zip`: official Node, published Playwright, QuickJS, the published FloeBrowser SDK and its native media collector, and product helpers, with a closed SHA-256 file inventory.

The Runtime never accepts a client-supplied URL, executable path or checksum.

No installation automatically restarts following a Runtime restart.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Readiness
The existing installation snapshot reports package state separately from `launch` state, structured reason and applicable action. A bounded native `--version` probe recognizes missing shared libraries without opening a page; unknown failures retain their own category.

Neither `--no-sandbox`, global AppArmor changes nor exemptions for replaceable user-owned executables are permitted.

## Explicit preparation
The shared installation controller starts `prepare_system` only after user action. The normal enabled switch, operation ID, progress subscription, cancellation and one-shot open continuation remain authoritative.

Runtime independently checks the installed version and policy before accepting the ready phase.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The operation retains personal browser processes, browser profiles, login state, bookmarks and saved tab recovery records. System preparation changes only the verified built-in browser version and its narrowly matched policy.

frontmatter.title: Semantic desktop operations and explicit control

concepts.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns desktop target execution. macOS targets an explicit
application window; Linux owns a private Xvfb and D-Bus session. Semantic actions
use native accessibility first. A foreground operation requires current task
authorization and respects explicit Stop and takeover. Platform permissions do not prove
that every application or action can run unobtrusively in the background.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## macOS windows
The Swift helper inventories regular and accessory application windows, reads AX roles, labels, non-sensitive values, supported actions and bounds, and exposes bounded subtree queries.

Application discovery reuses HostApplicationCatalog; exact candidate selection
uses NSWorkspace with current app/foreground permission. Launch completion is
synchronized, cancellation stops further actions, and window readiness is bounded.
Minimized windows are restored once and allowed to settle; zero/multiple windows
return explicit selection facts. No path-supplied shell launcher or independent
application lifecycle is exposed to guest scripts.

Secret fields enter the existing private takeover channel rather than model observations.

Snapshots declare source macos_accessibility and application_provided coverage.
truncated:false means the available tree was not cut, not that all visible content

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Missing, changed or unauthorized bytes fail explicitly. No unrestricted URL fallback.
- [Image reads](image-read-and-retention.md) share immutable Computer storage;
  computer:// identities and retention stay intact.
- Safe results include target, location, summary and safety. Semantic/script
  operations include images only when requested.
- Floret prepares Computer PNGs >=256 KiB as smaller JPEG90 (Go 4:2:0).
  Transparency, dimensions, originals, hashes and visible history stay intact.
- Model notices report dimensions/bytes/encoding; image pixels differ from CSS coordinates.
- Ordinary/summary/Retry/Fork share preparation before estimation/freezing.
  Retries reuse bytes; encoding revisions invalidate provider state. Ordinary
  image.read originals bypass compression.
- Flower caps JSON/base64 at 32 MiB independently of tokens: product policy,
  not a provider limit. Remote DTOs share the cap; services own final rendering.
- Floret compacts complete tool pairs and retains causes. UI provides numeric
  diagnostics and input/model guidance without unchanged Retry or secret payloads.

## Browser image coordinates
A model screenshot returns frame_geometry: its existing computer:// resource,
document identity, actual PNG dimensions, CSS visual viewport and image-to-input
scale/offset. Browser image input explicitly supplies coordinate_space:
"image_pixels", frame and document_id. Default coordinates remain browser CSS
viewport pixels or the native adapter's existing units. Native image mode is
rejected before dispatch; full-page/cropped arbitrary images have no input mapping.

The current controller holds one bounded model anchor. Viewer sampling cannot
replace it. Changed target, document, scroll, viewport or scale rejects the image
operation before input. This checks known changes, not arbitrary dynamic layout
races; semantic locators remain preferable for moving controls. Existing model
JPEG preparation preserves dimensions. Script geometry is invalidated after an
action and suppressed after takeover or failed observation. The final attachment
supplies after_frame when several screenshots were taken.

## Browser observation and private input
The shared browser controller enforces visible password fields, structured
one-time-code input semantics, secret-change latches and explicit permissions in
each frame, including shadow roots. Native adapters enforce platform secure-field
roles. They do not classify ordinary labels or page prose as CAPTCHA, OTP or
instruction attacks. Observed content is untrusted data, never authorization.
The model decides task meaning and whether human help is needed; it never receives
confirmed protected values or pixels for classification. Unmarked secrets are not
guaranteed detectable by accessibility; native apps must expose secure fields and
users retain explicit takeover control. An unreadable frame stops the observation
without inventing a human requirement. Unknown read failures are not retried;
only measured viewport instability has a bounded same-target resampling window.

See [guided connection](computer-use-browser-connection.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Result encoding recovery
Run the explicit local browser qualification from the repository root:

It builds the production FlowerSurface with installed published UI packages, uses the production runtime adapter and canonical detail projection against a real task-owned Service, and injects one counted executor effect followed by an invalid optional result. It is opt-in and stays outside ordinary CI and exact-main gates.

## Semantic execution acceptance
Browser and desktop belong to one delivery scope.

Cancellation and revocation before the click prevent dispatch; unknown click acknowledgements remain terminal.

Foreground macOS and credentialed model qualification remain explicit runs; the integration gate cannot substitute for their evidence.

## Real DeepSeek reliability acceptance
`TestComputerReliabilityDeepSeek` is an explicit paid lane through the production Service, Floret, configured DeepSeek provider and catalog-installed Chromium. It resolves the local `deepseek-flash` model (catalog display: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017)) and rejects substitution. Required environment: `REDEVEN_COMPUTER_RELIABILITY_E2E=1`, absolute `REDEVEN_COMPUTER_CONFIG_ROOT`, `REDEVEN_COMPUTER_EVIDENCE_DIR` and `REDEVEN_BROWSER_TEST_INSTALLATION`. Run `go test ./internal/ai -run '^TestComputerReliabilityDeepSeek$' -count=1 -v -timeout=22m` with `GOWORK=off`.

Set REDEVEN_COMPUTER_ACCEPTANCE_REPETITIONS=1..5 (default 1). Native scenarios run serially in the harness and also require REDEVEN_COMPUTER_NATIVE_E2E=1 and the release Swift helper; serialize native cases on the shared desktop. Browser-only cases may use -parallel 3. Scenarios include bounded text, limit repair, budget/prefix retention, key validation before focus, paginated reads, frame-bound image input, default delay, current title, stale frame rejection, invalid guest options, scroll return facts, conditional waits, natural input/read tasks, strict timeout termination, below-fold semantic input, exact asynchronous content waits, canonical navigation landmarks failure namespace reset, multi-page script batches, browser-to-task-file processing and installed native application entry. Reset diagnostics and completed waits are checked against canonical tool results. observation_capture verifies four PageDown inputs followed by one fresh screenshot; frame_refs verifies a retained parent ref after child navigation; option_field verifies exact unsupported-option diagnostics. strict_wait also checks the failed wait index and sanitized condition facts.

Natural visual_natural, form_natural and table_natural cases vary canvas position,
form labels and table size across repetitions. The visual case requires a returned
screenshot before a later pointer input and verifies actual canvas events; it is
not a prescribed coordinate replay. Native focus-change qualification uses an
AppKit app that changes its own key window during a drag, requiring a factual pause,
balanced release and explicit recovery without replay. REDEVEN_COMPUTER_NATIVE_TEST_HOST
can select an absolute baseline helper for that isolated regression.
The native_drag_focus_change model scenario exercises the same interruption
through the production Service and requires a retained partial input receipt,
one balanced press/release and no completed drag or automatic replay.

Semantic scroll qualification covers documents, oversized regions, clipped containers
and covered targets. Independent wheel events require one dispatched wheel or zero
when rejected; scroll events can also come from reported scroll-into-view preparation.
Real extension tests inject DOM/AX protocol failures before reads and clicks, retain
method/code, verify zero input and recover the same reference on an explicit read.
Managed tests cover malformed responses, transformed clipping, shadow DOM, same-process
and cross-process frames; geometry tests repeat document scroll under real zoom/DPR.

Natural tasks use the production default tool surface. Only the legacy default-wait
case explicitly retains its primitive. Read canonical tool results through
ThreadToolResultReader, decoding Floret's error-status ERROR prefix before the
host JSON envelope. Diagnostic assertions require data.script_error; echoed
scripts, logs and final prose cannot satisfy them. Retain plain pre-dispatch
runtime rejections separately; never infer script diagnostics from their text.
Count fixture events separately. A completed wait in the confirmed prefix remains
completed even if later guest JavaScript fails; whole-script success is not a wait
receipt. Reports retain safety and input-progress facts for failure classification.

Diagnostic scenarios specify the required operations, while table and download
tasks exercise autonomous planning. Verify returned tool payloads and counted
fixture events; submitted scripts and the model's final claims do not establish
execution. Stale-image rejection requires an actual returned `STALE_REFERENCE`
and zero pointer events. Image input requires one counted pointer event. Read
download bytes from the isolated fixture's owned directory without issuing an
anonymous runtime call after the model has acquired target control.

The batch case checks three fixture page visits, at least three completed reads,
at least two navigations or clicks in one script, and a returned screenshot.
Returned logged totals and final-answer totals are separate report fields; neither
can substitute for execution facts. Mixed processing requires one export, a
completed save_download and the terminal-produced project file. Native entry
requires discovery, confirmed launch/selection, exact text, one counted click and
a screenshot. Full source provider and secret files are hash-checked unchanged.

TestComputerScriptExamplesQualification executes the exact maintained download
help and batch example through production QuickJS, Runtime and installed Chromium,
checking byte equality for a multi-chunk file and the actual page values.
TestComputerNativeApplicationEntryQualification separately exercises single, no,
multiple and minimized windows with the real native helper.

TestComputerNativeDragQualification drives the published Swift helper against a
disposable AppKit app, checking 0/1/500/5000 ms and cancellation during a 5000 ms
drag. Each case requires exactly one press/release pair; cancellation must release
before the endpoint. AppKit receive times and system event timestamps are retained.
The native_drag, native_drag_validation and native_drag_zero model scenarios
exercise discovery, screenshot-based inspection, one timed drag, invalid-duration
rejection and zero-delay input through the production Service/tool registry.
Configuration and credentials stay unchanged; model mistakes remain in evidence.

The timed_drag and drag_validation scenarios verify fixture-generated mouse
events independently of model text: one press/release, endpoints, intermediate
movement and actual held duration. The invalid request must retain the Runtime's
INVALID_COMPUTER_ARGUMENTS duration_ms/integer_0_5000 diagnostic without input.
optional_probe verifies conditional continuation after zero matches and a normal
wait timeout; caught_lookup verifies that catching a failed unique lookup cannot
resume input within that invocation. computerDrag.node-test.mjs qualifies the
shared browser implementation through managed and connected hosts, image-bound
input, duration endpoints and interruption/unknown-effect cleanup.

Retain failed batches and classify model instruction failures, test defects and
product defects separately. Scenario completion is not a zero-tool-error claim,
and repeated qualification does not establish a general success probability.
Freeze implementation hashes before qualification and rerun affected checks
after integration changes.

Scenarios also verify a 2,800+ node page and complete table totals, task-tab isolation and account restrictions, current-download identity/content despite an older same-named file, and one counted save followed by a diagnostic failure with no replay. Reports retain provider wire IDs, tool error counts, canonical histories, final answers and fixture outcomes. Configuration hashes must stay unchanged. The native-entry case qualifies only its disposable AppKit app. This scope does not certify production accounts, arbitrary native applications or a universal model success rate.

## Existing product fixtures

The built Desktop computer lane selects configured exact deepseek-flash in its
isolated provider copy without requiring or changing the current user model.
Missing configured identity or an alternate wire override fails qualification.
TestComputerNativeScriptQualification separately exercises QuickJS, Go and Swift
scroll/screenshot against a disposable native fixture, checking counted effects
and focus/pointer restoration. External desktop input invalidates that evidence.
Desktop qualification observes the preload workspace stream; Linux Webtop uses CDP's passive HTTP workspace stream copy. A missing native or browser live-frame match fails that scope.

The report names the native macOS, connected Chrome and other scopes it does not qualify.

## Private preview and handback
`checkDesktopSystemBrowser.mjs` runs a deterministic provider against the real built Desktop, Runtime, Chrome extension and Native Messaging. Both carriers must show canonical connection assistance with no target bound, then continue after a verified extension connection.

Test threads and fixture servers are removed on exit; the owner of the isolated Desktop launch must stop its exact process tree and verify port release.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Execution
`computer.observe` reads bounded semantic information, with an optional image.
Inside `computer.exec`, `await ui.observe({emit:false})` returns a local object with
`observation.nodes`; script reads receive the full observation. The `full:true`
option controls the emitted snapshot instead of the default diff.

See the [adapter result contract](floret-redeven-adapter-and-projection.md).

## Platform adapters
The [browser contract](computer-use-browser.md) covers managed profiles, explicit CDP tabs and same-device Chrome extension bindings.

Stage viewing uses its independent bounded sampler; those samples never enter model history. See [Computer media](computer-use-media.md).

## Task access
Each computer invocation receives the permission snapshot established at its tool authorization boundary. Opaque origins never become origin grants.

Target selection chooses where work runs; it is not another confirmation of an already authorized action.

## Packaging and compatibility
Browser execution JSONL and Native Messaging use protocol 6 for Runtime-owned pause control, explicit page selection, reveal, popup progress and confirmed progress on observation failure.

Native window capture continues to respect Desktop-window exclusion and never substitutes an unrestricted display capture after failure.
