concepts.summary:
One `computer.exec` is one Floret tool invocation and one effect attempt.
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns its isolated QuickJS process and checks every host
operation. The guest receives only the controlled `ui`, `browser` and `log`
interfaces. Partial progress survives failure; uncertain effects never replay.
Loops, conditions and navigation within the same selected page may compose in one call.
A new target or permission boundary stops the batch with its confirmed prefix.
A permission requirement or private input ends it through Floret's existing
interaction boundary.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Rendered text reads require an explicitly selected HTML element. Document, text
and SVG nodes return TARGET_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE before reading; no parent/body
substitution or scope expansion occurs. Unknown observation failures stop the
operation; explicit fresh reads remain possible without input replay.

Floret owns batch exclusion through tools.Definition.BatchExclusiveGroup. Redeven
declares one computer-control group for selected-target calls. Conflicting
prepared calls are rejected before authorization; independent tools and inventory
can run alongside one computer call. Target gates still protect cross-batch use.

## Guest API and limits
`computer.exec` requires a target, code and a user-readable description.

Each call allows 30 seconds and 50 operations. ui.budget() and returned budget
metadata expose remaining time and operations. Explicit logs stream before later
operations under a 64 KiB UTF-8 budget, retaining safe findings on timeout or
uncertain effects. Private pauses, failed safety reads and navigation failures
discard content. Batch known steps across pages within the runtime budget; return
screenshots for model judgment when the next action depends on pixels. Argument
diagnostics identify the method when known, field, expected form and fixed repair
examples; raw errors remain private.
Observation diagnostics retain a validated CDP method and signed integer protocol
code when the connected-browser source supplies them. They reuse the existing
diagnostic field and invocation trace; raw exceptions never become model content.
Missing codes remain unknown, and no diagnostic authorizes retry or input replay.

Only snapshot/observe and locator.snapshot accept emit. Collection reads return
data for explicit logging; screenshots and help always emit.

Known unsupported option names are returned exactly; arbitrary keys and values
are never echoed. locator.snapshot still accepts only limit and emit.

Native ui.scroll uses the window center; ui.scrollAt(x,y,delta_y,delta_x=0)
targets a region without clicking first. Selector scroll remains semantic.
Browser drag accepts integer duration_ms from 0 through 5000. The shared managed
and connected-browser implementation holds the button while following a straight
path over the requested duration; zero adds no delay. A monotonic schedule avoids
accumulating one extra delay per transport call. Dispatch overhead can extend the
duration. Cancellation, takeover and document invalidation stop remaining moves;
cleanup releases at the last confirmed pointer position. A lost input reply keeps
its unknown-effect classification and is never replayed. Native delivery uses the published FloeNativeDesktop NativeInputSequence, with
one monotonic schedule after acknowledged mouse-down. It accepts the same
integer 0..5000 ms contract. The host checks authorization/target/cancellation,
retains exact per-event receipts, and releases only its outstanding input on
interruption. No application-specific timing heuristic or automatic retry is
added. Native qualification measures separate-process AppKit events; browser
tests do not certify native timing.
Browser locator.text() reads rendered innerText from one unique observed element
through a fixed isolated-world function, bounded to 12,000 Unicode characters
with explicit truncation and rendered_element scope. Hidden and unloaded content
is excluded. No arbitrary DOM execution is exposed.

Approval Required uses the current target and URL in the existing tool approval; temporary authorization expires with the target lease and never becomes a persistent origin grant.

The Runtime admits at most eight active script namespaces. The short tool definition teaches the entry point; selection returns the core guide and ui.help(topic) discloses read, visual, downloads or legacy signatures. Both selection and runtime help share one authored source. Exact signatures include: string names (no RegExp selectors), numeric scroll deltas, condition waits, and sequential awaited operations. Unsupported guest arguments fail before dispatch. Closed diagnostic codes distinguish reference/type/syntax/argument errors, operation concurrency and bounded output; raw interpreter exceptions remain private. A failed invocation retires its namespace while confirmed earlier actions survive.

Semantic snapshots retain their 256 KiB output budget. The script response allows a bounded 512 KiB envelope so metadata cannot make a valid snapshot fail at the transport boundary. Logs have a separate 64 KiB total budget. Local `emit:false` reads receive the same URL/title identity as emitted observations.

`context_reset` explicitly reports namespace retirement after failure. Safe diagnostics include phase and submitted-source line/column/symbol when available; raw exception text and stacks stay private. Failed namespaces cannot retain dormant Promise callbacks. Any failed host operation seals further operations, even when caught by guest JavaScript. Unique node/action lookups fail on missing or ambiguous matches; optional browser checks use count/query (zero is data) or waitFor (timeout is data). `const`/`let` are invocation-local; explicit `globalThis` values last only within a healthy turn/target namespace. Timers are unavailable.

Default `ui.snapshot` automatic output uses a compact 32 KiB presentation budget, short opaque browser references and parent links. Truncation marks omitted nodes and children; omitted content is unknown. Guest reads retain the canonical 256 KiB budget. `full:true` and `locator.node()` provide details with the same 2,000-code-point field budgets and explicit name/description/value truncation flags. Changing detail mode resets the diff baseline; failures use the same bounded output projection.

Browser waits additionally accept `{state:'text'|'value',equals:string,timeout_ms?}` for exact visible-element textContent/value matching. They only sample state and never resend input. Native targets reject these conditions. Download cursors always include a `downloads` array, including when empty.

## Small default surface
New unrestricted turns discover only computer.targets, computer.select_target and
computer.exec. Filtering occurs after current permission and explicit allowlist
selection, never grants authority, and does not remove primitive executors.
Explicit primitive consumers and saved provider surfaces retain legacy discovery.
Canonical Retry queries only primitive names actually used in its source Turn,
through authorized public canonical queries, then applies current permissions.
Missing released query metadata is prepared once through Floret Host before the
query is retried. It does not expand unrelated retries or create a second history store. Without exec permission,
primitive read-only consumers keep their existing tools.

Only one selected-target computer call may occupy a prepared batch. Independent
tools may share that batch; Floret owns conflict admission. Rejection never replays
input or changes target binding.

Scalar attribute reads preserve string|null: an attribute over 2,000 Unicode
code points returns TARGET_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, never a silent prefix. Closed
read diagnostics retain method, expected capability and choose_supported_read
through the browser, Runtime and script result. They do not infer a replacement
element, widen scope or repeat input. The model chooses another explicit read.

## Read and validation contracts

See [script reads and validation](computer-script-read-contract.md) for success
shapes, strict argument boundaries, branchable absence/timeout and bounded
collections. Failed operations seal the invocation; they never replay input.

## Observation and references
The [semantic snapshot contract](computer-use-semantics.md) owns schema v2, role normalization, tree validation, states, relationships and privacy projection. `ui.getByRole(role, {name?, exact?, root_ref?})` uses a canonical role.

ui.snapshot returns the canonical flat snapshot directly, with one role per node;
locator.node and locator.snapshot provide direct node/subtree reads. Legacy
observe/read wrappers remain unchanged. ui.type inserts at current focus; fill
replaces contents. ui.doubleClick and ui.scroll provide native input parity.
browser.downloadCursor returns its existing fields plus an immutable wait method
bound to that cursor. Download recovery inspects existing IDs after a confirmed
click; it never repeats the export. Browser screenshots return immutable image-bound input methods with captured
frame/document identity; mutating returned metadata cannot retarget the handle.

Private takeover keeps observations and pixels out of model history.

needs_observation has one script-owned value for both execution facts and the
model result. A safe snapshot (including emit:false) or screenshot clears it;
later input, stale refs, observation failure or unknown effects require a fresh
read. observation_status describes a safe current observation in this call,
not the presence of a title. A title alone never establishes freshness.

The Runtime revalidates target policy, grants, cancellation and current control before each host operation. The target remains owned by the same canonical turn across the batch; independent live sampling may run between operations.

No second history or recovery ledger exists.
Paused and uncertain operations retain their sanitized input_progress receipt
through both script and assistance results. Posted/observed event counts describe
the interrupted operation, not a completed action or evidence to replay it.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Snapshot and node identity
Observations include `semantic_schema_version: 2`, `document_id`, `roots`, `nodes`, `truncated`, optional `focus_ref`, `total` and `execution_mode`.

Browser role resolution scans the complete authorized AX scope independently of the bounded model observation. A unique control after node 1000 remains resolvable; a duplicate beyond the presentation boundary remains ambiguous. References still require document revision and fresh DOM/AX identity validation.

`children_truncated` marks exported nodes with omitted descendants, including Runtime byte pruning. It is not evidence of empty rows or virtualization. Agents can read a row or table subtree through `root_ref`; completeness claims require checking the returned truncation facts.

Single-node reads use the same bounded observation path on browser, macOS and
Linux. child_refs only links returned nodes; an omitted child is not an empty
subtree. Native child-list read failures stop observation rather than becoming
empty arrays.

Name, description and string value have a 2,000 Unicode code-point budget.
name_truncated, description_truncated and value_truncated are true only when
the adapter omitted part of that field; snapshot truncated continues to describe
omitted nodes. Runtime validates these flags and preserves them in compact,
detailed, diff and single-node output. A detailed read does not remove field limits.
Browser query items also carry name_truncated when needed.

References compare the full native name through a bounded SHA-256 digest, never
the displayed prefix. Changed names receive different tokens so a fresh observation
cannot rebind an old reference. Browser collection cursors include complete-name digests
for every match, including items outside the current page. The existing reference
table and cursor owner remain authoritative; no additional lifecycle or replay
state exists. A failed or malformed DOM/AX identity read is observation-unavailable,
not proof of a stale reference. Preserve the observed token and sanitized protocol
method/code, reject input before dispatch, and require successful validation on a
later explicit call. Only confirmed identity changes invalidate the token. Semantic selectors match full names, including on native adapters.

Both directions of every parent/child edge must agree. An observation describes the bounded returned tree, not an exhaustive view of every application node.

## Roles, states and relationships
One Runtime alias inventory owns normalization and canonical selector expansion.
Standard landmarks including navigation, main, banner, contentinfo and
complementary, plus supported structural/live-region roles, round-trip through
this inventory. Unknown `other` remains reference-only, never a wildcard. Invalid
canonical selectors return safe field/expected/recovery diagnostics before dispatch.
Browser references are opaque bounded hashes of controller, document revision,
frame, native node identity, role and complete-name digest. The existing reference table remains their sole
owner; no second alias registry exists.

An ignored or truncated target has no invented reference; a platform-computed name or safe description may still be available.

Adapters retain the existing sensitive-field, CAPTCHA, origin/application and revision checks before exposing content. Runtime additionally rejects secure AX subroles and password-text nodes, constrains types and sizes, and strips unknown metadata.

Confirmed actions survive an observation failure; failed content never enters model history and input is not replayed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Operation facts and independent questions
Structurally confirmed password/one-time-code controls, secure native fields, missing permissions and explicit user control return structured assistance facts. Flower can make another read within its execution budget; persistent failure requires an accurate explanation, never invented instructions to inspect.

Password controls establish secret_input, not login intent. Existing explicit
login consumers remain supported. NativeWindow retains one set of pause reasons:
changed foreground/window identity reports target_focus_changed, disabled input
monitoring reports input_monitor_unavailable, and explicit private control reports
user_control. These reasons reuse the existing paused assistance and canonical
recovery path. A fresh recovery observation clears the local latch and rechecks
permissions/privacy before further input; it never replays actions. The Runtime
retains the authoritative control barrier. UI instructions describe a state check,
not an inferred user action.

Tool rows retain their execution outcome; only the separate question displays waiting.

## One canonical provenance resolver
`resolveComputerInputEvidence` is the only resolver for computer assistance. Titles, question wording, arbitrary addresses and evidence references alone are never authorization.

Existing history-bound setup acknowledgements retain their scoped continuation behavior.

## Answer, observe, continue or stop
Independent questions retain their generated question IDs, choices and text editor. A failed setup panel allows retry, close and ordinary answering or Stop; changing conversations always remains possible.

These process-local controls do not become durable Floret state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and selection
`computer.targets` lists browser profiles/pages and application windows without a preselected target. Explicit system/personal-browser tasks use `system`, which excludes managed and native window candidates and never starts a managed profile.

Set application to a name or bundle ID for bounded installed-app discovery,
including apps not running. Discovery never launches. Selecting an application
candidate opens/restores that exact catalog entry; one accessible window is
selected, while zero or multiple windows return launch facts and window candidates.
App and foreground grants, current target ownership and private pause boundaries
are checked before launch. Launch uncertainty never authorizes automatic replay.

A changed title/URL requires fresh discovery rather than a silent substitute.

## Default work and explicit switching
For `current`, the Runtime reads the thread's `computer_target_id`. An existing selection must still resolve to that exact resource.

Empty, failed and pending inventory reads retain cancellation, return and close controls.

## Persistence and fork
The migrated product store remains the only selection store.

A lost task page fails until an authorized candidate is selected. Deleting product settings removes the selection and grants; a later bind never recreates a deleted thread.

## Binding contract and observation identity
Selection returns version 2 with exact backend availability and the shared core
script guide and one bounded initial observation through the normal runtime gate.
Observation failure retains selected:true and needs_observation; private pauses
retain selection without leaking content. Confirmed app opening remains
action_executed:true. ui.help discloses read, visual and download details on demand.
The earlier verbose capability fields are superseded by this model-facing guide;
there are no product consumers of those fields. It is not a new registry or authorization source. Native adapters reject
browser-only query, attribute and image-coordinate operations before dispatch.

discovery_name is the discovery label. target_name comes from this call's
observed title, or the stable target ID if no title was observed;
observation_status distinguishes current observation from no new observation.
A failed or zero-operation script must not present an old about:blank label as a
current page. Flower activity shows localized validation/preparation/confirmed or
unknown-effect guidance from returned facts. These facts do not create retry authority.

It authorizes endpoint and thread ownership, resolves resources, sanitizes Activity, maps typed views, native updates and failures, and projects live summaries. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Flower Goals](flower-goals.md) use the optional published Goal controller. Ordinary executable items retain strict identity.

## Incremental observation and public projection
Floret supplies optional `ThreadFactsSource`, `ThreadWindowSource` and canonical body readers. The published module `v7.87.4` includes bounded item-text reads, lazy hidden-field preparation, prepared-thread startup reuse and single-mutation title summaries. Title extraction uses at most 16 KiB of the existing canonical array prefix without detail preparation or new index writes. Blank-module adoption opens released-writer fixtures and verifies historical continuation and restart. Floret alone owns text cadence, versions, append buffers, Activity reduction and canonical reads.

Root detail, child detail and command receipts use the bounded window projection. The accepted window includes its canonical Summary in the same baseline; there is no separate preparation window or independently sampled read watermark. POST history selects an authorized page and, when an observer is supplied, installs its reading interest on the same ordered Floret subscription. POST history-item expands one canonical item by its published body locators: frozen live extent, manifest parts or hash-verified field chunks. Every read refreshes endpoint, namespace and user authorization. The client never supplies raw entry locators as authority. Historical zero-byte Activity sources are synthesized only by Floret on explicit expansion; Redeven must not duplicate those defaults.

Workspace updates carry facts only; unchanged sidebar-visible facts preserve cache identity at text-stream cadence. Each observer has exactly two cancellable reading slots, for the conversation and optional child panel. Computer assistance outside the selected interval uses server-only canonical evidence, which is not included in the bounded response. See [live delivery](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) and [qualification](../operations/flower-thread-switch-qualification.md).

No database schema or migration changes are part of this optimization.

## Model output and presentation
[tool_result_encoding.go](../../internal/ai/tool_result_encoding.go) owns the single final result encoder: execution facts, tool content policy, final JSON, then Text and an independent Decoder.UseNumber Structured snapshot. Activity independently projects valid source data; its display truncation never changes model output. Floret applies the engine-owned uncertain-effect warning outside the tool payload budget, preserving complete JSON diagnostics in the next provider request and through restart/retry.

Its `request_key` remains the send idempotency identity used only to settle the short-lived browser outbox; the two values are not interchangeable.

Flower ask_user exposes only write and select_or_write. The latter always presents fixed choices with a separate custom-text answer, even when write_label is omitted. Floret owns normalization of historical select requests; Redeven does not add a second compatibility path. Ordinary InputRequired selection remains a separate contract.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The adapter may add product authorization, resource resolution, DTO mapping, and browser-safe presentation. It must not import Floret internals, read or migrate Floret storage, create a legacy run handler, infer lifecycle from error text or timestamps, or introduce a second event/retry/replay state machine.

The obsolete logged max_tool_calls declaration is removed because it never enforced a limit.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Redeven threadstore product v1 stores generated attachment identity, the authenticated user hash, a server-only relative storage name, sanitized detected media metadata, exact byte size, SHA-256, optional strict UTF-8 code-point and logical-line counts, source, state, idempotency identity, and retention claims.

The canonical Floret `ResourceRef` is content-addressed and the display locator is `attachment://v1/<attachment-id>/<encoded-name>`.

Retention ownership does not authorize canonical reads.

## Provider Preparation
Redeven derives one model-scoped capability snapshot from the selected provider route and model modalities. Strict UTF-8 text may instead use the bounded `attachment.read` host tool.

Historical reads repeat canonical membership and byte-integrity checks rather than trusting acceptance-time state. Upload/tool-image reads search current-path public Floret windows (50 items, 128-byte previews) through one authorized subscription, correlated to each requested page and a stable leaf. They never hydrate full history or authorize from retention inventory. The internal resolved handle certifies ownership and metadata only: materialization hashes while copying, text/provider/image consumers verify their exact snapshot, and public download opens verify bytes before returning a path. Thus upload materialization does not prehash and then reread the original. Reads honor cancellation and declared-size bounds; corruption never publishes a work copy.

## Canonical image recovery
Floret v7.51.1 exposes user and confirmed tool attachment descriptors through one canonical view. Upload retention recognizes tool media separately and never parses tool image references as upload records.

## Local processing and lifecycle

Immutable originals and mutable working copies share canonical thread references but have different lifetimes. attachment.materialize reauthorizes the execution identity and canonical attachment, requires RWX and the normal write-effect policy, then creates a unique regular work copy under the current thread scratch directory. Upload copies stream through a 32 KiB buffer with cancellation, exact size and SHA-256 validation. Image locators reuse bounded canonical image validation. Failed copies remove private staging; repeated same-name inputs never overwrite edited copies. Only the working path is returned, never the original backing path.

Working-file cleanup deletes copies, not inputs or historical images. Originals can be materialized again after cleanup, restart, compaction or parent deletion when another conversation retains them. Historical Fork inherits input references only through its canonical cut and independently copies current scratch/staging. Product settings and upload claims publish transactionally; no second admitted-message mapping is stored.

The Files panel derives input/media pages from the public Floret window interface with fresh product authorization. The last-reference inventory remains separate and includes inactive paths and queued inputs. External referenced files and delivered outputs keep their existing destinations and are never removed by conversation cleanup. Existing upload/media backup scope is unchanged; disposable task files are not added to backups.

sections.body: Redeven does not inspect or migrate Floret storage, persist message ordering, expose a filesystem path, accept a client owner, authorize by locator, or infer canonical membership from its claim table. Neither transport embeds bytes or a URL identity in a turn JSON body.

## Preserved snapshots
Ordinary startup, binary changes and transactional migrations do not create full snapshots. A damaged old snapshot cannot block healthy live data.

Abandoned task staging is removed only after any durable replacement completes and before a new generation opens; an unclosed generation prevents that path.

## Administrator recovery
Settings and the Flower maintenance action expose backup time, source build, size and protection.

Old unfinished Turns become terminal, old interactions become resolved and non-executable, and queued input remains canonical readonly `RestoredInputs`.

Diagnostics use the existing sanitized export and do not include conversations, credentials, database contents or uploaded files by default.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Compaction and continuation
[Manual compaction](flower-context-compaction.md) defaults to explicit continue_goal intent. Retry and restart use canonical preparation and confirmed tools. Redeven forwards intent and renders state without a second execution coordinator.

## Goal ownership and execution
User and model updates enter Floret's shared journal writer with request identity and expected version. An existing unfinished Goal remains authoritative across continuation and context restoration.

Stop cancels execution and reflection; deletion only cancels future Goal checks.

## Interaction and recovery
Selecting or entering /goal opens an in-composer command chip.

Each popup opening confirms detail through the existing read coordinator before showing canonical text.

A failed binding leaves the draft available for retry; no cross-thread target validation is relaxed and no attachment is uploaded twice.

sections.title: Contract

[Goal changes](flower-goals.md) use Floret-owned typed context facts, separate from the four product-collected partitions.

Skill rediscovery uses one authoritative catalog and deterministic text; disabled or newly restricted skills cannot reuse an activation cache. Loaded skill instructions remain historical model facts.

## Skill catalog and explicit reads
The automatic skill catalog contains current available names and descriptions in stable priority/name order.

Disabled, deleted, restricted, unreadable or invalid skills cannot return older instructions as current content.

Whole-request wire bytes and body tool-result bytes are reported separately by the regression tests; these are byte measurements, not tokenizer counts or production change rates.

## Snapshot lifecycle
UserInput.Context retains ordinary submitted facts and references. Automatic facts use ModelContextSnapshot, never historical free-text parsing.

No new thread, storage migration, historical text parsing, or product-owned snapshot is required.

Authorized canonical reads and the existing workspace subscription carry the same snapshot, record location, changed/removed keys and latest request use.

Subtask details use the same component and bounded detail cache.

## Presentation
One confirmed request supplies native input-token usage, visible Unicode character counts and recent cache rate as independent measurements. Missing historical values remain unavailable; visible characters never estimate or explain token differences, and no provider history is reconstructed.

concepts.summary:
Flower can help users create plugins, but the generated-plugin flow is not a
second plugin platform. Redeven owns the user intent capture, prompt
orchestration, review UX, approval presentation, and product timeline
projection. ReDevPlugin owns templates, validators, package builders, lifecycle
APIs, runtime contracts, sandbox surfaces, and platform policy. Floret owns the
tool dispatch and approval lifecycle that Flower must use.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
A Flower-generated plugin flow is a sequence of approved product actions over released ReDevPlugin APIs.

A plugin-generation handler may run already-approved local steps and call released ReDevPlugin adapters, but it must not perform its own approval wait, bypass Floret dispatch, mutate Flower activity rows directly, or convert plugin audit rows into Flower timeline state.

If a generated plugin needs a platform capability that does not exist in released ReDevPlugin, the requirement is recorded upstream instead of hidden behind a Redeven-local helper.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower must not write plugin registry rows, mint bridge tokens, place plugin UI assets directly under Env App routes, bypass package inspection, signature assessment, explicit confirmation, or trust policy, grant storage/network/ runtime access outside ReDevPlugin brokers, or call a business adapter before ReDevPlugin has built the request context.

A requested approval remains waiting until Floret resolves it.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
`internal/ai/prompt_builder.go` is the sole source of the base system prompt.

Visual output uses the existing [inline HTML preview](../ui/flower-inline-media.md)
contract when it communicates better than text; ordinary nonvisual answers remain
text. Existing direct WebGL guidance remains unchanged.

Delivering a created or confirmed local file requires a clickable Markdown link
with a clear file name or title and the full absolute path. Plain text or inline
code cannot be the only delivery entry point. Destinations containing spaces or
parentheses use angle brackets, such as `[Report](</workspace/report (final).html>)`.
Paths must not be invented and links must not use `file://`. Paths inside commands
and code examples may remain code. Existing authorized file previews own opening;
this prompt rule does not change historical messages or file authorization.

Discovery checks symlinks and Git boundaries; incomplete discovery and context overflow fail admission rather than silently clipping facts.

There is no separate social or creative prompt path.

Deterministic tests require the exact base prompt across all 18 permission, profile
and allowlist combinations, pin reviewed tool-definition hashes, check file-delivery
requirements and bound the prompt to 2,000 bytes.

Synthetic receipts never execute proposed tools; the Service lane runs inside disposable state. Skipped paid runs are not new model qualification, and historical scores do not establish quality for this prompt.

The base prompt adds one short execution strategy: use the most direct tool/API/CLI,
batch known steps with scripts, inspect UI state as needed, and use reported
effects/current state after interruption. This stays within the existing 2,000-byte
budget; it does not add a procedural checklist.

Default discovery still has three computer entry points. Definitions allow loops,
conditions and multiple pages within the existing budget. Selection/help responses
own exact signatures, snapshot shape, document-bound refs, automatic image output,
backend-specific coordinates and download handoff. Historical primitive consumers
retain executable contracts under current permissions.

concepts.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations

frontmatter.description: Keep canonical Floret storage opaque and preserve every supported product migration through deterministic imports.
frontmatter.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations

concepts.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns canonical Agent data and its physical and logical formats; Redeven owns product facts, read state and uploaded resources.
- Outcome: supported existing data upgrades automatically and remains usable for new conversations.
- Invariants: stable database kinds, contiguous transactional migrations, immutable historical decoders, public Floret APIs and one service generation.
- Failure boundary: unknown formats, future versions, drift or failed validation block Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Storage owners
Redeven consumes the exact published Floret version in go.mod with `GOWORK=off`.

Floret owns bounded startup recognition and background per-thread migration. Each validated dependency closure publishes atomically; retained sources retire only after complete verification. The oldest v2-v5 snapshots reserve historical identities through a resumable scan before new-thread admission. Segmented stores admit new threads immediately. Redeven uses public status, thread preparation and per-thread media contracts and never decodes upstream records.

Published Floret v7.87.0 removes hidden Activity field preparation from ordinary startup, retains summary metadata on large activity admission, batches explicit locator writes and skips same-value SQLite upserts. Its recent manifest cache is bounded, memory-only and owned upstream. No new host indexes, full-text indexes or duplicate conversation storage are introduced. First disclosure may still prepare the selected complete activity once; this is not a claim of field-granular cold preparation.

Cancellation, shutdown and execution-context settlement resolve canonical control records through Floret. The host keeps the original Stop request and does not read or reconstruct upstream conversation bodies to settle it.

A read-state failure cannot become a core Runtime constructor failure or a synthetic read record.

## Readonly checks and owner transactions
`sqliteutil` owns WAL-aware readonly preflight, integrity checks and complete SQLite snapshots for product and read-state owners. Inspection never creates missing data or runs a migration.

Required upgrade snapshots precede Floret space maintenance and all migrations, as specified by the [backup and recovery contract](flower-backup-and-recovery.md).

## Frozen historical queue conversion
The migration-only `pendinginputlegacy` package owns the complete interpretation of historical queue bytes: session identity, options, context shapes, default values, resource metadata and normalization limits.

The v4-to-v5 product transaction imports canonical pending inputs through Floret's public idempotent import API, records necessary product authority and removes retired source tables before commit. The upgrade operation contains only target build, original snapshot identity and completion; owner versions and canonical records remain the progress authority.

## Resource and authorization retention
Product upload references retain resources for every canonical thread that contains them, including ordinary forks, nested forks and restored inputs.

After activation, product recovery pages settings, retains each thread's complete descriptors and promotes eligible admitted input. Failures retain the cleanup gate while independent threads recover. Tool-media collection keeps its complete global inventory, write gate and idle constraint.

Bounded keyset maintenance and compaction stop and drain with their owning generation.

frontmatter.title: Flower working files and deliverables

concepts.summary:
Flower keeps intermediate files under the Runtime's application state and final
files at the user's destination. Redeven owns filesystem policy, bytes and UI;
published Floret owns tool results and conversation identities. No artifact
index, duplicated transcript, new Floret API or domain migration is introduced.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Placement and authority

Paths: <StateDir>/task-files/<ThreadID>/scratch and optional staging. Scratch persists helpers, data, captures and diagnostics across turns; staging holds unfinished work. Admission/provider preparation publish the same absolute paths in managed execution context. System guidance applies even when a skill suggests project-relative intermediates.

Terminal children receive FLOWER_SCRATCH_DIR/FLOWER_STAGING_DIR, no FLOWER_OUTPUT_DIR. Cwd, HOME, package caches and OS temporary variables retain semantics. Never set long thread paths as TMPDIR (Unix sockets/CLIs); OS temp follows OS lifecycle, persistent work uses scratch.

Final files go to requested/established output destinations, otherwise selected project/worktree; temporary cwd cannot redirect them. No extra export step. Source/tests/conventional builds retain normal paths. Prompts do not sandbox shell effects, and filename heuristics cannot reroute writes.

Current policy grants one private writable root without expanding project permission; sibling roots and symlink aliases are denied. Fork gets independent writable scratch; historical references grant no ancestor access. file.write, file.edit and apply_patch share this registry policy; patch cwd is only the relative-path base. Detached scratch and authorized external roots need no special patch whitelist. See [file editing](tool-permission-runtime.md).

## Fork

One action with no file selector/technical warning copies current scratch/staging for current or historical cuts. Conversation stops at the canonical cut; files are not historical snapshots. Project/final files remain shared, uncopied and unredirected.

Preparation excludes new source admissions/cleanup, waits cancellably for admitted work and rejects unreaped processes. Rooted bounded-buffer copying preserves executable helpers and validates identity/size/time plus final tree. Rename only a complete private staging tree into new ThreadID. Reject unsupported types/external links; no hard links or writable ancestor aliases.

Publish product settings and validated canonical upload retention claims in one transaction only when files are ready. Source deletion shares the preparation gate through that publication. Failed preparation is not visible/admitted; replaying that canonical Fork request completes preparation. Never recopy admitted forks after edits/cleanup. A small source marker supports interrupted publication/context, not artifact/conversation ledgers. Cleanup preserves it; deletion removes it. Recheck product ownership and remove unadmitted copies after publication failure, including cancellation. Startup/periodic recovery streams directory names in batches of 50, skips in-flight target/staging gates, and removes private stages or marked fork trees without product settings. Explicit orphan adoption/deletion shares the target gate. Retry retains the canonical fork identity and prepares a fresh independent copy; admitted copies are never recopied or removed by recovery.

Context instructs the model to inspect inherited files, map old scratch/staging suffixes into its own root and repair hardcoded paths before use, including nested forks. Do not rewrite history/content or ask users to select snapshot semantics. Ancestor cleanup/deletion cannot remove descendant copies.

## Delivery and discovery

file.present verifies a regular file outside application state, hashes cancellably and checks identity/size/mtime consistency. Return path/title/MIME/size/SHA-256/mtime/endpoint and canonical thread/turn/run identities. Never move/upload/delete; failed canonical publication cannot remove user files.

Files panel queries successful canonical results through authorized public Floret boundaries: 50 records/page, ≤32 KiB/record, original Fork/restart provenance. No startup crawl/second ledger. Recheck read authority. Available means current accessible file with unchanged size/mtime, not rehashed historical identity. Changed/missing/unavailable are observations; stored hashes describe delivery-time bytes. Files stay user-mutable, without hidden version copies.

Desktop/mobile dialog shows final results, original inputs, collapsed conversation images and expandable working files. Inputs and images reuse authorized attachment preview/download and can navigate to their source message. Material discovery reads exactly one 50-item canonical window per request, with 128-byte body previews and no full-history View or retention inventory scan. Empty intervals retain their next cursor; refresh resets a changed canonical leaf. Existing host preview/directory routing and HTML isolation remain; absent callbacks use shared image/PDF/text preview and read-only listing. Existing save destinations reauthorize each 256 KiB download chunk; version/offset drift aborts destination. Desktop allows exact thread endpoints/query keys only. Downloads neither publish nor relocate originals; browser Blob fallback retains its memory behavior.

## File panel presentation

Use the published Dialog, file-type icon catalog and Button loading affordances.
Deliverables and materials have counted section headings; conversation images
and working files use keyboard-operable, initially collapsed disclosures. Flat
rows prioritize clickable file titles, compact type/size and exceptional
availability states; successful availability does not add a badge. Raw MIME
parameters and internal endpoint IDs do not occupy primary reading space. Absolute
file paths and the working-directory address are not rendered, including tooltips
and expansion controls. Canonical paths remain action inputs for previews,
downloads and folder navigation. Long titles wrap while icon actions stay beside
the file identity at phone widths. The filename is the preview action; always-visible,
accessibly named icon controls provide downloads, folder navigation and source
messages. Counts are plain text and file icons have no backing tile. A single
header close control replaces a redundant footer; refresh sits beside the first
section heading. Cleanup remains a separate confirmed destructive action.
Only the dialog body scrolls; the header and close action remain reachable.

Browser evidence: internal/envapp/ui_src/src/ui/FlowerTaskFiles.browser.test.tsx
covers long localized names, file icons, material disclosures, desktop/phone
geometry, source routing, stale responses and protected cleanup.

## Cleanup

List ≤200 files while inspecting ≤10,000 entries; show truncation/lower bounds. Explicit confirmed RWX cleanup uses rooted operations on owned scratch/staging only. Active/queued turns, interactions, admitted work and unreaped terminals block it. In-process admissions and canonical view suffice; no durable cleanup lease/ledger.

Deletion settles canonical work and stops owned terminals before removing private files. Interrupted deletion resumes from existing product settings only when canonical Summary confirms ErrThreadDeleted; a missing/unavailable thread is never deletion authority. Maintenance checks at most 50 settings per pass, gives each attempted item a bounded wait, advances past failures, and retries retained anchors on the next cycle. Explicit deletion and recovery use the same files-then-product cleanup path, including child threads. Remove each retry anchor only after cleanup succeeds. Normal deletion refuses live work; force uses explicit cancellation. Cleanup preserves original uploads and conversation images. Thread deletion releases upload claims; the canonical retention inventory protects other paths, queues and forks until the last reference is gone. Final files are excluded, archival deletes nothing, no TTL; disclose project-local state.

sections.body:
Legacy files scattered in a project remain untouched: names such as tmp or
task-evidence do not prove ownership. The existing file browser permits explicit
user inspection/deletion; this change does not guess legacy ownership or relocate
historical paths. Complete terminal-log retention and immutable file snapshots
remain separate capabilities and are not claimed here.

frontmatter.description: Find readable conversations and browse their canonical content through a minimal tool contract.
frontmatter.title: Flower canonical thread queries

concepts.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Find, browse, read

- `threads.query` defaults to `object: threads`, listing recently updated
  conversations first. Optional `title` is one literal, case-insensitive title
  fragment. Optional `thread_id` selects one exact conversation.
- To browse `messages` or `tool_calls`, provide one `thread_id`. Records are
  chronological; there are no model-controlled sort keys or detailed filters.
- `limit` defaults to 50, with a maximum of 200. Continue with `next_cursor` and
  unchanged input. Pass a record's `ref` to `threads.read` for complete content,
  following its cursor until no continuation remains.
- Nested `filter`, message-body matching, argument/result matching, keywords,
  phrases, time/role/tool/status predicates, grouping and aggregation are not
  accepted by the tool schema or handler. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly.
- Reasoning, secrets and private provider state remain excluded. Tool arguments
  and confirmed results are available only through authorized content reads.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Authorization owner

Authenticated session authority supplies read permission, user, endpoint and
namespace identity. Redeven reconstructs the readable scope for every page and
read. Tool parameters and returned references never grant authority. Changed
scope invalidates frozen cursors; a new query starts under current permission.
The adapter uses published Floret public APIs and never reads Floret SQL or
reconstructs canonical records.

## Historical results and presentation

Saved query/read results remain previewable after restart and after their
original refs expire. The historical aggregate result renderer remains solely
for immutable already-saved tool exchanges; it cannot dispatch aggregation.
Private query contents are not added to Activity snapshots. The intent label
and explicitly opened, bounded result preview remain the presentation boundary.

## Storage and execution

The canonical owner stores source locators and metadata. Flower requires no
full-text index and schedules no startup or background indexing. Metadata-only
browsing requests one thread's ordered records; canonical full content is read
only as needed. Floret's retired optional indexing declarations are not a
product capability. The engine's published query API may retain compatibility
filters without exposing those filters to Flower's model tools.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- File mode accepts file_path and optional target_id; locator mode requires a
  canonical media:v1 locator, excludes file_path/target_id, and reuses original
  bytes without reopening the source. Default behavior remains unchanged.
- Every permission mode checks image capability, CanRead, filesystem scope and
  ToolTargetPolicy. Unavailable explicit targets fail without device fallback.
- File reads retain their 10 MiB bound; Computer snapshots retain 16 MiB.
- Locator-only crop accepts integer x/y/width/height within original image pixels,
  never clips, and saves a new lossless PNG with source_crop metadata. It uses
  fresh canonical authorization. Image pixels differ from CSS action coordinates.
- Ordinary image.read results preserve original encoding. Visual summaries may
  optimize Computer frames through [model preparation](computer-use-media.md).
  Original locators remain available; no automatic resizing or derivative cache.
- Floret preserves image order in summaries. Tokens and JSON bytes have separate
  limits; indivisible overflow fails.
- toolMediaStore retains immutable images in computer/keyframes across source
  changes, Retry, restart, Fork and compaction.
- Previews check ownership/canonical membership directly. Markdown images stay unchanged.

## Maintenance and interactive writes

One in-process media gate protects writes and the complete canonical inventory
through deletion, following Floret's published retention contract. Maintenance
skips a held gate or queued writers. An interactive write cancels a running
maintenance scan and waits for that scan to settle; its own wait honors caller
cancellation. Partial or failed inventory never authorizes deletion. No second
membership ledger, detached scan, speculative unlock or input replay is used.

## Configuration and protocol
Configuration lives at `<stateDir>/ai/mcp.json`, with schema version 2, one monotonic configuration revision, and server revisions for optimistic edits. Persistence failure leaves the in-memory catalog unchanged.

Catalog limits are 32 servers, 128 tools per server, 32 KiB per schema, and 4 MiB total persisted configuration.

Save and explicit Check read `serverInfo.icons` from the existing SDK initialize result. Connection-preserving disabled edits retain icons; changed connection settings clear stale discovery.

Rejected sources receive the generated identity described in [the shared UI contract](../ui/flower-extensions.md#entry-icons).

## Execution and dependencies
Enabled, previously discovered tools join the dynamic tool surface before the existing permission filter. Their identity binds the exact server configuration and tool schema, so a changed or disabled configuration cannot execute through an old invocation name.

Enabled, checked configuration satisfies the catalog indicator; it does not promise current network reachability or bypass approval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Evidence and projection
Lifecycle evidence may retain frozen trigger candidates, pressure and validated replacement. Floret installs complete actor-owned context before publishing its version. Changed context bypasses text cadence; equal snapshots coalesce text in bounded queues. Redeven neither accumulates usage nor reconstructs lifecycle facts, invents budgets or infers capacity from weights.

## Independent capacity evidence
Published Floret v7.89.1 supplies optional typed request-byte evidence alongside
compaction decisions. Host preparation failures include exact actual/limit byte
counts; server HTTP 413 carries no guessed counts. Both can occur while the last
measured token ratio is low. The indicator retains that confirmed ratio, while
the divider explains the independent capacity cause and message-text estimate.
Cause-only events, reloads and Desktop RPC retain this distinction. Historical
records without this evidence remain unknown; no error-text inference is used.

## Timeline
One row between short separators uses a compact surface-owned tooltip without expansion or reflow. Success labels canonical message text estimates explicitly, never as full provider-request input. Localize missing-count, running and cancelled explanations. Wrap original errors without clipping; localize the fallback only when absent.

The tooltip follows the active surface and global theme outside chat. Prefer above, or below near the top boundary. Delay pointer-exit dismissal for hovering/selection. Escape, Tab, blur and outside clicks dismiss it; the visibility owner closes it on process collapse. Retain keyboard/touch access and independent retry.

## Capability and transport
OpenAI-compatible Chat reasoning is capability-driven. Redeven reads only response fields named by that result, emits their fragments as reasoning without trimming provider whitespace, and never treats reasoning-only output as assistant body text.

Budget-only and fixed-thinking models never acquire synthetic effort names or a toggle merely because another model supports one.

## Default selection
Default asks for the model's own reasoning behavior. Thread creation, Thread
edits, and every Turn canonicalize it once, in
`config.CanonicalAIReasoningSelection`: on a model without verified reasoning
controls a budget-free Default is the omitted selection and is neither stored
nor sent. Default with a budget, Off, On, and named efforts remain explicit
intent and are rejected for such a model; personal memory keeps no reasoning
choice for it. Clients may send Default without knowing the model's capability
and must not drop or rewrite it themselves.

## Settings ownership
Thread model, reasoning and permission settings are Redeven product state. Execution authority records admission permission for historical attribution only, never as live tool authorization. The configured `current_model_id` initializes future threads only.

## Automatic titles
Published Floret v7.26.0 owns title reasoning and output limits. They never change the thread's saved reasoning choice or the main response policy.

The [live timeline contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) owns canonical title status, persistence, and workspace-summary presentation.

frontmatter.title: OKF bundle lifecycle

concepts.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`build_assets.sh` invokes `build_okf_bundle.sh`, which runs `cmd/okf-bundle` against explicit source and dist roots. The builder emits the bundle, manifest and checksum deterministically. Summary and section bodies are embedded as structured data; Evidence remains in its source file but is omitted from ordinary concept opening unless requested. `okf/dist/*` is generated from source and is never an authoring surface.

## Quality gates
Report mode exposes layout, indexing, summary, evidence, duplication, lifecycle and budget issues without blocking cleanup. Strict mode fails structural and source-integrity violations, overdue reviews, and source totals above the hard cap. Final integration runs strict content quality after source integrity and before verifying the generated bundle.

## Source budget
Count Unicode characters in every source Markdown file under `okf/`, including the index and log, after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exclude `okf/dist/`. The report shows total, remaining capacity and index/concept/log usage. Exceeding 900,000 warns; strict quality accepts exactly 1,000,000 and fails above it. A per-concept `quality_exception` cannot waive this hard cap.

## Review and log lifecycle
Every concept declares `lifecycle` and `reviewed_at`: review contracts every 180 days, active measurements and operational evidence every 90 days, and retained history every 365 days. Retained history also needs a concise `retention_reason`. Report mode warns and strict mode fails on invalid or overdue metadata; expiry prompts review and never deletes a document automatically. Keep `log.md` to compact summaries from the last 30 days after durable knowledge moves into its concept.

## Index and retention
Keep categories and concept links in the index; the parser derives each retrieval summary from the concept's `# Summary`. Prefer an existing concept, preserve only decision-relevant historical conclusions and counterevidence, and remove obsolete detail from the current tree so Git history remains the recovery path.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Runtime OKF code loads the embedded bundle once, indexes root directory sections, scores structured summaries and sections in memory, and opens a concept summary or one selected section by id or path. Internal ids, paths, and unfiltered result objects never enter that display contract. OKF activity labels and operation values come from `ToolPresentationSpec`, so the Floret projection does not own a separate OKF display vocabulary.

## Tool workflow
`okf.index` browses `okf/index.md` as a structured directory and returns summaries plus section counts. `okf.search` returns a bounded short candidate list with query-aware snippets and the best matching section id/title; title and Summary matches outrank section body matches.

Models should follow `okf.index -> okf.search -> okf.open Summary -> okf.open section` and must not rely on snippets for detailed contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The tools return scoped Redeven repository knowledge and do not mutate OKF source or dist artifacts. They must not be used for current news, recent public events, market or pricing facts, third-party documentation, external facts, or general web facts. Source-level conclusions still require file or terminal verification after OKF navigation.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |

## Kimi Code
The kimi_code provider uses its own subscription key and official China/global coding endpoint. Admit only six reviewed model/wire identities, capacity ceilings and reasoning levels. An explicit 1M override is user intent, not entitlement evidence. Preparation rejects unknown IDs, thinking-off and response-ID continuation before dispatch.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
The `subagents` tool supports spawn, send input, wait, list, status, inspect, close, and close all.

The model-facing result keeps child identity, task name, status, current turn, queue count, failure and interaction facts. Display timestamps, duplicated IDs and counts, and UI action flags remain outside that projection. Spawn and wait do not repeat task descriptions; list and explicit inspect retain them. A preview is omitted only when the same result carries the complete handoff.

Complete handoff bodies bypass generic output caps. Explicit event reads retain their full page contract. Bounded-wait and input-request metadata derive from the original execution result, never its compact model projection. Wait returns on child events and includes available complete reports; inspect explicitly reads reports. Tool descriptions state input and output semantics without prescribing a coordination workflow.

Parent reports, lifecycle events, bounded waiting, and the compact event panel are described in [Subagent parent events](subagent-parent-events.md).

Forks copy conversation facts, never child ownership.

Missing targets are presented as missing rather than completed or timed out.

frontmatter.title: AI terminal tool runtime

concepts.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. One adapter authorizes execution once and publishes current views. Product SQL stores no parallel terminal lifecycle or effect recovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Task-file placement](flower-task-files.md) supplies thread scratch/staging through
child-only environment variables while preserving project cwd and OS temporary
path conventions. Cleanup waits for owned terminal processes to be reaped.

PTYs use Floret execution/effect identities. `terminal.exec` waits 5 seconds when `yield_ms` is omitted or zero; positive values cap at 30 seconds. Yield returns a running process ID without stopping the command.

On macOS/Linux, one exit worker observes command exit without reaping, kills its process group, retires numeric signaling, verifies no live members within 2 seconds, then reaps and drains output. The unreaped root pins its PID through cleanup. Child cleanup preserves shell exit codes; only confirmed Stop termination means cancellation. Stop, input failure, the 30-minute limit and Service shutdown share this worker. Unconfirmed cleanup reports a runtime error and retains workload admission. Settlement stops the watchdog.

Long-lived commands stay foreground under the yielded process ID. Backgrounding and `nohup` cannot transfer ownership; escaping the PTY group/session is unsupported. Independent services need a managed lifecycle; previews use the managed browser. Names, CPU use and age never establish ownership.

`terminal.read` observes output after the caller's sequence for up to 60 seconds, returning early on output/exit. An expired observation retains process ID and cursor and reports `wait_expired`/`wait_ms`; `timed_out` means command timeout. Continue with the same ID and returned `last_seq`, without sleeps or command restarts.

Normal expiry uses Floret `BoundedWait`; Floret measures handler time and owns repeat protection. Immediate, failed, canceled and early reads gain no exemption, nor do neighboring repeated effects. No extra retry counter, clock, wake or durable ledger exists.

Reads are read-only effects: cancellation preserves process and cursor, then confirms the canceled result after observation returns. Execution/input retain shell-effect uncertainty rules. `terminal.write` bounds stdin; `terminal.terminate` kills the owned group and waits for reap/output drain. Thread Stop policy governs cleanup.

Read results contain incremental output, status, cursor, wait and exit facts. Command, cwd and timing remain in canonical Activity without repeated model echoes.

Browser payloads exclude local working paths, stdin, authorization proofs, and effect internals.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: No authority barriers, admission receipts, recovery handles or projection-cursor waits exist. Reads never retry settlement. Open-detail polling refreshes bytes, never canonical status or provider dispatch.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Official surface
- `tessiven.runtimes` / `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven/runtimes` returns   independent source availability and exact target paths. - `tessiven.runtime.inspect` / `POST .../runtimes/inspect` reads status,   bounded public diagnostics, or the original Desktop operation. - `tessiven.runtime.action` / `POST .../runtimes/actions` requests connection   or one supported `start`, `stop`, `restart`, or `update` process operation. - `tessiven.inspect/action` retain the canonical canvas version, bound instance,   and resource identity checks for Managed Services and containers.

No sibling module, replacement SDK, or product lifecycle queue is introduced.

## Source authority and discovery
Desktop registers its Tessiven host through owner-authenticated private Runtime control. Web Service, CodeSpace, nested frame, unrelated-origin and worker requests cannot declare a native source;

Ambiguous references fail closed.

## Connection and business access
Explicit connect reuses saved configuration and existing connection leases.

It cannot carry claimed permission flags, an arbitrary URL, another Runtime reference, or a process-lifecycle action.

Member removal and replacement retire the transport; no local or alternate route is substituted.

## Native lifecycle handoff
Process actions use saved direct Desktop placements and the existing [Desktop lifecycle owner](../desktop/desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md). The model cannot choose a download URL or release version; the existing release selector owns updates and post-operation verification.

Unknown connection outcomes require checking the selected connection in its native owner rather than retrying.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Default Flower tools omit write_todos; historical Todo results remain readable. The Floret-native goal tool has independent control ownership; see [Flower Goals](flower-goals.md).

## Mechanism
The registry includes readonly file/search helpers, standard mutation, patch, terminal, web search, OKF, interaction, skill, subagent, MCP, and Floret-native tools. Structured detail uses Floret's bounded typed rows; operation, status, repeated names, and raw tool fields never create an expand affordance.

The resolver validates MIME, size, and digest through the target-owned media store; it never stores image bytes in durable tool state.

## File editing

Redeven owns Flower patch execution. cwd only resolves relative input paths;
the filesystem registry owns logical/canonical write policy for every local
patch and Move endpoint, including authorized roots outside cwd and the current
thread's private scratch. Readonly roots, private siblings/ancestors and their
symlink aliases remain denied. Target-routed tools retain target-owned policy.

Symlinks and new-file ancestors resolve before Floret authorization. Execution
compares the ordered canonical resource sequence, rejecting swapped destinations
as well as changed targets. Plans retain submitted paths and re-resolve them at
full preflight, before each file commit and before Move source deletion. Source
and destination snapshots must still match. These checks do not eliminate every
filesystem TOCTOU race or constitute an OS sandbox.

Use file.edit for unique literal replacements, file.write for complete files,
and apply_patch for multi-chunk/file changes. Its strict JSON input argument and
declared routing fields have no patch or input_format aliases. Model names never
imply endpoint support for freeform grammar.

Chunks search original content forward, honoring anchors, EOF and numeric ranges.
Only order failures allow reordering: every chunk needs one exact, non-overlapping
match, without anchors, ranges, EOF markers or pure additions. Sorted chunks use
the same matcher and write plan. Forward patches, recorded arguments and rejection
classifications remain unchanged. Ambiguity names the blocking chunk and requests
unique context. The provider still requests source order.

Pure additions append. Untouched lines retain their endings; insertions use the
first ending (LF for empty files), and nonempty updates retain a final newline.
Exact matching precedes whitespace and punctuation normalization. Explicit Add
and Move may replace regular files. Use one operation per canonical path.

Diagnostics distinguish order, overlap, anchor, EOF, repeated/missing context and
duplicate paths, with chunk, patch-body line, search boundary, exact source line
when available, and a remedy. They never select writes. Floret validates JSON.

Plans validate before writing and recheck source/destination snapshots per commit.
Validation errors confirm no writes; commit errors report completed operations
and uncertain effects, never permission to replay. completed_files retains whole
operation completion semantics. Partial result data and canonical Activity carry
only confirmed mutations, paths, counts and actual before/after diffs. If a Move
writes its destination but cannot delete its source, report the destination's
create/update diff against its own prior contents, not a completed rename.
Replacement is atomic per file, not per patch or Move. The existing published
Floret ordered-resource, EffectOutcome and typed PatchActivity contracts own
authorization, settlement and persistence; no second lifecycle is introduced.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and execution

Discover Docker/Podman independently, one service/engine, no inactive-context scan/fallback. Each has a shared two-second command budget; reuse selected endpoint inventory for health. Resource readiness stays separately bounded. Docker Desktop requires selected desktop-linux/desktop-windows context or exact endpoint alias; installed plugins cannot claim other engines. Validate with docker desktop version --format json, never slow desktop status. Resolve Podman Machine ownership before health.

Known Desktop management/health errors retain ID, implementation, config sources and supported actions. Missing CLI/permission/timeout/unknown failures never mean stopped. Start requires stopped; Stop/Restart running. Save-and-restart requires known state before writes; plain save remains available.

Typed lifecycle actions share two minutes across steps, separate from ten-second query/two-second discovery; parent deadlines/cancel apply. macOS Start uses /usr/bin/open -g -b com.docker.docker then bounded endpoint polling; Restart stops first under that deadline. Other platforms/Stop use official CLI. LaunchServices receives only identity/home/PATH/temp/shell/locale/timezone/proxy/certificates, excluding Redeven metadata, Electron/Node controls, CLI overrides and secrets. Explicit empty env stays empty; CLI/probes retain theirs. Launch acceptance is not success; reload final state while locked. Never elevate, sudo/pkexec/polkit, alter groups/socket permissions.

Read-gated GET /_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources/services exposes mode/source IDs; one failure cannot hide another. Migration maps legacy state→engine and client_proxy→docker_cli.

## Interaction

One preflight confirmation shows service name, localized risks/impact counts and action; no retyped name/extra review. Client binds name; server checks identity/authority/request+plan hashes. Cancel creates no operation; duplicates stay locked. Hide hashes/raw prose; history resolves names/localized errors.

Settings entry warns. Header aligns outlined square Back/title independently of description; narrow target≥44px. Refresh retains cards, animates only indicator and uses inline errors. Known Desktop/unknown health retains disabled Start/guidance; revalidation enables it. Active divider section replaces normal controls with elapsed/cancel/secondary history. Failure exposes recovery/revalidation. History never auto-opens; unmeasured work has no percent. SSE/poll completion reloads service/runtime facts.

Observed health leads; active work retains locks/feedback. Terminal start/restart failure leaves card on running; stop failure leaves on stopped. Unknown/config failures retain recovery; completed/cancelled records stay in history. Current running never rewrites restart result. History keeps original result/error/duration apart from current state, no empty errors or historical time as live progress.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: `containerengine` owns exact argv, validation, atomic replacement/rollback and observation. `containerresource` owns preflight, impact, locking and sanitized durable state. Local API owns Read/RWX/Admin and no-store delivery. Docker Desktop/Podman Machine/remote tools retain private settings; administrators own installation/OS authority.

frontmatter.title: Native container operation observation

concepts.summary:
Every native Containers mutation has one durable Redeven operation identity and
one resource-local lock. Submission, cancellation, progress events, restart
recovery, and terminal reconciliation flow through `containerresource`.
Inventory refreshes and UI observation never become a second lifecycle owner.
Lost submissions, stale plans, runtime restarts, and unavailable engines are
reported explicitly and are never hidden behind automatic replay.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Admission and serialization
The operation key contains engine, opaque endpoint ID, resource kind, and canonical identity.

Reusing a request ID with different hashes produces an idempotency conflict instead of a second operation.

## Execution, cancellation, and events
The service owns an operation context from queued state through reconciliation. Cancellation is an explicit API action; closing Activity, Workbench, an inspector, an event stream, or the browser never implies cancellation.

Terminal errors use a small public taxonomy for storage, registry availability, rate limiting, not-found, and access denial; the drawer maps known codes to localized guidance alongside the durable timeline. Unknown codes use a localized generic failure; codes and backend messages remain diagnostic evidence, not visible UI copy. Timeout guidance acknowledges that host work may still be in progress. Desktop service cards direct users to its native application for setup/startup recovery and expose status revalidation. Service history shows state transitions without generic execution stages or a synthetic percentage bar.

## Authoritative terminal observation
After engine execution returns, the service reloads the exact endpoint-bound resource or relevant bounded inventory.

The operation is never replayed, regardless of whether the resource appears present or absent.

## UI observation
Inventory requests and streams are fenced by source runtime, endpoint, resource view, and request generation. A superseded response cannot replace current data.

Mobile and desktop expose the same state and cancellation authority. Service lifecycle feedback stays on its card; history is secondary. Polling terminal transitions refresh authoritative service/runtime facts even when the event stream was lost. The portaled history drawer owns its responsive container and independent scrolling. Desktop uses a history sidebar; narrow drawers place a horizontal history strip above details. Rows use stable operation IDs and pressed selection; polling preserves focus and detail nodes. Details separate identity, live cancellation, duration/current health and timeline. The active final timeline step uses a pending indicator, never a completed check.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: - The database is operation evidence, not a mutation queue or replay journal. - UI inventory and SSE consumers observe service authority; they do not own   lifecycle state or reconciliation. - A runtime restart converts active work to interrupted after read-only   observation; it never assumes success or retries the command. - The full native container ownership contract is defined in   [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md).

Cross-database atomicity is never assumed or simulated by copying upstream lifecycle state into Redeven tables.

All built-in browser event subscriptions and the ReDevPlugin host request adapter use that runtime's logical streams. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One session and one request path
Product subscriptions call the Shell-bound session event reader. Floe Webapp's acquisition lifecycle opens a logical HTTP stream on the current Flowersec session and parses SSE with its shared bounded parser.

Session multiplexing removes those event requests from the browser HTTP pool; changing request priority alone cannot do so.

## Authority and resource lifetime
Local session issuance declares only Env App API and plugin API paths plus the plugin CSRF and expected-management-revision headers. Remote issuers must declare the same plugin request authority and upload cap in their signed scope.

Product code must not reset a successful response while its bytes are still being consumed.

## Observation and recovery
Flower maintains one workspace stream; thread selection never reconnects it.

Its transport and cancellation regression coverage remain intact.

concepts.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
concepts.description: Compare aligned user operations and operating-system limits for macOS and Linux host applications.

frontmatter.description: Compare aligned user operations and operating-system limits for macOS and Linux host applications.
frontmatter.title: Cross-platform host application behavior

concepts.summary:
Host Applications separates viewing, sharing, window closure and process exit on
both platforms. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and respect app cancellation.
Only an independently confirmed Force quit may bypass saving. The backend owns
process evidence, and the interface names the actual supported operation. OS
session, display and service policies remain authoritative; unavailable recovery
must not silently relaunch an unrelated or replacement process.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
| Operation | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close outer Desktop window / browser popup | Release this client lease; app survives | Same |
| Network loss, reload, second viewer | Reconnect same live app; stale input is revoked | Same |
| Release this client lease | End this capture/route; other clients and app survive | End this proxy/route; other clients and app survive |
| No window for more than 40 seconds | Waiting, with native menu/reopen | Waiting, reconnect same process without relaunch |
| Close last window | Viewer closes; app decides whether its process exits | Same |
| Cancel normal close/quit | Preserve application and save dialog | Same; ordinary control is Close all windows |
| Explicit Force quit in library | Confirm loss warning; exact AppKit instance | Confirm loss warning; exact owned backend and descendants |
| Orderly Runtime shutdown or process exit | Native app remains discoverable | Private display survives; new Runtime verifies/reconnects it |
| Running list | Regular apps in the logged-in OS session | Caller-owned Redeven instances, including detached/windowless apps |
| Host reboot / display server destruction / OS cleanup | No survival guarantee | Same; Runtime cgroup cleanup may also end its virtual display |

## Accepted operations and visible state
Quit and force-quit requests are asynchronous. The Host Applications surface must close the confirmation dialog after acceptance and show a per-application pending state until the authoritative running snapshot confirms the target instance is gone.

The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request.

sections.body: Linux cannot generically request AppKit-style application quit or reopen, nor adopt an arbitrary process on another display. macOS requires its real logged-in graphical session and explicit capture/input permissions. Neither backend can preserve an application after its OS or display environment has been destroyed.

The `host:v3` identity binds service ID, launch nonce, PID, and a digest of native facts:

New identities never use formatted dates, timezone, command text, or `kern.boottime`.

`localui.Server` is built with an agent, Code App app server, bind spec, runtime-control socket path, Local Environment identity, diagnostics store, and optional access gate.

Opening settings never resizes the app.

A browser advertising H.264 WebCodecs software decoding can receive VideoToolbox hardware video. Hardware encoder unavailability uses JPEG images; a browser decoder failure explicitly renegotiates image transport.

Unchanged resize requests retain frame credit.

Runtime diagnostics record connection-to-first-frame duration and generation; the browser debug log measures connection-to-first-decoded-frame duration.
