sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Waiting and process lifetime
A running process without its first shareable window remains attached indefinitely; there is no first-window termination deadline. Releasing the current client lease during this wait ends that sharing lease normally; missing pixels do not turn a lease release into a launch failure. An unexpected helper exit is a failed sharing session, not evidence that the host application ended.

## Window evidence
The window registry distinguishes present, unknown and confirmed-empty inventories. No first-window deadline is introduced.

## Capture and recovery
Capture availability is independent of lifetime. AX identity survives a capture-surface replacement while the input generation is renewed; retired callbacks cannot update the replacement. Failure to launch and unexpected helper loss remain failures; missing pixels do not change a confirmed process exit into a failed launch.

## Terminal state
Terminal state retains the native end reason: `application_exited` confirms the bound process exited, `windows_closed` confirms its last shared window closed, and `sharing_stopped` confirms detachment. Closing windows and stopping sharing never claim the process has quit. The [lifecycle validation matrix](../operations/host-application-lifecycle.md) separates automated recovery evidence from OS/application compatibility limits.

Redeven supplies session, authorization, web-security, trust, official release-source, observability, secret, external source, and business adapters; it never edits registry, inspection, token, lease, revoke-epoch, or plugin-data state directly.

The official signed-release module remains the stricter release-ref path.

## Surfaces and interaction ownership
The product Shell owns one released `PluginPlatformClient`, authenticated transport, and shared surface scope.

Redeven uses them for host placement behavior, never as identity, authorization, or permission evidence.

A recovery presentation may explain or retry the Host snapshot, but it is not a second open gate and owns no catch-up identity state machine.

macOS uses the exact remote Swift package in the existing Runtime helper.

The canonical official Alpine source remains the final fallback; every download still checks the expected size and SHA-256 before atomic cache publication, and a failed archive download can move to the next trusted source.

Capability normalization also applies to a retried connection after accepting or declining takeover, so a removed display cannot return through the stored request.

## Media and office interaction
Control and media travel through separate Flowersec native proxy streams bound to the same product attachment. Cancellation retires the selection and releases held keys; lock-screen input cannot use that text path.

Native session and frame authority remain governed by this concept.

Runtime publishes its own service protocol and independent component version. A missing or incompatible Gateway fails closed only for lifecycle management.

Runtime snapshot fields and generated wire schemas change together; an unknown response key must not turn a healthy Runtime into a reconnect loop.

Compatibility epoch 35 requires both Desktop and Runtime to understand explicit reasoning `on` alongside the existing default, off, effort, and budget choices. Earlier clients reject `on`; ordinary epoch admission prevents a mixed pair from accepting a Flower or Desktop model-source request it cannot interpret. See the [reasoning selection contract](../ui/flower-reasoning-selection.md) for model capability and control semantics.

Epoch 59 pairs Runtime authorization requests with the shared Desktop and Env App OpenAI account picker. A saved registry requires an account selection or explicit new-registration intent; old Desktop clients must update before Flower access. Registration semantics belong to the [ChatGPT account lifecycle](../ai/chatgpt-account-lifecycle.md).

Epoch 65 requires the model directory's backend-owned default_fetch_source field in provider search policies. See [model web search](../ai/model-web-search.md).

Epoch 67 requires complete changed pin metadata in Flower pin confirmations. New pins append to the endpoint's existing order; Desktop and Runtime must agree on the changed ranks and revisions before a confirmation is accepted. See [sidebar pin ordering](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md).

## AI Flower RPC registration
The local direct and remote agent production session profiles register the complete AI inventory before Flowersec freezes a session. A declared method therefore cannot fail at the router with a missing-handler 404. Stop remains one RPC lifecycle command without a fallback transport.

## Mechanism
The released runtime dependency set includes Floeterm terminal-go v0.19.2 and Flowersec Go v5.11.1.

frontmatter.description: Keep service facts, user goals, resource cleanup, and management archives actionable across failures and Runtime restarts.
frontmatter.title: Web Service management recovery

concepts.summary: Registry owns lifecycle records/transactions; Manager observes resources and available actions; Renderer presents current state, last result and next step. Unavailable inspection is not absence; historical failure is not current state. Destruction requires fresh ownership/explicit cleanup. Authorized detach works with an offline engine but preserves resources and claims no process stop.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Facts and actions
`ServiceFacts` separates presence, ownership, runtime state, inspection completeness, resource references, and check time.

Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start.

A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

## Review and execution
`GET /managed-web-services/{id}/inspection` requires read permission, is non-cacheable, and uses the same factual backend projection as the list.

Existing unrelated lifecycle transactions cannot be overwritten by recovery.

Instance-scoped allocation and legacy resource boundaries are owned by [Service resource ownership](service-resource-ownership.md).

## Uninstall transaction
Uninstall uses `runtime_manifest_json`, the existing operation coordinator, and the existing event stream.

A resource recreated under the same name cannot acquire the previous deletion authorization.

Detachment remains available while it is unresolved.

## Management archives and access
Registry version 4 adds `active`, `detached`, and `uninstalled`. Only active records participate in template uniqueness and must own an authorized Forward.

Names, ports, or cached reachability never prove ownership.

Failed migration rolls back completely; unknown versions and structural drift remain read-only failures. Desktop/Runtime compatibility epoch 15 covers these management contracts.

concepts.description: Share entry behavior between independent Desktop and server hosts.

frontmatter.description: Share entry behavior between independent Desktop and server hosts.
frontmatter.title: Independent Web Environment Center

concepts.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center deploys independently; Runtime never requires Center or Desktop to start. Both hosts share Contracts/Core/Controller/UI. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Shared behavior and host ownership

`desktop/src/envcenter` owns exact route identity, search/filter, failure/recovery classification, operation ordering, cancellation and Gateway list presentation. Desktop's adapter invokes its existing main-process lifecycle/window owner; Web invokes Center HTTP and browser tabs. Shared modules cannot import Electron, Node filesystem APIs or Web authentication.

Desktop does not contact Center, acquire Center credentials, or change Welcome layout, default navigation, local preparation preferences or shutdown ownership. Host configuration/secrets do not synchronize automatically. Go DTOs generate TypeScript and JSON schema through `cmd/center-contracts`, including enum/integer bounds.

Labels/hostnames grant no trust. Directory revisions and operation sequences reject stale observations. A canceled pending tab cannot navigate after delayed completion; cancellation preserves an already-open route owner. Refresh reads authority instead of creating another intent.

## Server entry

Portal, each Env and each child application use distinct HTTPS origins on the same registrable domain and port. TLS covers all origins. Browser bookmarks remain explicitly direct links.

Binding descriptor copy is a browser capability, not a network operation. Clipboard denial or absence produces local, localized manual-copy guidance without discarding the descriptor or changing authorization. Keyboard-accessible text selection remains available, and success is announced only after the browser confirms the write.

Center pairs as an access-only Gateway client after fingerprint confirmation. Runtime consent is independently persisted by `redeven web-binding apply --stdin --yes`. Binding pins Runtime ID, exact origin, client SPKI, application scope and revision. Published Flowersec carries mutually authenticated TLS 1.3 to the signed, pinned Runtime service. The target needs no inbound application TCP listener.

Each operation belongs to one administrator device and route. Browser nonce, exact origins, bounded redemption and a single-use code complete handoff. Same-request response-loss retry recovers one outcome. Host-only cookies do not replace Runtime password/MFA. Logout, security changes and source/route revocation cancel derived admissions/streams.

## Runtime and child applications

`internal/webbinding` owns durable consent; `internal/webconnector` composes pinned TLS; `internal/environmentcenter` owns administrator authority, directory and proxy admission. Deployed Center requires a separate state-free Connector process through a local Unix socket. Both peers verify the configured OS UID before exchanging credentials. Only admitted route credentials enter worker memory; administrator state, factors and master key remain with Center. Embedded protocol tests may use the direct adapter; deployed services never silently fall back.

A live control connection owns each worker lease. Center loss, logout or security revocation closes it and every derived stream. Connector restart loses leases; only a still-valid Center admission may establish a fresh lease on the next request. Business HTTP requests are never replayed by this owner. Systemd and Compose use distinct unprivileged identities and deny Connector access to Center state/TLS-key mounts.

IPC preserves bounded machine error codes so permission, capacity, compatibility and offline failures retain shared recovery semantics. Runtime responses cannot inject worker error authority. The published connection controller owns retry timing; only explicit transient Gateway admission conflicts are retryable, while denied/revoked identity and invalid proofs remain terminal.

Services, editor and graphical viewers receive resource-specific origins. Parent Runtime credentials stay in the trusted proxy and never reach child browsers. Editor admission pins the running instance. Raw graphical routes cannot bypass resource-scoped Flowersec. Child responses retain authenticated Runtime framing policy so editor worker iframes work; portal framing remains denied.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Center is trusted with plaintext application traffic. This is not browser-to-Runtime encryption against Center. Forwarded headers, loopback, SSH tunnels and browser-supplied headers cannot create management authority.

Web v1 does not implement Desktop SSH/WSL/local preparation, Cloud aggregation or local account/model delegation. Existing Desktop capabilities retain their owners. Remote terminal/files/Git/monitoring/container/Flower and graphical capabilities retain ordinary Runtime permissions and platform conditions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
The Code App app server backend owns codespace lifecycle, port resolution, managed runtime status, setup operations, Desktop-transfer chunks, completion, version selection, version removal, and operation cancellation. Only one setup operation may run at a time, an accepted operation id cannot be reused during the RuntimeManager lifetime, and stale chunk, completion, cancellation, or progress updates cannot terminate or overwrite a different operation.

External system-browser and ordinary browser opens retain the existing Local UI or remote launcher flow.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Resource intent and route ownership
After starting the selected CodeSpace, Env App submits `mode: browser` and its CodeSpace ID through the same root-frame-only IPC used for built-in editor windows.

The system browser never receives a private Local UI `/cs/<id>` URL, an environment credential, or a raw gateway header.

Runtime accepts only this shaped loopback origin or the built-in numeric-loopback origin as presentation metadata; that metadata never selects an upstream dial target.

## One-time entry and browser session
Only main can mint an entry from the gateway object.

Runtime and editor traffic never carries the browser cookie; upstream responses cannot set the reserved cookie name.

An OS-open failure closes the newly acquired gateway and route.

concepts.summary:
- Authority: the launcher owns Desktop, local Runtime, saved local Gateways, and bundles.
- Outcome: run current source, stop together, prune obsolete bundles.
- Invariants: preserve user data, identities, unrelated services, and recent, selected or live bundles.
- Failure boundary: preparation errors clean up; incomplete inventory prevents pruning.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Build and launch

scripts/dev_desktop.sh captures HEAD/current tracked and non-ignored source; concurrent edits fail. Generated OKF/ignored assets are outputs; protect authored OKF/builders/Go embeds. A profile-local receipt reuses output only when HEAD, dirty source, dependency bytes, toolchains, target/settings and verified Desktop/immutable Runtime bytes match. Missing/changed/incomplete output rebuilds; failed preparation never launches old bundles. Only installing pinned Rust admits preparation-time toolchain drift.

--rebuild forces build; REDEVEN_AGENT_FORCE_INSTALL=1 reinstalls all three JS packages once. Manifests choose pnpm/npm; receipts bind selected locks/toolchain, not a second installer from compatibility locks. First launch establishes receipts.

On macOS, preparation reads enabled static HTTP/HTTPS system proxies once and exports them to dependency and bundle build tools. Any explicit HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY variable (including lowercase or empty values) owns network policy and disables discovery; REDEVEN_DEV_SYSTEM_PROXY=0 also opts out. Preserve explicit NO_PROXY; otherwise include loopback and compatible system exclusions. PAC/SOCKS-only settings require explicit environment policy. Diagnostics never expose credentials; TLS and official artifact verification remain mandatory. Remove only inferred variables before launching Desktop, Runtime or Gateways.

Official Node checksum and archive acquisition share a three-attempt budget per transfer, with one- and two-second backoff for transient transport failures and HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504. Read origin and proxy CONNECT status separately from artifact bytes; permanent HTTP and certificate errors stop immediately. Retry the same official URL under the existing proxy policy. Resume only the current build's temporary archive; verify the complete checksum before caching, remove failed partial files, and require fresh official checksums even for cached archives.

Development may cache Cargo registry/targets while staging exact locked published crates freshly. Verify digest/execution/consumption and regenerate evidence. Complete caches resolve/install offline; incomplete caches follow acquisition policy with diagnostics. Corrupt crates or compiler failure cannot retry via another path. Release Cargo dirs stay isolated. Source changes rebuild whole product, not component/watch mode.

Desktop compilation overlaps Runtime preparation. Runtime assets/Go, plugin staging and Computer resources have independent outputs. Env App no-emit typecheck overlaps bundling under its checkout lock. Notices run after all asset tasks because installed metadata/YAML parser cannot race cold dependency install. Go waits for embeds; publication/receipts wait for all builds and unchanged-input checks. Release order stays sequential.

Three dependency-scan workers overlap toolchain probes with serial-equivalent digests/order. Supervisors label diagnostics, preserve failures and stop owned groups/descendants on cancel or sibling failure.

Saved local Gateways reuse compatible intact installs; Desktop source change does not force replacement. Service owner prepares missing/damaged packages; explicit Update selects current build. Verified archive caches bind full launch input key including dirty source; changed keys discard previous generation, missing key creates session cache. Package owner verifies archives.

Dev embedded compression: gzip1/Brotli4 with identical decoded bytes; ordinary/release use maximum. Profile enters build identity. Gateway source copies omit unrelated worktrees/native caches. Logs separate dependencies/verification/Desktop/Runtime/Gateway phases and total. Empty-profile warm timings cannot certify changed-source/saved-Gateway launches; qualify both rebuilt/reused launches with local Gateway, exact Runtime commit and cleanup.

Normal exit, preparation failure, Ctrl+C/SIGTERM stop only owned local services; production shutdown semantics remain. Electron resolution emits path only, logs to stderr, propagates failure and rechecks executable after dependency builds.

## Credentials and retention

Unpackaged dev encrypts with AES-256-GCM/random profile key 0600, retained with profile; protects plaintext, not same-user access. Other launches use Electron system storage without constructor probing. Legacy Keychain opens recovery without reading preferences/system secrets; only explicit action decrypts and atomically migrates each file. Failure preserves credentials/retry/quit; corrupt keys require repair, never reset accounts/Runtime/Keychain.

Publish complete bundles under <development-state-root>/desktop/bundles/<manifest-sha256>. Keep newest three, selected (including reuse) and all live bundles. This bounds inactive verified package count, not bytes; active/unverified entries may grow.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime state identity
Each Runtime state directory owns an immutable Ed25519 seed in `access-identity.key`. Invalid or symlinked existing material fails closed and is never replaced.

Existing TLS, Gateway trust and Runtime authentication remain authoritative.

## Observation and grouping
Main-process observations bind an entry ID to its configured connection and verified identity.

Runtime membership summaries use the Gateway pairing fingerprint: SHA-256 of the canonical, trimmed Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM, encoded as unpadded base64url with `SHA256:`.

Existing registrations, Gateway member and Cloud binding authority remain in their respective stores.

## Explicit default and one-time opening
The existing main Open button uses the saved default. Implicit defaults use stable registration / first-observation order, never probe completion order or a newly rebuilt Gateway catalog timestamp.

[Gateway access sessions](../gateway/gateway-access-sessions.md) owns transport isolation and same-route session reuse.

## Membership discovery and migration
Members are discovered from the signed v6 directory and matched to trusted Runtime membership summaries.

Existing Cloud-only Runtime configurations must rejoin and cannot silently gain the new member delegation. [Gateway Cloud access](../gateway/gateway-cloud-access.md) owns proof-based preservation of a formal environment ID.

Settings, progress, recovery and titles use Environment, environment window or Redeven. Env App is internal, never a label or brand. All shipped catalogs explicitly translate this copy.

Center visible content within the primary button, excluding the menu toggle. Idle text reserves no icon space. Submission shows a loader/shimmer, exposes busy state and blocks repeat clicks; completion restores centered text. Keep geometry fixed and meaningful icons grouped with labels.

Linked cards place Runtime, Redeven Cloud and paired Gateway tabs in the standalone badge slot. Cloud authorization or sync failure never disables Runtime actions. [Center navigation](desktop-welcome-navigation.md) transitions preserve card layout and do not restart on snapshots.

A bundled original-color OS mark beside the Runtime name reflects trusted platform data. Unknown platforms use a device mark; recognized Linux distributions use brand marks, otherwise Tux. Keep the slot fixed.

frontmatter.title: Desktop interaction continuity

concepts.summary: Desktop Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher and Runtime own business facts and execution progress. Background observations must preserve an open dialog or popup, its draft, selection, step, details, focus, native text selection and scroll. Only explicit opening, closing, switching, handoff or the current operation's completion changes visibility. Invalid authority preserves the visible session and input, blocks stale submission and offers verification or an accessible exit. Closing progress does not cancel its task.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and observations
Each interaction field has one owner: the existing library overlay, guidance, lifecycle disclosure, Gateway foreground action or settings opening. Retained cards supply presentation only; submission reads current authoritative data.

Addresses no longer shareable still lose QR disclosure under the connection-security contract.

Before the first asynchronous submission, one synchronous transition records the attempt, closes its menu and opens its operation surface. Duplicate activation cannot submit twice.

Deferred initial focus never overrides a user-selected menu item.

The interaction-continuity package command runs required state and real component suites, including the production snapshot subscription and observer. The cached commit group runs affected staged sources; bounded integration checks affected base-to-tip paths.

Synthetic composition verifies DOM continuity; it does not prove physical operating-system IME behavior.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:

Published presence and overlay ownership provide one exit and input-routing lifecycle.

Failure, permission loss, cancellation failure and missing progress retain an exit or recovery action. Closing never infers cancellation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership
Keys combine host authority, exact container engine/id and normalized Runtime root. Native Local keys use the actual canonical state directory, resolving symlinks without equating parent and child. [Scoped Runtime operations](../ai/tessiven-runtime-operations.md) recheck source/target authority before this coordinator admits a handoff.

## Execution
- Start reuses one verified healthy Runtime. Stop succeeds on empty inventory and verifies termination.
- Restart stops the observed Runtime, starts the installed binary and verifies readiness.
- Update prepares/verifies its package before modification, starts even a previously stopped Runtime and verifies it.
- Refresh observes directly without mutation. Reinstall follows [its recovery contract](desktop-reinstall-operations.md).

The current binary supplies temporary exact inventory and best-effort stop. Builds, downloads, archive preparation, upload and extraction belong to package progress, never process discovery. Desktop exit/update retires WSL Bridges without stopping WSL Runtime.

## Actions
Direct targets retain lifecycle and Provider Connect/Disconnect actions in every diagnosis. Conflicting actions stay visible but disabled, naming the active operation. Access-only targets offer Open/Connect/refresh-access without lifecycle or management fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Direct readiness
Native Local Environment is available on macOS/Linux; Windows uses registered WSL Environments. A newly published listener without final status remains pending within the startup deadline. Desktop update warns that Desktop and Local Runtime restart and interrupt Local sessions; Later changes nothing.

WSL, SSH and container observations use the saved channel. Unknown/failed health offers Refresh with its real diagnostic. Pending refresh retains prior diagnosis/startup age but withdraws live Presence; completion replaces it. Main retains credential-free `observed_runtime_control_status` until probe failure or management-configuration change. Gateway failure affects only that route.

A completed probe preserves missing-control diagnostics even when it publishes no Presence. Unknown or unauthenticated status must not become an observed stopped Runtime. Missing diagnostics may guide recovery but never grant live management capability; only current Presence can do so.

Direct lifecycle actions remain available in every diagnosis. Failed nested recovery names the actual operation and retains structured diagnostics; raw stderr appears only in technical details.

## Access and Flower
[Verified access routes](desktop-environment-access.md) owns association/defaults. Gateway directory presence, membership and application probing are distinct; failure never changes routes or starts Runtime recovery.

[Runtime Flower access](../../desktop/src/shared/runtimeFlowerAccess.ts) checks actual protocol/epoch for commands, subscriptions, frames and attachments. Desktop restart does not prove Runtime changed. Welcome admits Flower only with compatible openable Runtime and AI `ready`/`degraded`; transitional states show preparation with a return action, while missing/blocked/unavailable facts cannot admit requests.

concepts.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
concepts.description: Direct SSH and SSH-container Runtime lifecycle execution owned by Desktop.

frontmatter.description: Direct SSH and SSH-container Runtime lifecycle execution owned by Desktop.
frontmatter.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations

concepts.summary: Desktop manages SSH-host and SSH-container Runtime only through the saved connection and placement. One process-local lifecycle coordinator, Launcher Operation, transport lease and temporary helper serve Start, Stop, Restart, Update, Refresh, Open recovery and Reinstall. Gateway/Provider credentials never substitute for SSH authority. The target stores no Desktop lifecycle lock or supervisor state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Transport/authentication

Keys bind normalized destination/port, authentication, SSH executable and credential scope. Preserve failures without substitution/replay. macOS/Linux reuse ControlMaster; Windows uses bounded native OpenSSH and one persistent child per private Bridge, no WSL/ControlMaster. Cancel/dispose only owned children.

Omitted passwords reuse exact-scope private credentials, never clear them. Explicit changes reject during leases; no cross-scope inheritance. Without passwords, attempt configured keys/agent in batch mode even for password-mode registration; never send empty retries. Explicit connection allows this; passive status may defer. Password presence grants no authority. Start/Restart/Update carry transient credentials through certificate/access preflight, preparation and verification without saving. Observations reject passwords.

Normalized Connect Timeout bounds connection/probe/inventory/readiness; package/startup keep separate deadlines. Packaged Windows x64 askpass accepts password/passphrase, rejects host-key prompts, emits only private stdout and retains OpenSSH trust. Missing helper fails; secrets never enter argv/files/logs. Bounded SSH includes omit wildcard/negated picker aliases; explicit destinations remain valid. Save exact root/container engine+ID separately from display name.

## Preparation/execution

One operation reuses transport, probes platform once and prepares a small helper only for inventory/stop. Start/Stop never build full packages. Update verifies before mutation; build/download/upload remain visible. Clean builds use published dependencies and install Desktop dependencies before Env App assets.

Archives: ≤256 MiB compressed/512 MiB expanded tar stream including Runtime, Computer and signed plugins. Enforce while decoding before target writes; parse inventory once. Upload uses bounded writes/progress deadline; progressing transfer may exceed command timeout, which resumes after final write. Stall/cancel/loss terminates owned command; pipe progress is not receipt. Credential prompts have no upload deadline.

Shared private slot metadata across upload/install/container/reinstall: runtime, managed, bin and both executables0700; stamp/evidence0600 regardless of umask. Normalization failure preserves live slot; ReDevPlugin owns executable admission.

Host actions use confirmed user/root; container actions inspect exact saved container. Start/Restart/Update/Reinstall may start it; Stop cannot and accepts empty Runtime inventory. Signal verified scope matches only; retain typed before/after. Wipe-reinstall may treat helper inventory/stop as best effort only when direct access can isolate root.

Remote snippets perform one bounded probe/stage/inventory/stop/install/start/verify/isolate/cleanup. Desktop owns ordering/deadlines/cancellation/progress/retry; no remote lock, heartbeat or lifecycle machine.

## Progress/failures

Bootstrap uses generated signed https://github.com/floegence/redeven/releases/latest/download/redeven-install.sh with selected tag; Portal supplies no second installer. One Launcher Operation owns transfers: local upload writes, acquired response bytes with known size, shared acquisition progress. Direct downloads consume complete Downloading Redeven: N% records; stderr is diagnostics, stdout only staged path. Companion output cannot reset Runtime progress.

No extra download/parser process/SSH poll. Transfer100% is not verified install/readiness. Failure/cancel freezes measured progress. Acquisition/directory/upload/unpack are preparation; only activation mutates live slot. Operation exists before first SSH command. Distinguish connection, engine/container, preparation, command and readiness failures with technical stderr. Empty successful startup-report means pending to deadline; nonzero read is command failure, valid blocked report Runtime failure, only nonempty malformed report invalid. Every lifecycle path uses this interpretation.

sections.body: SSH registrations retain direct lifecycle menus. Gateway/Provider-only entries cannot borrow them. Never signal unrelated processes, substitute similar containers, delete home directories or prune containers globally. Multiple Desktop processes managing one target are unsupported and do not justify target-side coordination.

frontmatter.title: Desktop transport recovery

concepts.summary: Each Desktop placement bridge owns one HTTP/2 session, an immutable-generation recovery snapshot, and one exact registry identity. Recovery replaces the stdio exec and HTTP/2 session once through that owner, validates process and Runtime identity, rejects stale callbacks, and disposes transport and model resources through one terminal settlement path. Health observers and individual streams cannot independently recreate the bridge lifecycle.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Recovery presentation
Recovery uses an unboxed layout within the existing shell, with generous whitespace, semantic theme colors, standard buttons, and fine separators around the authoritative countdown or active phase.

A 30-second stalled-app timeout shows an actionable failure instead of an endless loading surface.

## Mechanism
Each established bridge owns one immutable transport-recovery snapshot with a monotonic `generation` and `revision`, the real `waiting`, `connecting`, `paused`, `ready`, or `failed` phase, completed attempt count, known retry and recovery timestamps, a structured failure, and explicitly allowed actions.

Lifecycle generation fencing cancels matching Opens so a late response cannot recreate the old session.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Transport recovery IPC is a narrow current-session capability. The separate Desktop Restart handoff exposes only the current window's bounded user-authored state to its fresh session, never ports, tokens, other Environment snapshots, Runtime handles, or launcher operations. Terminal transport failure may preserve the renderer window for diagnosis and navigation, but every previously loaded Runtime surface remains non-interactive until a fresh session is explicitly opened.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and registration
The main process publishes one immutable platform-capability snapshot. Renderer surfaces consume it and never infer the host operating system.

UI recovery copy may show Microsoft WSL commands for the user to run.

## Linux Runtime lifecycle
WSL and SSH host operations consume the same managed-Linux probe, uploaded install, atomic activation, startup report, inventory, exact stop, and verification scripts.

Runtime installs under the Linux user's home-backed `~/.redeven`, never under `/mnt`, and does not require `systemd`.

Only the Environment Stop action stops it.

## Private Bridge and failure behavior
`desktop-bridge` remains a foreground `wsl.exe` child carrying the shared `redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1` HTTP/2 session over private standard input and output.

Multiple registered distributions have independent target ids, processes, Bridges, update state, and lifecycle coordinator keys.

## Package and update boundary
The Windows Desktop bundle uses `managed_wsl_archive` and contains one verified `redeven_linux_amd64.tar.gz`; it must not contain or execute `redeven.exe`.

Public Windows assets remain forbidden until Authenticode signing, signed NSIS update metadata, signing receipts, and a real signed n-1 to n update are enabled together.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Windows and WSL 2 remain separate authorities. No boundary may be hidden by a native Windows Runtime, SSH-shaped WSL compatibility path, public port, localhost-forwarding dependency, system service, or second lifecycle state machine.

The first-party host-application bootstrap places its controls in one 40-pixel Desktop titlebar, alongside platform-owned traffic lights or caption buttons. Empty header space drags the window when no toolbar popover is open; buttons and popovers explicitly reject dragging.

The control is unavailable until its selected target has decoded pixels.

## Appearance and language
The bootstrap consumes published Floe `standalone.css`: primitive sizing and fonts, all 26 shell presets, shared floating material and input focus rules. Local CSS owns only viewer layout and maps control states to upstream semantic tokens; it must not maintain a second light/dark palette.

The inline assets add no request or connection wait.

## Backend commands
The shared toolbar and picture-preset presentation do not own backend state. macOS retains native menu, window-generation, frame credit and capture-quality semantics.

It never sends server shutdown or force-kills the application. macOS quit retains its existing application-wide confirmation. These distinct actions must not be collapsed into one destructive command.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reverse application streams
After local consent, Runtime redeems its invitation with its own identity and initiates a persistent Flowersec session to the member TLS endpoint. Gateway opens a reverse ByteStream on that Runtime's connection and relays both streams with bounded buffers and cancellation.

TLS, WebSocket, streaming responses and secure cookies retain their original semantics.

## Application and management separation
A reverse stream enters the original public Runtime handler. It never acquires a trusted Desktop management marker.

The catalog alone does not authorize service or Runtime process operations.

## Limits and revocation
The shared budget admits at most 32 business connections per member and 1,024 in total, including pending opens. One member exceeding a limit cannot consume another member's allocation.

Cloud closure receipts and partition limits are owned by [Gateway Cloud access](gateway-cloud-access.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Host administration
Local, SSH, local-container and SSH-container connections acquire management only after actually reaching the target Gateway and verifying its private host credential. It never exposes the credential to Renderer, URL connections, Runtime channels or logs.

Removing a Desktop connection does not stop or delete the Gateway service.

## URL enrollment and reconnection
Administrators create client access codes through POST `/gateway/v6/clients/access-codes` or `redeven-gateway clients access-code`. An identical completion retry returns the original result after response loss; other clients cannot consume that code.

A client access code neither enrolls a Runtime nor grants Gateway administration.

## Client visibility and revocation
Host administrators list clients through POST `/gateway/v6/clients/list` or `redeven-gateway clients list`. The display name is a recognition label, never identity evidence.

Revocation survives restart.

## State and compatibility
Trust schema 3 retains Gateway and client keys, preserves previously allowed environment access and removes legacy management grants. A handshake mismatch requests a Gateway/Desktop update, not identity replacement or state reinstallation.

Joining a Gateway establishes local membership only. A directory cannot obtain Runtime credentials.

Namespace authorization, local egress permission and batch-enrollment delegation are separate decisions.

Runtime control registration, independent recovery, data transport and enabled official-platform requests use the explicitly selected route. Gateway outages and denied egress never trigger a direct Internet fallback or global proxy environment variables.

Ownership changes require separate authorization.

## One recovery owner
Registration, heartbeat and credential replenishment share one connection controller and independent credential source.

Unknown results resume that operation.

Each route operation can be queried after an unknown result; cancellation reports a committed operation truthfully.

## Management notifications and closure
Each Gateway has one authenticated HTTPS notification owner. Reconnection starts with an authoritative snapshot.

No short data lease is introduced during ordinary control outages.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Enrollment owner

Creation offers Not now or After setup, add Gateway access before inspection/startup. Connect before verification/consent; an earlier Env App open proves no live connection. Creation and cards share one app-owned enrollment session, never separate dialogs/auth/recovery owners. Settings suspends it; closure restores its initiating control.

Each opening owns a sender/target-bound lease on the exact Env App bridge. Env App closure cannot release it; cancel, renderer navigation/destruction and authority changes do. Reject late requests, but retain admitted-write transport through settlement. Connection may instead try the saved management channel with available SSH/OpenSSH authentication. Passive auth_required or absent saved password cannot preempt that attempt. Only current authentication failure exposes the focused inline Enter-submittable password and stops credential-free retries. Distinguish auth, Gateway and container-engine failures.

Only scoped enrollment status accepts a temporary password; verification/consent never do. It overrides connection credentials without saving preferences; clear renderer secrets after connection/failure/closure. Reopening gets a fresh scope and authentication attempt. Proven stopped Runtime/container shows explicit Start. Start/restart/update use the existing lifecycle owner/dispatch, try available auth first, and request temporary credentials only for typed SSH failure. Carry credentials unchanged through execution/access verification; never persist, clear after settlement. Startup observations cannot interrupt their owning action or race clearing. Recovery revokes consent before reconnecting. Opening/connecting never implicitly starts Runtime.

Connection loss stops submission/polling; explicit recovery retains drafts. Loss/authority change requires fresh verification. Observations cannot cancel pending actions. Settings suspends the connection and invalidates verification, retaining step/code drafts; return reconnects before submission. Internal checks use inline feedback, not refreshed toasts. Unknown status never means rejected credentials; details retain the diagnosis.

## Gateway choice and invitations

Saved/manual tabs retain independent drafts/input nodes. Selection keys an enabled saved registration ID across URL, local/SSH and container kinds, never address/connectivity. Keep endpoint-less registrations with inline setup. Prefer confirmed member_endpoints; URL registrations may use canonical HTTPS origin if catalog endpoints are absent. Never derive endpoints from SSH/listener coordinates. Reject revoked/changed trust, invalid or Host-rejected origins and remote loopback without hiding eligible registrations. Late inventory preserves typing/focus; removal of a selected usable address revokes verification.

For managed Gateways with manage_members, the same owner saves addresses via update_gateway_endpoints, preserving endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions. Hold authoritative IPC endpoints only until catalog change; never resurrect removals. Explicit invite_gateway_runtime or pasted codes are required; saving/selection/issuance does not enroll. URL/access-only users get administrator address/code guidance. Authority changes, closure and suspension reject late responses while observations retain pending actions. Runtime verification/explicit consent are mandatory. Success consumes code; reopening clears code/consent.

Accepted enrollment shows a result; membership differs from connectivity. Unknown submission queries exact Gateway membership and never resubmits its invitation. Positive status completes; authoritative absence clears consumed/uncertain material and returns to verification. Ordinary checks consume no invitation. Done returns to origin.

## Welcome and task continuity

Retain toolbar, horizontal Environment/Redeven Cloud/Gateway navigation, search/filter and bottom bar. Cards use a responsive grid, compact wide columns and one narrow column. Name/Manage opens an in-shell page: Overview, Clients, Runtimes, Network, Redeven Cloud, Service maintenance; no separate Desktop connection section. Title-row back arrow has localized All Gateways name/tooltip and restores query/position/focus. Reopen retains drafts; global navigation suspends existing task/page owners.

Card header groups identity/management; equal-width full-row Connect client/Runtime actions stay together in narrow locales. Footer holds observed status with refresh/recovery. Manage/More share Floe small-control height/centerline and expand touch targets together. Access-only cards omit enrollment. Align overview values and member names/status. Shared Dropdown contains local Edit, Enable/Disable and Remove only; bounded edit Dialog and removal confirmation explain local-only scope (no remote revocation/service stop). Clients/Cloud initialize independently. URL connections never inherit stale administration. One mounted action owner survives filtering; no hidden maintenance card.

Creation first chooses existing service or new deployment, with distinct URL-pairing/host-container transport. Save returns exact registration ID and opens its overview/status/next action; saving establishes neither deployment nor connectivity. Start stays explicit.

Connect Runtime distinguishes Desktop-managed versus another administrator. Managed choice and Environment Add Gateway access share the app enrollment session with corresponding object preselected. Other-admin choice opens the existing invitation issuer in a bounded task dialog; missing addresses link to the network editor. Picker includes stopped/unopened environments. No nested member enrollment or second issuer. Wait for outgoing modal presence before transition, preserving draft/return context. Hiding retains draft/admitted work; existing card actions resume it, without a global banner. Resume reacquires management and revokes old consent, never reuses released leases.

## Management presentation

Use quiet Floe content, compact sidebar, wrapped navigation below 768 px. Only active sections affect Welcome scroll extent; visited sections remain mounted for drafts/codes/progress. Enrollment/edit/service tasks use published Dialogs over the page, without competing nested overlays. Keyboard dismissal/transitions restore origin. Ready empty cards show count without a banner. Semantic tokens, shared controls and explicit catalogs follow floe-webapp.

Readiness uses observed service and verified protocol, not Desktop build equality. Refresh/pairing/invitations reuse compatible installed Gateways. Repair never invents start-required; pairing rejection cannot become update-required from release/commit differences. [Service](gateway-service.md) owns compatibility/integrity.

Runtimes owns membership, per-member Cloud overrides, recheck/removal; global policy belongs to Redeven Cloud. Clients exclusively owns listing/confirmed revocation. Client enrollment prepares editable HTTPS address; only explicit issuance creates a code. Show code/expiry/address with separate/combined copy, retaining draft/code on return. Endpoint observations cannot overwrite addresses. Member/publication/endpoint choices use shared Dropdown. Refresh failure retains lists/invitations; cancellation cannot reopen or discard drafts. Settings/code import grants no Runtime/Namespace authority. [Network settings](gateway-network-settings.md) owns endpoints/listeners/collapsed restrictions and validation/restart.

Panels are viewport-bounded with explicit translations. Shared field-surface Dropdown owns keyboard/focus; focus changes the existing border, not an outer frame. No native select/parallel menu. All catalogs provide HTTPS hostname:port, listener and Host examples; invitation timers use plural rules. Localized member recovery leaves raw/future codes in collapsed details; policy feedback pairs action labels with hook IDs.

Service/card actions share foreground owner, admission and progress. A bounded service Dialog also handles network restart; closing cannot reopen popovers or redispatch. Confirmation shows action/target/affected sessions, no diagnostic inventory, with title-row close. Admission replaces controls with pending until authoritative progress; no duplicate request.

Show observed steps, current state and elapsed time; invent no future stages/percentages. Raw details stay collapsed after timeline; failure keeps concise recovery separately. Stable trigger/close hide the panel and restore focus without stopping work. Reopen retains steps/timing. After reconnect, adopt an existing running operation before offering new confirmation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Membership authority
An administrator verified through the Gateway host creates a ten-minute, single-use invitation code and shares an administrator-confirmed Gateway address. Gateway never obtains Runtime Cloud credentials from its directory.

Desktop display association uses the trusted Runtime management membership summary and the paired Gateway key; public health proof remains a separate observation and grants no authority.

## Policy and executable hooks
New installations deny Cloud by default.

Programs use an absolute executable and argument array, never a shell. Desktop member management and `redeven-gateway members reevaluate --member ID --version N` check the current member version before applying the same reevaluation.

## Own-process management
The separate Gateway archive and state root contain no Runtime lifecycle data. Saving, refresh, pairing or member management never starts a stopped service implicitly.

Cancellation still stops development startup and exact owned-process cleanup remains required.

## Compatibility and updates

Gateway release tags and source commits are diagnostics, not admission gates. Desktop validates the installed binary against its own installation stamp, then observes service readiness and the actual Gateway wire/authority contract. An unrelated Desktop or Runtime release never forces Gateway replacement. Start/restart reuse an intact installed package; explicit Update validates the staged archive against the selected release and commit before activation. Package corruption, stopped service, pairing failure and protocol incompatibility remain distinct diagnoses; authorization rejection never implies an outdated build.

Gateway v6 owns its authority epoch independently of Runtime Service. The existing value 69 is preserved so deployed services remain compatible; change it only for a reviewed Gateway authority break. Runtime metadata versions do not gate membership. Preserve signed identity, consent, permissions, freshness and current protocol validation; best-effort compatibility does not accept unknown security contracts. A feature failure affects that operation, not unrelated members or Runtime lifecycle authority.

## Address changes and upgrade
[Gateway network settings](gateway-network-settings.md) owns atomic network configuration, next-start listener changes, request Host admission and its persistent migration boundary.

If all fail, the membership stays intact and reports Gateway unavailable.

Optional Cloud publishing remains a separate flow.

frontmatter.title: Flower explicit long-thread qualification

concepts.summary:
Long conversations must preserve complete content and responsive interaction while
work continues. This is a required product property, not optional release tuning.
The long-thread suite runs explicitly for acceptance or targeted investigation.
It is not registered in unified commit, integration or CI gates, and is not a
prerequisite for each commit. Keep the independent suite and fixed budgets available
without adding its setup and sustained measurement cost to ordinary development.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Explicit execution and provenance

Run node scripts/check_flower_long_thread.mjs --fast for focused regressions,
or omit --fast for browser correctness and the sustained real-runtime scenario.
Install frozen published Desktop and Env App dependencies before testing. A visible
composited Electron environment is required; unavailable prerequisites are failures,
not skips. Unified gate manifests and entrypoints must not invoke this suite.

Retain the tested source commit/tree, clean status, toolchain, dependency hashes,
metrics and supervised cleanup evidence. Product or dependency changes invalidate
their earlier performance result. A later policy-only change may cite that result
only with an explicit unchanged-product comparison and separate policy tests; never
label the unmeasured final commit as performance-tested.

Nonzero exits, absent tests/tools, interrupted runs, missing metrics and cleanup
failures fail the explicit acceptance. Negative tests retain the observed 110 ms
presented-latency / 21 position-commits-per-second regression. A lightweight runner
test verifies ordinary profiles exclude this qualification. A failed run is evidence
of failure, never a waived pass. No workload/threshold overrides are accepted.

## Correctness

Fast suites protect indexed record stability, ordered live queue semantics,
retention/reading windows, turn/disclosure identity, per-block content-boundary invalidation, keyed subscription disposal, local thinking
updates, structural versus mutable field dependencies, sealed-body handoff and incremental Markdown.
Tool sequence classification has one mounted owner per entry: retained rows reuse
classified facts while live state, pending bodies, preview labels and the first
non-whitespace prose boundary remain reactive. Removed entries dispose their owners.
Title arrivals classify identities once per mounted entry and inspect visibility
only when admitted and claimed. Group/disclosure changes cannot rescan completed
title bodies; restored and reconnected titles remain static. Fast regressions
exercise 600 retained rows, and browser cases protect genuine arrival motion.
Stable tool groups own their disclosure observer. Tail growth and title motion
publish only changed group blockers; removed groups dispose their pending
observations. A 600-group regression rejects repeated historical fold checks.
Body chunks extend an already admitted item and never advance whole-timeline
restoration provenance. This preserves fresh title motion and prevents body/live
receipts from repeatedly observing every historical group. Full item hydration
retains its restoration boundary. Browser regressions cover root and child views.
Body receipts request synchronous anchor correction only when loading becomes
complete; growing byte extents of already retained content do not force layout.
Structural batches publish ordered membership once after every affected record is
ready; replacing many records must not rescan the full document for each record.
Parent-event reading intervals track membership and coverage independently of
cache-wide text updates; immutable turn facts do not allocate per-field subscriptions.
Browser suites additionally exercise history navigation, reconnect, selection,
disclosure ownership, input/approval and terminal states. The sustained scenario
creates 500 real canonical turns through the product Service and the published
Floret runtime with deterministic fake providers: 1,000 messages and 1,000 completed
tools, verified completely after admission. It does not use a real provider, user
state, raw database editing or product runtime fallbacks.

Generate mixed text, reasoning, Markdown and a tool every 60 provider updates at
80 updates/second, including a 32 KiB initial body. Preserve the actual workload
rate independently of UI responsiveness. Accumulate at least 120 seconds in one
active turn before late samples. After stopping, compare every generated prose
and reasoning item through real history/disclosure controls with canonical content
and full Markdown parsing, including exact code blocks. Draft, focus and selection
must survive drag. Browser regression suites retain the remaining interaction
contracts; the synthetic floating output is not a terminal emulator qualification.
Content inspection waits for the observed terminal state, enters reading mode,
and reveals measured history sections before operating their descendants. It
must not force clicks through hidden content or mutate product disclosure state.

## Responsiveness

Sample idle, early work, late work and a repeat on the same visible production UI
with two production PersistentFloatingWindows. Each sample lasts at least twelve
seconds measured with a monotonic clock. Pointer cancellation, released buttons,
window blur or a hidden document invalidates the sample. The visible test-only
Electron host ignores physical mouse events so normal desktop pointer motion
cannot cancel the independently injected CDP drag. Input handlers, compositor
presentation and every interruption check remain active. Read the runtime counter
before pressing, then use one CDP session for press, continuous movement and
release so no backend request pauses input establishment. Chromium timestamps
input on its own monotonic clock; injecting Node wall time can place the input
after its renderer processing and corrupt presentation spans. Independent 60 Hz CDP
input scheduling must offer at least 55 events/second;
awaiting every dispatch in the producer is prohibited. Require at least 45 actual
position commits/second and 80% of idle cadence, not merely low latency among the
few events the renderer happens to deliver.

Require presented drag latency P95 <=75 ms, a work-versus-idle penalty <=25 ms,
at least 95% of live prose markers observed with P95 <=250 ms,
frame interval P95 <=25 ms, live reactive apply P95 <=12 ms/max <=50 ms, and no
main-thread task >=100 ms. These are initial product acceptance budgets, not claims
that the current implementation passes or that CDP measures physical mouse-to-photon.
Do not relax them just to admit the known long-active-turn regression.

Chromium trace analysis pairs nested async slices by process, identity and scope.
Only completed MOUSE_DRAGGED spans with a compositor presentation stage enter the
presentation quantile; coalesced/nonpresented spans remain separately counted.
Require at least 30 presented samples/second. A healthy rAF average alone cannot
certify pointer responsiveness. No CPU profiling or screencast runs during timing.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The desktop test supervisor owns the fixture, build, Electron, profile/state
directories and ports, and verifies cleanup before reporting success. Synthetic
metrics/traces remain outside Git. The report records source, lock hashes and host;
standalone dirty development measurements do not certify an exact committed tip.
Historical seeding verifies the full canonical result once instead of rescanning
the complete prefix after each admission; this changes setup cost, not coverage.

Optimization must reduce the synchronous work per envelope: stable per-turn and
per-row inputs, keyed mounted subscriptions, linear membership checks, and bounded
offscreen layout with reading/selection/focus pins. Layout sections retain their
DOM and disclosure owners; this is layout containment, not DOM virtualization.
Skipping offscreen layout must also cover a growing active turn. Preserve canonical order and semantic boundaries,
full history access, drafts and disclosure state. Throttling, suppressed output,
a second lifecycle, or shortened fixtures cannot substitute for those invariants.
Shared floating-window mechanics belong to Floe; product projection belongs here.
Floe's published progress shimmer pauses only its decorative paint while its shared
drag/resize marker is active, preserving animation identity and phase on release.
Progress text, token counts, streamed content and terminal state remain live. Browser
regressions cover native release, pointer cancellation and window blur, including
preserved preview drafts and selection. The acceptance workload and latency budgets
remain unchanged; disabling streaming or masking failure cannot satisfy this rule.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Run `scripts/check_flower_tasks_ollama.sh` explicitly; `--interleavings` selects
combined operation cases. Every request uses the selected installed model, with
real chosen tools and exact Ollama Chat history. Observe actual effects and canonical
state; retain failure without simulation or automatic reruns.

| Scenario | Required observable result |
| --- | --- |
| Data/file task | Read structured data, compute sum, write/verify, modify in a later turn |
| Stop generation | Prompt acceptance, cancelled terminal state, no failure retry of cancellation, later task accepted |
| Stop terminal | Preserve confirmed initial effect, kill owned process, prevent delayed write, accept later task |
| Queue edits | Optimistic text match, stale edit rejection, reorder/delete and exact execution/user-text order |
| Send now | Cancel active provider request and execute selected queued task |
| Concurrent duplicate input | One retained task; conflicting content for same key rejected across stop/restart/promotion |
| Stop/restart at generation, approval or Ask User | Original stop identity, stale response rejection and exactly-once retained queue promotion |
| Queue edits during approval | Stop/restart before promotion; late approval cannot execute cancelled tool |
| Duplicate approvals | Same answer replays before/after restart, conflicting answer rejects, one actual effect |
| Cancel Ask User | Replacement input runs after restart; stale answer cannot revive task |
| Two interrupted continuations | Concurrent Retry/queued input retain original write exactly once |
| Duplicate send-now | Consumed items reject edits; restart replay does not reexecute |
| Permission/model change | Queued permission changes, active model-change rejection and immutable existing approval snapshot |
| Repeated permission transitions | Readonly/approval, stop/restart, stale/fresh approval, post-effect failure, downgrade/retry and restored full-access effects |

Tests own isolated state, services and tools. Remove temporary stores/files after
each case while retaining reports; source configuration and credentials stay unchanged.

sections.title: Contract

Floret owns canonical request preparation; Redeven consumes the published runtime
without sibling replacements or a second cache. No cadence reduction, dropped output,
history deletion or durable ledger is permitted. [Storage ownership](../ai/flower-storage-ownership-and-migrations.md)
and [streaming interaction](../ui/flower-streaming-stability.md) remain normative.

## Method and reproduction

Real Service/SQLite and production Electron use fake providers, 100 completed turns
(200 requests), 16,384-byte system prompt, mixed Markdown/Unicode/reasoning, tool
boundaries every 40 updates and 40 Hz output. Each fresh fixture warms ten seconds
and measures 120 seconds before exact canonical/rendered prose, reasoning and code
checks. Apple M5 Pro (18 cores/64 GiB), macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, Node 26.7.0; CPU is
cumulative process time (100% = one core), combined includes all fixture Electron
processes, and allocations are cumulative bytes rather than retained heap.

The historical comparison retains its seed prompt scope. An ordinary fork creates
a new scope and cannot reproduce request-history amplification. Leave that override
unset for concurrency/lifecycle scenarios.

```sh
GOWORK=off go test -c ./internal/ai -o /tmp/flower-cpu-fixture.test
node scripts/qualify_flower_cpu.mjs --build --dist=<isolated-ui-directory>
REDEVEN_CPU_QUALIFICATION=1 REDEVEN_CPU_HISTORY_TURNS=100 \
REDEVEN_CPU_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BYTES=16384 REDEVEN_CPU_TOOL_EVERY=40 \
REDEVEN_CPU_RETAIN_SEED_SCOPE=1 REDEVEN_CPU_STATE=<fresh-empty-directory> \
REDEVEN_CPU_DIST=<isolated-ui-directory> \
/tmp/flower-cpu-fixture.test -test.run '^TestFlowerCPUQualification$' -test.timeout=45m
node scripts/qualify_flower_cpu.mjs --fixture=<state>/fixture.json \
  --seconds=120 --warmup=10 --threads=1 --hz=40 --stop-samples=3 --output=<sample>.json
```

Keep the fixture alive for connection, stop it via its quit operation and verify
owned cleanup. Retain raw samples/failures and binary/UI/source hashes locally;
match reference UI and qualifier revisions because thinking selectors changed in
`7d649a3b6`. Never touch the user's running Flower.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Use the same machine, published dependencies, synthetic data and build mode.
Point-read scaling requires ≥70% short-target P95 reduction; warm synchronous P95
is <8 ms and visible feedback precedes commit. Keep raw source identities/results
locally; never commit user databases/credentials or continue real tasks.

Root detail uses Floret window subscriptions. GET/PATCH and root observation share
public projection; send acknowledgments carry exact identities without a current
view. Child reads own an independent bounded interest.
Initial windows and explicit body requests bound transport, excluding metadata and
pending controls. Cold send admission reads bounded current facts but still scans
historical metadata; complete execution preparation follows admission. Explicitly
expanded activities use selected values and bounded field ranges. Backend read and loopback/render timings are
separate measurements, never additive.

```sh
GOWORK=off go test ./internal/ai -count=1 -timeout=15m
GOWORK=off go test ./internal/ai -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkFlowerThreadDetailPointRead -benchtime=1x -count=1 -timeout=10m
python3 scripts/check_flower_storage_compatibility.py
```

Run focused `TestFlowerHistory`, ThreadCache/runtime record tests, history/streaming/
tool-sequence browser suites, both host typechecks and locale validation. Synthetic
and released-writer qualification stays outside ordinary CI/hooks. Private baseline
frames must validate before shared-frame assertions; do not discard arbitrary frames.

Deep-scroll qualification must cross the product HTTP decoder.
`TestServerFlowerHistoryScrollQualification` serves only an owned isolated copy with
execution deferred. `qualify_flower_thread_open.mjs --history-scroll-steps=80` checks
both directions, canonical progress, successful membership requests above 8 KiB,
and idle request stability after each ten gestures. The service-only fixture cannot
qualify HTTP request-size limits. Never commit its raw history or database.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:

The live capture checks below used Runtime source `5b4e303718adcb5e1b7e244dd306ab8043d2ad9d`, `GOWORK=off`, and no sibling module or package overlays.

A 4,194,321-byte payload matches byte for byte; a payload larger than 32 MiB closes its stream and never reaches the upstream.

The prepared Xpra 20/21 classes are covered upstream; this phase did not launch a retained Xpra host application on a physical host.

The launcher now names the actual Desktop connection or reported local hostname, keeps optional view/grant-reuse settings collapsed, omits a single-display selector, and separates status checking from connecting.

This verifies the launcher and locked-host boundary; the unlocked macOS limits above still apply.

sections.title: Contract

| Scenario | Required result and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Existing single-instance Mac app | Reuse exact process; lease release preserves it (native fixture) |
| First window after 40 seconds | Keep waiting, then reveal without relaunch (48-second fixture and Go watchdog) |
| Multiple windows | Counted picker with literal titles, retained selection/focus and direct switching (viewer/browser tests) |
| Close cancelled | Retain process/session and viewer (native cancellation fixture) |
| Unreadable/replaced surface | Uncertainty never expires into closure (Swift inventory/presence tests) |
| Linux dialog-only app | Reveal decoded dialog at native dimensions (Xpra adapter) |
| Final window actually closes | Close established physical viewer (native/viewer tests) |
| Last lease released | End sharing, retain newly launched app and all windows (multi-window fixture) |
| One stale quit selection | Reject whole selection before termination (native quit fixture) |
| App cancels quit | Keep process, pixels and sharing; permit another explicit request (cancellation/reconnect fixture) |
| Unknown quit result | Keep confirmation error; never infer exit or auto-retry (Env App test) |
| Read-only caller | May list running apps, never quit/detach (API/UI tests) |
| Network loss/reload | Keep app; suspend capture/input, reclaim buffers, reconnect same session/current credential (WebSocket/native/viewer tests) |
| Second viewer | Revoke previous input, release held keys, suspend old capture before successor resumes (WebSocket/native tests) |
| Permission loss/console lock | Invalidate capture/input and expose distinct recovery (Swift/viewer tests) |
| Helper exit | Sharing failure is not app exit; reclaim route, credential, buffers and helper before terminal state (Go/viewer tests) |
| Late callback/unknown terminal reason | Ignore stale results; retain terminal page without automatic physical closure (macOS/Xpra viewer tests) |
| Unproven foreground/window ownership | Nonblocking input failure, no replay into another app (native/viewer tests) |
| Missing video decoder | Negotiate same-process image transport (picture/viewer acceptance) |

320/390/1000 px, native-menu keyboard access, distinct window close/confirmed quit,

concepts.summary:
The [display contract](../architecture/host-application-display.md) owns picture
behavior. Floe Native Apps owns capture, encoding and region decoding; Redeven owns

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reproducible measurements
Compare baseline and candidate on the same host, browser version, source size and workload.

An SSH tunnel changes transport overhead and must be recorded.

| Metric | Definition and controlled viewer acceptance budget |
| --- | --- |
| Input to presented pixels | DOM key event through remote application to changed canvas pixels on the next animation frame; nearest-rank P95 of 20 samples below 150 ms in every mode |
| Input during motion | The same 20-sample measurement while document scroll continues; P95 below 250 ms, including Save data cadence |
| Presented FPS | At most one changed-canvas presentation per animation frame; Motion first at least 25 FPS during document scroll |
| Received payload | All incoming WebSocket data bytes, including JSON; excludes WebSocket/TLS/SSH framing and network retransmissions |
| Idle bandwidth | Below 0.25 Mb/s after settling; a fully unchanged document should send zero image bytes |
| Document-motion bandwidth | Below 5 Mb/s for Automatic/Clarity/Save data and 15 Mb/s for Motion first at the recorded source size |
| Decode work | No more than two current-target frames plus one retired decode; no reconnect on a picture change |
| First frame | Navigation to first decoded canvas presentation; excludes browser-process launch before the viewer attaches |

## Published-module product results
A sandboxed Chrome 153 client on Ubuntu passed all v0.21.0 viewer budgets over loopback, isolating capture, forwarding, decoding and presentation from networking:

| Application | Automatic Mb/s | Motion-first FPS | Static-input P95 across modes | Scrolling-input P95 across modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome | 2.14 | 27.0 | 46–65 ms | 129–237 ms |
| Firefox | 4.37 | 37.4 | 65–81 ms | 99–231 ms |

## Observed native pipeline improvement
Sequential tests on Ubuntu 26.04 amd64, Chrome 153.0.8010.36 (1292 by 753 pixels) and Firefox 155.0.1 (1000 by 700 pixels) compared the authentic v0.20.0 component with the v0.21.0 implementation.

| Workload | v0.20.0 | Automatic | Motion first | Save data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome scroll, Mb/s | 25.04 | 1.59 | 10.61 | 0.64 |
| Chrome scroll, FPS | 25.1 | 19.4 | 34.0 | 8.8 |
| Chrome input P95, ms | 59.6 | 52.8 | 49.9 | 81.3 |
| Firefox scroll, Mb/s | 30.64 | 2.20 | 6.53 | 0.59 |
| Firefox scroll, FPS | 32.4 | 28.7 | 37.4 | 7.9 |
| Firefox input P95, ms | 103.3 | 54.5 | 54.5 | 78.3 |

The historical Xpra matrix below covers userspace installations without a desktop environment or monitor. Container checks cannot certify a distribution's boot, kernel, SELinux/AppArmor, GPU, or login policies.

| Arch Linux x86_64 | Distribution Xpra 6.4.4, upstream HTML5 v20 | GIO and isolated X11 launch/resume/stop in the prepared userspace; complete Runtime and browser flow under the translation constraints below |

The disposable AppKit fixture verifies real bundle metadata/icons, direct launch, captured pixels, pointer input, Unicode text, native shortcuts, actual menu invocation, real AX resize, reconnect without a new process, stale input rejection, and application-window closure.

This covers the idle-helper replayd contention that single-application startup tests cannot detect; the [capture ownership contract](../architecture/macos-application-capture-owner.md) defines the required process and channel boundaries.

## Implementation And Distribution
Upstream commit `ec0d9cc8e64fd3e9e2020da017bec57a56ce0f94` replaces full-frame Python allocation and copying with a bounded Gst buffer pool.

These results certify the tested host-desktop component, not the whole optional application distribution.

## Correctness
Thirty-six focused Python tests pass, including existing damage, sequence, mapping and cursor rules.

- BGRA, BGRx, RGBA and RGBx; packed, padded and non-aligned source rows. - Separate cursor updates and embedded composition without corrupting retained clean pixels. - Bounded pool capacity, final-frame recovery, parent lease retention and interruptible shutdown. - Retained frame bytes after pool deactivation and idempotent capture close.

These checks retain the cursor, mode, reconnect and permission contracts; neither a debug workspace nor sibling source overlay is used.

## Performance Of The Final Implementation
The same udesk24 VM ran alternating old/new/old/new tests at 2560 by 1440 with software x264. The real private PipeWire producer emits a moving rectangle through MemFd at 60 FPS and never reads the user desktop.

| Old A2 | 46.86 | 19.96 ms | 29.94 / 52.37 ms |
| New B2 | 59.90 | 2.64 ms | 8.68 / 9.99 ms |

| Run | Paint confirmations per second | Capture entry to returned paint ACK, median / P95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Old A1 | 32.78 | 68.89 / 140.23 ms |
| New B1 | 60.07 | 24.19 / 25.36 ms |
| Old A2 | 26.19 | 99.17 / 144.48 ms |
| New B2 | 60.01 | 14.89 / 17.29 ms |

## Real Functional Evidence
| Interaction | Observed host or Viewer outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Picture | Physical GNOME panel and Clash Verge, then the fullscreen task GTK fixture, appear in the real Viewer. |
| Mouse | A real Viewer click increments the fixture's visible button counter and host event log. |
| Keyboard | Physical `a` press/release reaches GTK; twenty later presses add exactly twenty `a` characters to the host document. |
| Unicode and Enter | In **Use local input method**, CUA sets the real keyboard textarea once to submit an input event; GTK and Viewer show exact `abC中文😀$`, then physical Enter and `second` produce `abC中文😀$\nsecond`. This is assisted commit, not human IME composition acceptance. |
| Lock | Viewer **Lock host** locks GNOME; ordinary controls, clipboard and the editable keyboard surface become disabled. A later observation shows actual lock pixels; the initial black interval has no measured duration or established cause. |
| Physical unlock | **Start unlocking** and physical Enter expose the GNOME password box. One wrong submission keeps the host locked; the authorized correct physical password restores the desktop and `LockedHint=no`. A subsequent click and `x` change the fixture, proving restored input. |
| Shortcut | The first Alt+Tab submission lacked host-effect evidence. A later real shortcut switches from the GTK fixture to Clash Verge and back. Only the latter observations qualify window switching. |
| Fullscreen | The real Viewer enters Electron fullscreen; Escape restores native window controls while retaining the remote picture. |
| Explicit disconnect | Picture is removed, input and shortcut controls are disabled, and **Desktop disconnected** instructs the user to close and reconnect. Closing and reopening from Env App previously restored the picture. |
