sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Initialization

ThreadFactsSource.SubscribeFacts supplies account/workload/Computer/workspace facts without bodies or viewers. Root and child own independent authorized ThreadWindowSource interests. One worker coalesces ≤64 dirty parents without blocking the facts pump; [adapter ownership](../ai/floret-redeven-adapter-and-projection.md) applies.

Register observation before freezing authorized roots in navigation order. Release budgeted IDs/backing arrays as pages drain. Ready publishes observer identity, then ≤25-summary pages; only the last carries baseline_complete, followed by private read states. Accepted reading bypasses sidebar preparation; ordinary facts wait. Cancellation releases subscribers/queues without Next. Canonical failures invalidate observation; no arbitrary timeout or skipped pinned roots.

Merge pages immediately; prune only on completion, retaining selection/local creations. First page, confirmed empty inventory or accepted selected detail admits the surface; partial empty Ready does not. Explicit HTTP refresh uses cancellable 25-row pages, ten seconds per progressing page, retaining delivered pages on failure. Desktop cancels history/item POSTs. [Startup](../architecture/flower-startup-presentation.md) owns display.

## Windows and reading

Ready installs the current observer baseline before shared foreground loading. Covered responses coalesce demand; explicit command confirmation stays forced. Navigation/disposal/transport changes cancel obsolete waiters. Reconnect binds new-observer reads without losing content, scroll or drafts.

Root/child slots have independent monotonic revisions. Baselines/deltas share a subscription; page replacement fences older interest revisions. Limits:

| Read | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Initial | 50 items, 1 KiB text previews, Activity summaries, existing byte budget |
| Earlier/newer | 150 items, 512 KiB |
| Window POST | 64 KiB JSON, 150 identities |
| Body/item locator | 8 KiB |
| Exact membership | 448 KiB canonical previews, excluding hydrated bodies |

Selection charges max(transmitted bytes, original window_bytes). Receipts refresh the accepted interval, never force Latest. Network interest is independent of retained reading. Keep visited sealed owners/bodies on the confirmed path and mounted visible/focused/selected live islands; evict inactive documents whole. Gap reads stop at missing intervals; prefetch stays ahead of the reading edge. One coalesced input demand owns each handoff, including stationary-edge input. HTTP/layout completion cannot recursively walk collapsed history. Failed navigation retains drafts/content and localized Retry.

Publish bounded windows without completing turns for counts. Exact sequence statistics require both boundaries plus complete intervening items/events; running groups may qualify. Otherwise show only localized Consecutive tool calls. Statistics never request history, receipts or bodies. Receipt alignment reads ≤one preview page per displayed span; gaps remain scroll demand. [Tool sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) owns presentation.

Foreground readers own publication; live baselines queue during handoff. Reuse only a confirmed preceding cached prefix matching sealed ID, kind, turn/run, ordinal and canonical ordinal; old windows cannot infer new ends. Pagination retains manual disclosure through anchor changes/navigation and preserves focused/selected canonical DOM.

Collapsed patches use summary name/type for one mutation or localized multi-file count, with no details or invented targets/diff rows. Expansion retains titles, totals and file statistics. Activity summaries carry shape/counts/scalars/small values without field locators; explicit structure/value reads use authorized frozen sources, without storage/index/migration changes.

## Bodies and incremental transport

Only unseen text shows skeletons. Accepted prose, attachments/references, anchors and follow choices survive refresh/completion. One visibility observer admits demand within 160 px; text/open tools share two slots and a 15-second deadline. Priority: visible live text/interactive disclosure, visible history, background; age every eight admissions. Offscreen/navigation cancels demand/read; failures expose local Retry.

ThreadCache alone retains bodies by item/turn/run/source. Freshly authorized ThreadItemTextReader reads ≤16 KiB at accepted UTF-8 offsets. One source task coalesces extents, accepts earlier in-flight prefixes and yields between chunks. No polling, full-prefix/history downloads or duplicate store. Changed sources, including sealing, restart at canonical preview offset; live/sealed suffixes need not match. Keep readable prose until replacement chunks complete, then publish once. Same-source refresh retains progress; late old chunks cannot overwrite. A retired live locator is an explicit source_changed response only after published Floret ItemBody confirms the same item now has a canonical source. Its read releases its slot and waits for authoritative observation, without polling, guessing canonical offsets or suppressing unrelated read errors. Terminal/exhausted failures offer localized Retry, never execution replay.

Ending a text segment (`live: false`) does not itself change its source. A longer validated same-source live preview advances cached text and pending state atomically, preserving the locator for later growth. Covered chunk responses validate their overlap and yield without layout invalidation; any missing suffix resumes at the current cache offset. Source changes discard obsolete responses. Response/request identity, range, conflicting prefixes and empty nonterminal chunks remain explicit failures. Regression tests control both completion orders and overlapping reads, retaining the bubble, draft, focus and geometry while the turn continues through tools.

Schema v3 has one decoder. Base64 fragments include identity, zero-based index/count and total bytes. Merge ≤32 KiB fragments only with matching revision/thread/item/turn/run, contiguous version and UTF-8 offset. Growth sends locators. Same-source server/frame coalescing uses constant storage, original base version and intact semantic boundaries. Limits: sixteen pending batches, 32 MiB envelope/subscriber, 32 MiB global retained references. Started frames are immutable; byte-accounted covered versions suppress represented deltas. Summary/private-state/child inventories use separate mailboxes.

Pending controls are page-independent. Authorized server-only 64-item pages read Computer safety facts from pending turns to their user boundaries; confirm leaf/version, use individual reads for oversized collections. No full View/history body. Missing authority or broken ordering invalidates observation.

## Layout and retention

Measured offscreen sections retain DOM/intrinsic height while skipping layout. Long active turns split after prose near 24 rows, keeping consecutive tool/thinking sequences together and existing section/row owners stable across prepend. Visible, live, focused and selected sections retain layout; canonical content and disclosure owners remain accessible. Token growth updates per-block content presence only at empty/nonempty transitions; equal timeline and turn projections retain their identities. Mounted keyed subscriptions publish only changed section, entry, sequence and process facts and release with their Solid owners. Turn-end timestamps and final-answer ownership use keyed subscriptions too. Structural projectors read immutable record fields without allocating per-field reactive subscriptions; sealing through structural replacement, content-presence boundaries and preview replacement remain observable. Expired title arrivals do not revisit historical disclosure state. Thinking appends retain block identity. Membership checks use sets; empty receipt coverage does not republish on leaf-only changes. Following the latest output does not scan historical rows for a reading anchor. Inspection retains disclosure/nested offsets; Fork does not inherit another thread's manual choices. Unchanged sections/projections retain identity. One scroll owner corrects anchors before paint for growth, stationary-edge input and placeholder/summary replacement; readiness notification remains independently scheduled.

Incremental body chunks extend already admitted content without changing timeline restoration provenance. Full item hydration and baseline restoration still establish historical admission boundaries; live-body reads must not cancel unrelated fresh title or disclosure motion.

Cold sealed text stages complete bounded chunks in its item record across reconnect. Publish complete Markdown at final geometry, without entrance height animation or partial table/list/code formatting; retain visible prose during replacement and incremental live growth. Root/child navigation suppresses arrival scrolling until positioned/revealed. Cache accounting visits raw objects once, without recursive reactive unwrapping/subscriptions.

Compaction decorations follow visible anchors and the active run's latest operation; paging restores historical decorations without removing model history. Inactive detail budget: twelve threads or 32 MiB estimated bytes; summaries survive. Selected/retained/in-flight owners are protected. Append logs: 256 chunks/256 KiB with absolute cursors and exact-source catch-up. Active documents/selection are not capped.

History and terminal catch-up share one floating notice after 200 ms; fast reads mount nothing, publication is immediate, overlapping work adds no duplicates. [Command/composer ownership](flower-turn-launcher.md) retains immediate captured input and request-key DOM through admission, separating SendAck from windows.

## Recovery

One detail loader retries complete preparation/baseline after 200/600/1200 ms, ≤four attempts inside fifteen seconds. New revisions discard unpublished pages/envelopes. Leaf drift is recoverable; foreign threads/malformed ordering are terminal. Navigation/disposal/connection changes cancel reads/backoff. Success adds no read/timer. Preserve DOM/drafts/scroll; exhausted refresh uses interrupted-sync Retry, distinct from first-load failure. Never replay commands.

history_invalidated permits one bounded automatic read per selection/manual action; repeated loss offers Retry. Release cancels installed/pending interest without waiting for reads; child closure releases its slot only. One-shot windows cannot inherit old membership.

Transport loss/handshake deadlines/gaps use the existing bounded backoff owner. Final disposal aborts without reactive/cache publication into teardown; reconnect publishes its boundary. Activity observers attach after DOM adoption and detach with rows. Authorization/capacity/version/malformed-contract failures are terminal. Classify fetch/bridge errors before mapping; mapper exceptions do not retry. Diagnostics expose category/status/epoch, never bodies/arbitrary messages. SSE loss=503, baseline timeout=504, invalid request=400, capacity=429. Unknown results retain request keys; disconnect cannot replay effects.

One pointer-local floating stack owns connection/unconfirmed/settings/initial/detail/history/parent-report/navigation feedback. It takes no transcript height; collapsed companions float above the editor. Loading uses four sidebar wave bars, localized live status and reduced motion. Errors retain explanation/actions; terminal connection failure offers Resync. Notices cannot overlap; composer omits duplicates and preserves progress height. Canonical activity/cancellation owns Stopping. Read one canonical summary; viewer/current-only events cannot invent coverage. [Approval/input](flower-approval-context.md), [read state](flower-read-state.md) and [process disclosure](flower-turn-process-disclosure.md) own policy.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Streams, queues and cache are bounded ephemeral observation, never durable cursors
or another lifecycle. Database kinds and all released migration edges remain.

Explicit wheel, touch or keyboard intent can page from canonical history-window edges even when every loaded body is folded and no message anchor is visible. A visible message is only a layout anchor, never an admission requirement for paging. One coalesced input demand reads one bounded page; completion and idle layout cannot recursively traverse collapsed history.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
The composer always keeps its model label visible without an availability spinner or busy status.

Runtime status distinguishes no Desktop provider (`not_configured`), configured but unavailable keys or catalog (`missing_keys` or `empty`), and actual connection or protocol errors.

## Model identity and recovery
Thread snapshots, list items, and patches carry `model_id` and `reasoning_selection` as thread defaults. The last is a disabled, ungrouped display of a thread's missing model; Flower never silently replaces it.

See [reasoning selection ownership](flower-reasoning-selection.md) for loading, draft, and submission rules.

## Web search presentation
Model choices display the shared search badge from the server's readonly `web_search` projection. A provider brand or frontend model name never enables search. See [model directory ownership](../ai/model-directory-and-selection.md).

## Permission and navigation
Below the 768px viewport breakpoint, the composer keeps permission status and selection in its own More panel, alongside any other overflow controls.

Saving disables only the permission control, prevents duplicate requests, merges the authoritative settings response, and restores the confirmed value on failure.

Warm sessions switch without provider or transcript remount and stale loads cannot replace the current thread.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower does not treat the global model or permission as an existing-Thread launch override. After creation, its `model_id`, `reasoning_selection`, and `permission_type` are authoritative; Thread changes write to its settings, while new-thread overrides stay connection-local and never update environment defaults.

The header switcher is only a product-specific compact presentation; it does not create a second selected-thread owner or change the requested, committed, and content-presented ordering.

Flower shows how long a dispatched model request has waited and how much output

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Model request
Each logical request and attempt has its own start, first-output time, last semantic-progress time and estimated received output tokens. Local tools, approvals and user input never use this model-pause presentation.

Only phase text is a live region; numerical updates are readable without repeated automatic announcements.

## Progress symbol
The shared Flower mark retains its five-petal geometry.

The symbol is decorative beside the existing localized status text and does not create another live announcement or execution state.

## Edit arguments
The frozen tool definition supplies one optional argument preview parser per call. Their input budget is 1 MiB per call, with bounded JSON depth and field counts.

[Confirmed file Activity](flower-file-activity.md) remains the durable outcome.

sections.body: Floret owns request accounting and ephemeral thread snapshots. Redeven's pure argument parsers supply only display names and optional counts; they cannot authorize or execute edits. Canonical tool results remain the only durable change facts, and supersede every provisional count.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## First-time setup
Welcome setup requires no selected thread, configured provider or usable model, and absent/`not_configured`/`empty` Desktop source. Desktop `local_host` opens the current surface's settings, never another Welcome window or a remote destination. Artwork has no glow or continuous animation.

## Starter tasks
Four editable drafts cover current-folder understanding, connected computer, installed applications and folder organization. Names/dates alone never justify deletion. The [companion](flower-activity-companion.md) omits the grid.

## Settings composition
Settings edit the environment profile even with a Desktop model source. Flat sections preserve identity/drafts. Immediate switches block duplicate edits and roll back on failure.

## Provider configuration
[Provider configuration](flower-provider-configuration.md) owns authentication, layout and connection-before-model sequencing.

## Retained panels
FlowerSurface retains chat/extensions and a lazily loaded settings form in a bounded scrollable modal. Covered chat/navigation remain inert through close and do not acknowledge reads. Settings interactions belong to the companion: dialog close keeps it expanded; host collapse closes both while retaining form/progress/errors.

## Saving and ownership
Independent adapter operations save permission, model profile and default model. Permission uses a serialized 700 ms coalescing controller, fences older responses and restores the last confirmed value on failure. Computer-use failures restore the confirmed switch and expose errors.

concepts.title: Flower streaming stability
concepts.description: Incremental Markdown and local record updates preserve interactive identity.

frontmatter.description: Incremental Markdown and local record updates preserve interactive identity.
frontmatter.title: Flower streaming stability

concepts.summary: Flower renders actor-native changes through the indexed ThreadCache and the published Floe incremental Markdown parser. Ordinary growth changes the affected text/DOM region only. Stable history, code colors, copy controls, focus, selection and disclosure choices remain intact. A semantic change must remain visible; malformed updates recover through the single [live-state boundary](flower-live-timeline.md), never by omitting output or substituting a second lifecycle.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local data and rendering
Snapshots initialize indexed item/message records. Text/body extent growth retains history-window, turn and decoration identity; only membership, replacement, turn or context changes recompute their relevant metadata. Growing argument previews update their existing reactive block without revisiting completed tools; the same canonical validation still rejects invalid counters and retires withdrawn/stale attempts. Actual removal moves focus to an adjacent action or composer unless navigation already moved it. Regression fixtures retain 100 and 10,000 archived items and require zero historical ordinal reads for twenty text appends.

## One Markdown parser
Released Floe `createIncrementalMarkdownParser` owns Marked/CJK/GFM: reset sets a complete source baseline, append returns changed regions, finish authoritatively parses/corrects all content. Changed snapshots reset the complete baseline because tokens can move offsets and identities; reuse exact tokens at unchanged offsets and retire other old regions. Identical-source metadata retains regions. Completion, process collapse and replacement preserve all authored blocks. See [highlighting](flower-code-highlighting.md) and [media](flower-inline-media.md).

## Soft live text reveal
Added prose ranges fade to theme color over 320 ms through CSS custom highlights, without splitting nodes, delaying delivery, moving lines or replaying read content. History/corrections render immediately; links, code, media and controls keep their colors and behavior. Twenty fixed CSS phases use originating `currentColor`, avoiding stylesheet mutation, computed-style reads or per-frame inline writes.

Each owner has at most 32 transient groups; diff inspection is bounded at 8,192 characters/128 text nodes per region. Larger changes remain immediately readable. Completion lets valid effects settle; reset, unmount, hidden documents, reduced motion and forced colors clear them. Historical owners schedule no frames/listeners; unsupported highlight APIs use immediate text.

## Disclosure and layout
Cold historical text remains a loading presentation until all canonical chunks arrive. A reconnect retains both read offset and unpublished staging. Complete bodies enter at final geometry without height animation; browser acceptance samples table, code, list and text geometry from the first exposed frame. Existing readable text and live output retain their separate incremental behavior.

Composer/approval font measurements use releasable completion/error listeners, never retaining detached surfaces through `FontFaceSet.ready`. Companion reads only the newest relevant record and a bounded normalized Unicode tail.

## Interaction cadence and resources
One bounded frame queue applies every envelope in order, including semantic boundaries. Transport callbacks enqueue; each envelope commits atomically inside its host reactive batch. A four-millisecond cooperative budget includes reactive work and yields between envelopes through a timer task. It cannot preempt an individual expensive envelope. Apply failures are captured inside the reactive batch, allowing recovery notifications to commit before the error is rethrown to the connection owner. Ready waits for the queue to drain before admitting navigation; other reads pause at sixteen pending frames or one MiB. Disposal, failure and epoch changes release waiting readers and fence obsolete callbacks.

Coalesce only contiguous single-item appends with matching thread, item, turn, run and reading revision. Facts must match except timestamps and monotonic progress in the same request attempt. Preserve semantic boundaries and component clears. Join chunks once, preserving UTF-8 offsets and versions. A detected pending gap invalidates that batch and reports one synchronization error to the connection owner; no partially accepted batch is published.

Growth limits remain 64 frames, four MiB encoded bytes and a 250 ms presentation deadline; drag/resize cadence is 75 ms. Semantic work replaces a stalled animation-frame schedule with an immediate timer without overtaking earlier growth. One supported atomic wire envelope can use the existing 32 MiB allowance plus the growth reserve, while backpressure blocks further reads. Diagnostics expose bytes, age, count and application duration without transcript content. Copy feedback starts only on success, lasts 1.6 seconds, and never reports clipboard failure as success.

The opt-in real-Service qualifier freezes history/provider cadence, builds production UI and measures runtime, all Electron process CPU, frame/input/click/output latency, allocations and wire bytes. After timing it opens exact turn/nested-sequence controls and compares every assistant/thinking item with canonical content. The explicit [long-thread qualification](../operations/flower-long-thread-gate.md) additionally checks sustained growth and floating-window presentation. It remains outside unified commit, integration and CI gates, as do other explicit CPU matrices.

The synthetic qualifier measures task/script CPU, sampled allocations, retained heap, decoded envelopes and queue metrics; state-mutating probes run after timing. Decoded payload is not encrypted traffic, sampled allocation is not peak heap, and synthetic results do not qualify production providers/transports.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Terminal facts
Floret owns the nested `ActivityItem.presentation` contract and merges results with their stable call presentation. Labels and descriptions are authoritative; the typed operation supplies localized fallback text.

The five-line independently scrolling output viewport retains its existing owner.

An omitted output field is pending content, never an empty canonical frame with a nonzero first sequence. Wait for small-field hydration before polling or installing its sequence; large fields use source-bound ranges, then acknowledge their watermark before adding process deltas. Existing output and selection survive handoff.

Inactive output caches have 200-entry / 8 MiB estimated-byte limits. Mounted outputs remain retained until release; frame metadata coalesces after 128 records without changing sequence checks. These cache limits do not truncate an active process output or its canonical history.

## Interaction boundary
[Activity disclosure interaction](flower-activity-interaction.md) owns stable triggers, manual choices, animation, transcript following, and floating controls across all renderers. Approval state is never a row badge, chip, metadata line, title suffix, tooltip, detail, or ordinary activity ARIA label. Completing a decision removes that dock without inserting an approval outcome into history.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Activity details are designed renderer views, never arbitrary payload inspectors.

Presentation never changes Floret status, ordering, persistence, read acknowledgement, audit state, or terminal settlement.

Flower acknowledges navigation before transcript work. One coordinator serves

Readiness controls reveal; elapsed time controls feedback only.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Selection and navigation
Rail feedback precedes visible commit by two animation callbacks and a task; hidden documents do not wait for frames. Latest intent supersedes earlier work; summary effects cannot bypass foreground coordination.

Reveal only after the current selection accepts its required baseline/handoff, measurable layout and visible historical text settle. Cached windows requiring renewed interest remain hidden through that existing bounded read; a cache needing no read prepares immediately. The boundary is finite and never waits for runtime quiet. Canceled reads cannot release a newer selection; reselect, reconnect and retry retain the same loader ownership. The scroll owner also prepares the latest active tool sequence after row placement, so both outer and inner tails are positioned before reveal. Restored title, sequence and whole-turn disclosure settle without animation; a sequence inside a folded turn cannot block readiness; explicit group folds survive and retain a current activity label. Initial positioning has no smooth scrolling or time-based fallback. One cancellable 200 ms deadline spans detail/body/layout loading feedback; ready content/errors appear immediately. Selection, New chat and disposal cancel old feedback; frame, composer/navigation remain stable and failed body reads remain local and retry with renewed viewport demand or reconnect.

Cached destinations flush render effects; visible rows pass `checkVisibility({ contentVisibilityAuto: true })`. ResizeObserver adjusts above-viewport growth before paint, while reveal/body work stays in rAF; visibility events reuse this pass. Navigation clears arrival motion. No positioning polls or per-row observers. Explicit wheel/touch/scrollbar/keyboard input can interrupt preparation, and the awaited refresh cannot resume following afterward; scroll events alone cannot.

Two read slots prioritize visible text/margin and cancel obsolete demand. ThreadCache retains immutable bodies. Growth/refresh/completion never restart selection or remove accepted prose; [live delivery](flower-live-timeline.md) owns validation/retry. Selection opens Latest; reading restoration is separate. Ordinary threads sort by descending creation time, then ascending ThreadID.

## Continuous history and concurrent activity

Users browse earlier and newer history by scrolling. Viewport demand reads
canonical windows automatically; no load-earlier or load-newer action is part
of normal navigation. Retained windows preserve visible, selected and focused
rows while gaps are filled in either direction. Stable item identities preserve
expanded details and scroll anchors during live appends and replacements.
When a collapsed tail is shorter than the viewport, prepending history retains
the visible trailing room required by its reading anchor. The scroll owner
reclaims that room only as it leaves view or content fills it; loading must not
push existing messages down to fill the viewport. Viewport resizing preserves
the anchor, and destination preparation clears the temporary geometry. The
transcript content observer attaches after DOM mounting and corrects growth
before paint. This adds no history reads, persisted state or disclosure changes.
The floating Latest action stays available above the composer while reading
away from latest, including at the bottom of a historical window. It is hidden
during destination preparation and keeps pointer-gesture protection. If the
latest window is already installed, the action scrolls smoothly and retires
retained trailing room at arrival. Otherwise it cancels obsolete reading demand,
installs one bounded tail interest and reveals the prepared latest destination;
it never walks intervening pages. Main and child views share these semantics.
The accepted history baseline belongs to the live observer and reading revision;
superseded navigation cannot replace a newer selection.

Collapsed tools and parent reports retain presentation previews. Full activity
bodies and report text are requested when disclosed, under fresh authorization.
Collapse, navigation and disposal cancel unused demand; reconnect restores active
consumers. Retry is local to an actual read failure. Released empty activity
sources use Floret's canonical default presentation in source order.

Field-only activity presentation remains disabled for ordinary product history
until complete renderer parity is qualified. Complete body expansion is retained;
computer evidence and target hydration can still require full canonical reads.
This release does not promise a fixed opening latency or globally bounded memory
for all expanded terminal output.

## Detail read ownership
Floret supplies canonical summaries, source-bound windows and exact body reads; ThreadCache owns selection/detail with twelve entries. The bounded coordinator shares navigation, confirmation and reference-preflight demand. Cancellation never reconnects the workspace stream.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Resizing
One 220–380 CSS-pixel preference owns desktop sidebar width. Inline resizing updates only its grid track, at most once per frame; drawer width applies only in overlay mode. Mobile, companion and embedded layouts keep their sizing.

One primary-pointer gesture retains the latest sample and settles on release, cancellation, lost capture, blur, layout change or unmount. Release listeners, frames and cursor/selection shielding; persist once per gesture or immediately for keyboard changes. Storage failure cannot interrupt interaction. Width changes cannot reparse Markdown or invalidate the full transcript.

## Rename from the conversation header
The header pencil edits the existing ThreadID, including during execution/loading, with canonical title prefilled and selected. Header/sidebar share one save owner and thread cache.

## Selection and detail reads
[Selection](flower-thread-selection.md) owns deferred commitment, bounded reads, cancellation and recovery. ThreadCache owns committed selection/detail; sidebar intent reserves feedback only.

## Reference action
Right-click, More and Shift+F10 share the ThreadID-owned menu. [References](flower-thread-references.md) own deduplication, preview, admission and recovery.

## Pending replies and approvals
Localized reply/approval labels appear beside the title with bounded status/progress width. Background updates use the workspace stream without selection.

## Pin ordering
The stable `.flower-thread-rows` owner contains inline size for real/skeleton rows; movable cards cannot be size containers. Keyboard order matches visible search/pin-overlay order. Failed pin operations undo only their own presentation and reconcile via the existing summary stream or one explicit command read.

## Stable presentation and convergence
Key rows by ThreadID and group labels separately. ThreadCache owns summaries; each batch publishes once under existing title/revision rules, preserving menus, focus and running-wave continuity.

Explicit inspection survives. Answered input splits settled work into independently closed groups. This is presentation over published Floret facts, with no canonical summary or migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Membership and counts

A group has ≥two nodes in one thread/turn/run, including a tool. One call plus thinking qualifies; standalone thinking does not. Calls, failures, argument previews and adjacent leading/trailing thinking retain source order, outputs/actions/errors. A newer singleton may settle an older group without overriding its explicit choice.

Prose, users, interactions, compaction, approvals, non-tool errors and Goal updates break groups. Goal/Web Search calls remain tools. SubAgent calls and canonically scoped report/completion events join; unknown parent-event ownership breaks. Returned uncertain tool errors stay with their exact identity and display localized unconfirmed counts when coverage is complete, including folded state. Invalid success-with-uncertainty or uncertain parent lifecycle events break. Running attention/SubAgent waits join; other waits break. Empty live assistant placeholders are transparent; unknown text bodies cannot establish continuity. Answered input splits settled work into independently closed sequences, including the newest. Active calls and whole-turn disclosure retain their policies.

Canonical call IDs retain row lifetime; thinking moves in place. Pagination keeps the loaded anchor's choice while canonical first-node DOM takes ownership, including subsequent navigation. Icons use theme-owned active/completed/failure states.

Counts require known boundaries and no missing internal items/events; partial windows and running turns may contain complete groups. Unknown coverage shows only localized Consecutive tool calls (also accessible name), with no partial totals, running count, latest-tool preview or loading message. Known failures retain attention/detail behavior. Ordinary pagination may complete counts in place, retaining disclosure/focus/selection. Statistics never acquire history, whole turns, receipts or bodies.

## Disclosure and bodies

History restoration settles automatic sequence and whole-turn policy without motion before destination exposure; explicit user choices survive. The disclosure choice records whether its transition may animate, so ordinary manual actions restore motion without changing the automatic default. Only admitted live arrivals use the fold-before-prose handoff. Preparation waits for queued row placement even if the latest group is automatic, and skips inner positioning inside folded turns.

Session choices key runtime/thread/tool. Defaults settle initially and once when an active open group becomes eligible to fold. Explicit choices survive updates, completion, reconnect and navigation until refresh. Focus/selection/gestures/open details/thinking/away-from-tail reading protect expansion but cannot reopen a closed group; direct disclosure or explicit navigation can. Choice subscriptions are per-group.

An eligible live sequence closes over 260 ms into the actual shared summary-row height (2rem desktop, 2.75rem coarse pointer), never through zero beneath that row. The summary fades in during the final 100 ms after a 140 ms delay; only one summary layer and the shared viewport animate. Newly arriving prose remains mounted, invisible and inert until geometry settles, then fades in over 160 ms with no translation. Runtime delivery and streaming continue without buffering or remounting. Existing prose, inspected groups, history, navigation and reduced motion do not wait.

Title arrivals finish first. If a terminal snapshot also closes the enclosing turn, that row owns the fold directly; nested sequence geometry stays intact until completion. A terminal snapshot interrupting an existing sequence fold transfers its current opacity/transform so faded tools cannot flash back. The same ephemeral pending-content map identifies the motion owner, including subsequent prose arrivals. Reversal waits for the new motion, while disposal and reduced motion release pending content. No per-tool animation, new observer, timer or per-frame reactive state is introduced; shared-row height is measured once at collapse.

Closed groups mount shells/summary only. First expansion mounts details; later folding makes retained bodies inert. New members of manually closed groups wait. Whole-turn closure retains inspected bodies after motion. Existing owners lend DOM to the first node viewport and restore it on disposal, retaining focus/selection/nested state. Growth retains group/member identity; only changed membership/status/disclosure/order replaces its projection.

Thinking hydration observes its displayed movable node, not the vacated shell. Sealed pending thinking admits demand only when explicitly expanded and visible through nested clipping; live thinking keeps its policy. The shared two-slot queue gives interactive priority to explicit demand; fold/offscreen/navigation cancels obsolete reads. Completed text is reusable; loading reflects actual demand. Unopened tools neither read nor mount detail bodies.

## Geometry and input

Prose, Goal/tool/thinking icons, the folded summary and progress lane share one left edge. A permanent outer gutter is present before any activity arrives; singleton-to-group promotion never changes indentation or inserts a blank title row. The native scrollbar gutter is also stable. Each tool retains its icon and independent detail control. Within the full-width row target, intrinsic text is followed immediately by elapsed time and the detail chevron; only long text shrinks, never those controls. This uses CSS layout without a text-width observer or measurement loop.

Expanded groups have one native button in the left gutter: a downward chevron and a continuous bracket show the bounded group's extent. The whole rail collapses the group; there is no right-side group action. Its hit area is 24px wide, 44px for coarse pointers, outside the tool targets. The same button covers the summary when folded, with an inline chevron after its content. Summary text keeps stable bounds through the crossfade, independent of the rail width. Counts take priority over the optional latest-tool preview on narrow screens. The rail stays outside the scrolling body, follows the existing shared viewport's height and stops before following prose. No per-row connector or scroll-time clipping/hit testing is needed.

Rows remain 2rem desktop, 2.75rem coarse pointer. Sequence viewport: at most eight rows, ≤65% transcript height; additional rows remain reachable through scrolling, details share the viewport, and short content keeps natural height. Thinking: 20rem, ≤45% window and transcript limit. Both have thin scrollbars, keyboard focus, localized names and reachable controls.

Thinking, sequences and read-only terminal/file/diff/excerpt/code regions chain native scrolling; consume only locally scrollable input, forwarding short/edge input to ancestors. Transcript wheel/touch/keyboard upward intent pauses following; actual bottom return resumes. Explicit containment, cancelled events and zoom stay local; interactive terminals/editors keep ownership.

Inner content/transcript use the same input-aware controller; wheel/touch/keyboard/scrollbar reading pauses following, while programmatic events, geometry, images and row placement create no intent. Each open sequence observes mounted children through that owner, retaining nested input and anchors. Explicit opening positions latest tool before paint, including calls received while folded. Navigation waits for row placement and both destinations. Restored details have no preparation-time opening motion. Manual folds stay closed; complete counts may include the canonical latest-tool label without body reads. Collapse focuses its button. Thinking retains completion state and saved offset. [Activity motion](flower-activity-interaction.md#visual-motion) coordinates placement/arrival scrolling.

Controls expose viewport IDs/localized counts; closed members leave no gaps and candidate headers remain inaccessible until eligible. Auto-fold uses [turn disclosure](flower-turn-process-disclosure.md) real-content anchoring policy; manual toggles retain trigger anchors. Both catalogs share narrow/touch/focus/reduced-motion/forced-color behavior.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Core commands reject missing, duplicate, invalid or conflicting IDs; only the legacy RPC adapter may fill a missing one. [Goals](../ai/flower-goals.md) share the outbox. Empty-thread creation retains text/reference/attachment authority; first Send binds staged resources to the authorized canonical thread. Unknown effect outcomes are terminal with safe explanation and no replay action.

## Immediate send feedback
The immutable transport outbox owns submitted text, references and attachment
metadata before IndexedDB or HTTP completes. Ordinary sends render a pending
user row immediately and consume only the captured draft; newer edits stay in
the composer. Request-key message and section identities survive canonical
admission, including receipt/live ordering and prepended history. Images reserve
the same thumbnail geometry and use the authorized staged preview until admitted.
Failed and unknown outcomes retain the frozen request for explicit recovery;
server 5xx responses never prove rejection or authorize a fresh request identity.

Product admission uses published SendAck and narrow canonical summaries. HTTP
and RPC return admission identity without a post-commit history read; authorized
window observation supplies presentation separately. Agent preparation binds the
already persisted execution authority to the admitted turn. No duplicate
post-admission authority write or second conversation lifecycle is introduced.
Full model history remains an engine execution requirement, not a prerequisite
for painting the submitted message.

## Restored data and preserved inputs
New submissions capture storage generation immediately, even behind paused dispatch. Rejected input stays copyable/restorable; running it requires explicit new submission, never resumed old approvals/effects.

## Context preview presentation
One Env App `FlowerContextPreviewWindow` uses existing preview/text components for launcher and draft/canonical snapshots. Launcher owns attachment IO, sequencing and URL cleanup; Flower owns validity. Related-surface markers preserve input ownership; Escape dismisses preview before companion.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Canonical facts and eligibility
Validated ThreadView/HistoryPage turn facts include exact TurnID/RunID, optional control kind, start/end, outcome, elapsed/wait/work durations, ordered intermediate/final item IDs and complete-final boundary. Summaries cannot author them or trigger collapse; unknown output remains visible.

A single thinking-only process keeps its existing thinking disclosure and timing; it never gains a redundant work-duration summary or divider on completion. Eligibility follows typed process structure, not prompt text or elapsed-time heuristics. Other process summaries show at most two nonzero time units with subsecond copy. Interleaved answers default expanded with an accessible whole-turn toggle; folding hides only process rows and preserves visible answer checkpoints and nested choices. Counts appear only when loaded turn boundaries, item membership and parent-event coverage are complete; incomplete summaries retain canonical work duration without partial totals. [Sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) independently fold settled work on each side.

## Reading and interface state
Running/preparing/retrying/finalizing/waiting turns stay expanded with an inaccessible reserved header slot; the toggle appears only when eligible. After a canonical outcome and end time, confirmed intermediate/typed process rows fold automatically, including the latest failed/cancelled/interrupted turn. Final and trailing partial output remain visible. Focus, selection, gestures, open details/thinking and reading away from the tail retain inspected work; observation cannot later undo that protection. Capture an unaffected visible anchor only when a real automatic collapse starts, and correct geometry through the existing scroll owner. Open/closed choices survive pagination, reconnects and regrouping. A newly classified row under inspection remains visible until the next explicit group toggle, without reopening other folded rows. Only an explicit disclosure or navigation action can open a closed group. Inspected bodies stay mounted and inert when folded, preserving nested choices and offsets. Main, embedded and child views share rendering with separate scroll owners.

## Layout and accessibility
The turn header precedes its first loaded response after the original request, independently of which rows may fold. Canonical intermediate membership spans all executions of the same turn; source-run supersession remains engine-owned. In-turn Goal facts retain their turn ownership across continuation. Unknown prose and final output remain visible. A partial window uses its first loaded response without fetching earlier history for presentation. Retained canonical prefixes keep confirmed intermediate membership across a new run; incoming window facts replace overlapping classifications, and final boundaries remain run-scoped. Prepending the actual beginning moves the header while retaining its turn choice and keyboard focus; the button reads turn disclosure state independently of its anchor row visibility.

The first loaded response reserves header geometry before eligibility; revealing the toggle never inserts space or narrows content. Automatic turn/sequence folding follows the real content bottom before paint while the user is following output. Fold geometry owns motion; the viewport must not lock an obsolete absolute offset, add synthetic trailing space or run a competing growth animation. Long content becoming shorter than the viewport settles at zero scroll offset, with final output visible. Existing final answers stay mounted while process rows close over the existing 260 ms motion; reduced motion settles immediately. Paused reading and manual disclosure retain visible content/trigger anchors, including required temporary room during history insertion. Distance to latest excludes that room, so an overscrolled reader retains the return action. User input cancels automatic following immediately; later motion settlement cannot reclaim it.

When newly arriving prose waits for a sequence, terminal closure uses its existing outer row motion directly and releases prose only after that motion settles. Nested tools retain geometry during the outer fold; an interrupted inner fold transfers its painted opacity/transform. Manual open/close remains reversible and respects reduced motion; the disclosure owner retains the interaction choice. Canonical Path order, never timestamps, positions messages/receipts. Dialogue, final segments and secret-answer redaction remain intact.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Directory selection](filesystem-picker-navigation.md) owns validation; this contract owns entry points and destinations.

## Header and new-conversation entry points
The full-page header has a borderless folder/name browse button; new-conversation welcome selects the draft directory without persistent full-path secondary text. Only picker confirmation remembers a validated real directory. Browsing, cancellation, suggestions and destination navigation never write it; created-thread directories remain immutable.

## Directory and menu ownership
Right-click captures its row's thread/directory without loading, selecting or acknowledging it. Updates cannot retarget actions; handled child events cannot open outer menus. Copy/cancel restores valid triggers without scrolling.

## Destination behavior
Activity Files reuses its singleton window/geometry; Terminal creates a new session. Workbench creates the matching widget. Request IDs, lazy loading, terminal admission and layout persistence retain ownership. Created-thread browsing includes ThreadID; menu/terminal actions require it.

## Availability and recovery

Activity Bar Plugins opens a Shell-root Launcher without changing the normal surface. Search intersects category with NFKC/locale-case-folded display names, canonical keywords and explicit locale aliases. Tablet/desktop details overlay the grid without reflow and restore originating-row focus.

## Session recovery
An authenticated session-ready transition invokes idempotent Host `recoverEnabled` without a stability timer. All placements consume Host `action_state`; trust, grants, policy or recovery flags cannot derive `can_open`.

## Installation and package review
[Installation progress](plugin-installation-progress.md) owns durable Execution observation and approved setup; [package review](plugin-package-review.md) owns external packages. Failures preserve placement rather than delete components.

## Permissions and policy
Plugin Center joins inventory, grants, Host requirements and policy. Method effects cannot rename granted capabilities. Failure reloads authority and requires a new confirmation.

## Activity windows and pinned pages
Each window creates one fresh `PluginSurfaceSlot` through `openSurfaceInSlot`. Opening/bridge failures replace the iframe with local recovery; timeouts explain delay and offer Retry. Restart restores shortcuts but starts on a built-in page, never automatically opens third-party content.

## Workbench widgets and placement
[Layout continuity](plugin-layout-continuity.md) owns saved bindings, atomic placement, exact removal and recovery. Status overlays cannot forward input, guess focus or create a second bridge. Unpin removes only the shortcut.

## Confirmation and teardown
One abort-aware FIFO dialog decides requests independently with initial Cancel focus. Hidden, retired or revoked surfaces cannot approve queued work. Retired surfaces cannot download; Shell neither uploads nor retains exported bytes.

Narrow layouts remain usable and revisited panels retain draft/scroll. Authenticated APIs own writes; readers cannot edit administrator fields. Failures preserve input, while maintenance uses its existing controller after explicit confirmation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Navigation and visual hierarchy
Destinations are Config File, Connection, Runtime Status, Shell & Workspace, Codespaces & Tooling, Logging, Permission Policy, Flower and Debug Console. Page-owned geometry avoids competing global/lazy styles. Full padded diagnostic summaries toggle native disclosure with neutral hover and visible keyboard focus.

## Settings controls and identity
Runtime, Desktop environment, Flower, terminal and managed-service fields share the published Floe control height (32px, `--floe-control-height-md`), `--floe-radius-field` corners, 12px text, quiet fill and subdued 1px border. Row identity icons and provider brands occupy the same 32px square on `--floe-radius-md`, so icon, field and select edges stay concentric within a row. Floe owns keyboard, validation, menus and border-only focus. Scalar labels need no decorative icons.

## Configuration editing
Existing autosave/restart rules govern shell, filesystem, logging, ports and permissions. Settings PUT accepts flat fields, never response-group wrappers such as `runtime`/`logging`/`codespaces`. Health, diagnostics, backup/restore use right-column actions without bypassing permission/confirmation.

## Flower extension placement
[Flower extensions](flower-extensions.md) own Skills/MCP browsing and management.

## Product presentation
Ordinary shared Buttons, Cards, Radio, Checkbox, Switch, Tabs, progress controls, Dialogs, and FloatingWindows use their released component treatment. Hover must preserve the selected fill and text.

The plugin launcher keeps its existing action and localized name; artwork owns no input or navigation behavior.

concepts.summary: The Env App owns terminal font selection and document-local loading. New preferences use bundled JetBrains Mono at the existing default size of 12; existing font IDs and sizes remain intact. Each client resolves its own available font, while Floeterm owns character cells, cursor positions, and the authoritative session grid. A missing saved font falls back visibly without rewriting that preference. Font loading failure keeps the terminal usable in system monospace and offers an explicit retry.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One font resolver for every terminal surface
Activity, Workbench, container exec, and settings previews consume the same font catalog and resolution result.

The menu separates bundled fonts from available local fonts and exposes the saved selection through accessible pressed state; an unavailable saved selection remains visible but cannot be newly selected.

No fallback changes a persisted preference.

## Preferences and shared terminal geometry
Activity preferences stay on the client. Unknown saved IDs are retained and resolved through the same visible fallback; no protocol or storage-field migration is introduced.

Existing clipping and navigation apply when the canonical grid does not fit the local viewport.

## Settings presentation
Terminal settings start with the actual resolved font and current theme preview. Narrow galleries retain one readable card column, including at 320px and 200% zoom.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Catalog and Session assignment
Redeven owns `apps/terminal/groups.sqlite` as a versioned product database. Future versions, wrong kinds, and schema drift fail closed without replacing the file.

Reorder persists one complete non-Default order in a single database transaction and revision; Default remains protected at order zero.

## Activity, Workbench, and view-local state
One Terminal Session Catalog Provider owns the browser projection, the live in-memory Session display order, and the Redeven-specific `session_id -> group_id` membership map for the Environment. List requests carry membership and lifecycle fences, so an older response cannot overwrite a local move or newer notification.

Search matches Group name, Group path, and Session presentation; a matching folded child is revealed temporarily without changing that saved preference.

## Interaction and asynchronous lifecycle
The sidebar renders Group headers with explicit expand/collapse and scoped create-Session actions.

Header decoration must not offset that geometry on desktop or under Workbench scaling.

Individual failures are returned as explicit Session IDs; those Sessions remain hidden, no success is fabricated, and no silent retry loop is introduced.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Group membership is not Workbench placement, shell working directory, controller ownership, attachment identity, or persistent Session recovery. No Activity or Workbench component may maintain a second membership map, infer membership from paths, or repair an unknown Group by changing a Session to Default. Group disclosure and metadata updates remain renderer-neutral UI state and must not remount `TerminalSessionRuntime`.

concepts.summary:
Published Floe owns layout, routing, viewport interaction and route painting.
Tessiven supplies canonical topology projection, localized view controls and
palette. Folding, filtering and navigation never rewrite a saved document.
Canonical relationships remain inspectable while only the current connection
scope is routed and painted. Offscreen geometry cannot expand the SVG layer. Invalid graph data or actual worker failures stay visible;

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Layout and routing
Automatic layout and library thumbnails use the same published Floe layout engine, direction, layers, and visibility projection. Saved positions guide ordering within a layer and never override its rank. Positioned objects without relationships still contribute their actual world bounds, so fitting a newly mapped or isolated node keeps it inside the viewport.

## Connection scopes
Default browsing shows one directed overview connector per root endpoint pair. Group-internal relationships remain in the canonical pool overview and never create a group self-loop.

The interactive overview and library thumbnails always paint the root overview, even while the main canvas shows a focused host's detailed paths.

## Controls and rendering
- Canvas controls expand or collapse all logical groups in one compact reflow. They preserve the selected visible object, or its enclosing group when hidden,   and never create a document version. Large-graph   qualification measures actual host counts, including groups of ten   so a thousand-host fixture never silently measures only aggregate cards.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The saved canvas contract owns topology and versions; these browsing controls change only the visible scene. Tessiven does not replace worker failures with guessed routes or use viewport culling to alter the complete inspectable model.

sections.title: Contract

## Reading surface
The window uses the theme's main reading surface continuously across its titlebar, transcript and composer surroundings. A subtle border and shadow frame compact readable message spacing; canvas nodes must not bleed through reply text.

End padding keeps the final choice fully readable when scrolled to the bottom; the action controls remain outside the fade.

## Actions and continuity
Less frequent actions live in the More menu: new conversation, settings, subagents, available Computer actions and opening the full conversation.

Messages, tool disclosures, questions, approvals and errors remain canonical.

Existing canvases open the combined window directly.

frontmatter.title: UI presentation transactions

concepts.summary: Heavy navigation acknowledges selection synchronously, commits target visibility after that intent can paint, then performs focus, resize, scroll or measurement after content paint. Published Floe separates visual from committed values; Redeven applies this ordering across Activity, Workbench, terminal, Flower, Files/Git and heavy panels without duplicating business state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Initialization, persisted restoration, permission correction, automatic open and recovery use synchronous canonical commitment such as `commitNow()`. Genuinely blocking operations keep their dedicated presentation.

## Activity and retained content
Activity uses Shell UI-first mode and after-paint activation. Files preserves hidden virtual-grid measurements, usable width/range/scroll. Flower keeps the previous transcript during cold selection and replaces it only when the latest destination is ready.

## Measurement
Debug Console groups presentation events by surface/source. User interactions must avoid renderer tasks/frame gaps of 50 ms or more. Instrumentation flags intent at 32 ms and content at 100 ms; focused performance/browser gates enforce distributions and long-task limits.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
UI-first scheduling is not permission to duplicate canonical state or create a second business model.

Explicit environment replacement, permission-root replacement, connection recovery, resource-pressure policy already owned by the relevant subsystem, and user-requested closure may establish separate lifecycle boundaries; a navigation click alone may not.

concepts.summary: Workbench input ownership is declared through explicit marker contracts so canvas zoom, local scrolling, pointer actions, and text selection remain distinguishable. Wheel ownership uses exported local scroll viewport props that set `data-floe-canvas-wheel-interactive="true"` and a local-scroll role. Text selection surfaces use separate marker props and do not receive wheel ownership unless combined with local scroll viewport props.

Fit and actual-size actions reset the scale deterministically, while Ctrl/Cmd-wheel and keyboard `+`, `-`, `0`, and `1` remain scoped to the image viewport.

sections.title: Boundaries

Components embedded in projected Workbench surfaces must use the shared floating layer rather than hand-rolling viewport-to-surface coordinates.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One terminal owner and one view renderer
One `SessionActor` owns each session; sequence and geometry generation only advance. Every view receives the same authoritative Presentation with canonical dimensions. Paint complete backgrounds before cells, graphics, selection and cursor to avoid stale edges during resize, activation or theme changes.

## Multi-view geometry and controller ownership
Published Floeterm owns attachment arbitration and geometry. Browser views never parse output bytes, own history or create hidden renderers.

## Product footer placement
[Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md#activity-terminal-footer) owns the Activity-only measured footer entry. Workbench supplies none. Layout cannot attach a view, request control or intercept terminal input.

## Input, links, selection, and mobile interaction
`TerminalInputBridge` sends confirmed Unicode once, structured key intents to the native encoder and clipboard paste through its bounded interaction. Script/malformed URLs, stale capabilities and remote paths fail closed.

## Clear, history, refresh, and lifecycle
Clear is the actor's semantic reset, never canvas erasure, Ctrl-L, recreation or detach; stale generations have no effect. Close/delete removes catalog, attachments and capabilities; stale notifications cannot resurrect sessions.

## Product lifecycle and performance
Dormant sessions remain metadata-only and the catalog renderer-free. Ask Flower captures selection or bounded visible semantic text; working directory requires current local-path capability.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Redeven may adapt Flowersec streams, product permissions, local-path capability, responsive placement, notifications, and Desktop URL/file actions. It must not recreate terminal parsing, key encoding, history ownership, attachment arbitration, canonical geometry, semantic frame encoding, cursor state, graphics state, or renderer internals. Local sibling dependencies, raw-byte fallbacks, hidden renderers, automatic reattach on ordinary resize, error swallowing, and sequence rollback are prohibited.

## Activity presentation
The existing canonical active/running/idle state and the persisted activity indicator preference remain authoritative. Opaque widget bodies and neutral static shadows do not change during activation, dragging, or resizing.
